# Performance and User Experience Requirements for the shoppingMall E-Commerce Platform

## 1. Performance Requirements

### 1.1 Response Time
- WHEN any authenticated or guest user requests a product list or searches, THE system SHALL return results within 2 seconds for 95% of requests under typical network circumstances.
- WHEN a user (customer, seller, or admin) submits login credentials, THE system SHALL validate and return a result within 1.5 seconds, except in exceptional system degradation scenarios.
- WHEN a user places an order or performs checkout, THE system SHALL process and confirm the transaction within 3 seconds.
- WHEN a user interacts with the shopping cart (add, remove, update item), THE system SHALL apply the change and return the cart status within 1.5 seconds.
- WHEN a user submits a cancellation or refund request, THE system SHALL acknowledge the receipt instantly and provide a processing status within 3 seconds.

### 1.2 Throughput & Volume
- THE platform SHALL support a minimum of 500 concurrent active users with sustained read/write operations, scaling linearly to 2,000 with minimal reduction in perceived performance (within 10%).
- WHERE peak sales events are scheduled (e.g., holiday promotions), THE system SHALL support up to 20x normal request rates for a period of at least 4 consecutive hours.
- THE order processing pipeline SHALL handle a minimum of 100 new orders per minute during normal operations, scaling to 1,000 per minute during peak campaigns.

### 1.3 Data Consistency & Integrity
- WHEN users update sensitive information (addresses, payment methods), THE changes SHALL be confirmed and available to all relevant views immediately (within 1 second of write confirmation).
- IF a transaction fails at any stage, THEN THE system SHALL display an actionable error and preserve user state without data corruption.
- WHERE high-value operations occur (placing orders, processing refunds), THE system SHALL guarantee atomicity and consistency in all backend operations.

### 1.4 Performance Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Sends Request"] --> B["System Receives Request"]
  B --> C{"Is System Degraded?"}
  C -->|"No"| D["Respond Within SLA Time"]
  C -->|"Yes"| E["Serve Error/Degradation Notification"]
  D --> F["User Continues"]
  E --> F
```

## 2. User Experience Standards

### 2.1 General UX Principles
- THE system SHALL provide consistent feedback for every user action – confirmations, error reasons, and completion status.
- WHEN a background process (e.g., refund review) affects user-initiated operations, THE system SHALL communicate status updates at each significant step.
- THE system SHALL localize all feedback and error messages in the user-selected language (default: English for locale en-US).

### 2.2 User Journey Smoothness
- WHEN browsing product catalogs, THE system SHALL enable filtering, sorting, and paging with near-instant (<2 seconds) response.
- WHEN a user attempts an operation not permitted for their role (e.g., customer editing inventory), THEN THE system SHALL display a clear role-based restriction message.
- THE system SHALL retain changes to cart and wishlist between authenticated sessions for each customer.
- IF an operation is delayed beyond published performance standards, THEN THE system SHALL provide a progress indicator and allow for safe retry or cancellation.

### 2.3 Error Communication and Handling
- IF a user action fails (e.g., out-of-stock, payment declined), THEN THE system SHALL present a clear, actionable message and recovery steps.
- WHEN system errors or maintenance intervals will impact user experience, THE system SHALL notify users at least 30 minutes in advance (when possible) and provide status banners during the incident.
- THE system SHALL ensure all error messages are in user-friendly natural language, never exposing technical codes or internal references.

### 2.4 Accessibility & Inclusivity
- THE system SHALL adhere to WCAG 2.1 AA standards, ensuring support for screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, and high-contrast modes.
- WHERE visual indicators or colors are used, THE system SHALL offer alternative text or patterns for the visually impaired.

### 2.5 User Experience Flow Example
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Customer Product Interaction Flow"
      A["Customer Browses Catalog"] --> B["Customer Applies Filter"]
      B --> C["Results Returned (<2s)"]
      C --> D{"Add to Cart?"}
      D -->|"Yes"| E["Cart Updated"]
      D -->|"No"| F["Continue Browsing"]
      E --> G["Checkout Flow"]
      F --> G
  end
```

## 3. System Scalability and Availability

### 3.1 Scalability
- WHERE business expansion or seasonal campaigns occur, THE platform SHALL horizontally scale core backend services to handle 10x normal user load without observable degradation in end-user experience (response time <15% slower than baseline).
- THE system SHALL support seamless onboarding of new sellers, new product categories, and new customers without downtime or migration windows.

### 3.2 Availability & Redundancy
- THE platform SHALL deliver minimum 99.5% uptime measured monthly, with a long-term goal of 99.9% (excluding pre-scheduled maintenance, defined <2h/month).
- WHERE single points of failure exist, THE system SHALL implement failover or hot-standby for order processing, payment, and authentication subsystems.
- WHEN emerging failures are detected (backend, database, payment integration), THE system SHALL automatically degrade non-essential features to preserve order and payment processing functionality.

### 3.3 Disaster Recovery & Data Safety
- WHEN a component or service fails, THE system SHALL recover full operations within 15 minutes using backup and replication.
- THE system SHALL persist and archive transaction, inventory, and review data in real time, with daily integrity and recovery checks conducted automatically.

### 3.4 Scalability Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Normal Operations"] --> B{"User Spike Detected?"}
    B -->|"No"| C["Continue Normal Operation"]
    B -->|"Yes"| D["Automated Resource Scaling"]
    D --> E["Maintain Performance to SLA"]
    C --> E
```

## 4. Service Level Expectations

### 4.1 Service Target Metrics Table
| Metric                            | Minimum Target          | Ideal Target     | Notes                               |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|
| API response (product search)     | < 2 seconds (p95)      | < 1.2 seconds   | Under 95% load                      |
| API response (checkout)           | < 3 seconds (p99)      | < 2 seconds     | Full transaction/path                |
| System Uptime                     | 99.5% monthly          | 99.9%           | Excludes scheduled maintenance       |
| Error message clarity (user-rated)| 80% positive feedback  | 95%+            | Post-incident user survey            |
| Cart/wishlist persistence         | 30 days                | 180 days        | No data loss through session expiry  |

### 4.2 Incident Response
- WHEN a critical outage occurs, THE system SHALL notify all affected users within 10 minutes and update status at least every 30 minutes until resolved.
- WHEN incidents result in missed SLAs, THE system SHALL record, track, and present post-mortems to the admin team within 48 hours.

### 4.3 Continuous Improvement
- THE system SHALL regularly collect and analyze UX and performance metrics to identify improvement opportunities. Quarterly reviews SHALL be conducted and changes prioritized in product roadmap sessions.

---

This document outlines end-user-facing performance expectations, user experience criteria, and operational standards. All backend technical teams must ensure backend implementations meet or exceed these business requirements as perceived by all user roles.

# Error Handling and Exception Cases in the Shopping Mall Platform

## Introduction
This document provides a comprehensive catalog of error types and exception flows in the shopping mall service. Its goal is to ensure all errors encountered by customers, sellers, or admins are handled gracefully, communicated clearly in user-centric business language, and offer robust recovery paths. All requirements use the EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax) format for clarity, and major process flows are visually mapped for maximum developer utility.

## Major Error Types (by Process)

### 1. User Registration and Login
- Invalid credentials (wrong email or password)
- Duplicate account (e.g., registration with existing email)
- Password complexity or format errors
- Social login/account linking failures
- Excessive failed login attempts (account lock)
- Email verification timeout or invalid verification link
- Token/session expiration

### 2. Address Management
- Invalid address format or missing required fields
- Adding more addresses than allowed
- Attempting to delete primary/default address
- Address not found

### 3. Product Catalog and Search
- Product not found (removed or out of stock)
- Invalid search term or unsupported filters
- Attempt to access restricted or hidden products
- Category not found or deprecated

### 4. Product Variants and Inventory
- Variant not available (SKU combination does not exist)
- Out of stock (SKU reached zero quantity)
- Trying to add unavailable variant to cart

### 5. Cart and Wishlist Management
- Adding item for a removed or disabled product
- Adding more than stock quantity to cart
- Wishlist at maximum allowed items
- Attempt to remove item not in cart/wishlist

### 6. Order Placement and Payment
- Insufficient stock at checkout (item became unavailable)
- Payment gateway failure (declined, timeout, error)
- Invalid payment method (unsupported card/type)
- Order amount mismatch (price changed between selection and payment)
- Exceeding purchase quantity per policy

### 7. Order Tracking and Shipping
- Tracking number not found/invalid
- Shipment delayed or lost
- Unable to update shipping address (order shipped already)
- Attempt to cancel order after shipment

### 8. Product Reviews and Ratings
- Review submission before purchase
- Multiple reviews for same product/order
- Review/edit window expired
- Inappropriate or restricted review content

### 9. Seller Product/Inventory Management
- Unauthorized access to another seller's product
- Attempt to edit product locked by admin
- Upload with invalid SKU or missing details
- Inventory update for discontinued SKU

### 10. Order History, Cancellation, and Refunds
- Cancellation after non-cancellable state (e.g., shipped)
- Refund not allowed (policy violation)
- Duplicate or conflicting refund requests

### 11. Admin Actions
- Attempted action without required permissions
- Invalid admin operation (e.g., attempting destructive irreversible action without confirmation)
- Escalation for unresolved user/seller issue

---

## Error Triggers and Recovery Flows

### General Principles
- Every error MUST be communicated in clear, actionable user language, never as a technical message.
- Users must always have a recovery option or be notified of next steps.
- Admins and Sellers require error context for fast resolution.

### Triggers and Recovery (by Key Actors)

#### User Registration/Login Errors
- WHEN user provides invalid credentials, THE system SHALL inform them that the email or password is incorrect and allow retry.
- IF user exceeds maximum login attempts, THEN THE system SHALL lock the account for a cooldown period and display recovery instructions.
- WHEN user tries to register with existing email, THE system SHALL prompt them to log in or recover password.
- IF verification link is expired, THEN THE system SHALL provide an option to resend the link.

#### Address Management Errors
- WHEN address format is invalid, THE system SHALL highlight the error and prompt user to correct.
- IF user attempts to delete the only/default address, THEN THE system SHALL block the action with an explanation.

#### Product Catalog and Search Errors
- IF search yields no results, THEN THE system SHALL display a user-friendly "no results found" message and suggest alternatives.
- WHEN product is not found, THE system SHALL inform user that the product is unavailable.

#### Product Variant/Inventory Errors
- IF selected product variant is unavailable, THEN THE system SHALL block selection and suggest alternatives.
- WHERE cart quantity exceeds inventory, THE system SHALL limit quantity to available stock and inform user.

#### Cart and Wishlist Errors
- WHEN user adds product no longer available, THE system SHALL display reason and remove it from cart/wishlist.
- WHERE wishlist is full, THE system SHALL alert user and suggest removing other items before adding new.

#### Order and Payment Errors
- IF payment fails (for any reason), THEN THE system SHALL show failure reason and steps to retry or use alternate method.
- WHEN insufficient stock during checkout, THE system SHALL block order, update cart, and suggest alternative actions.
- IF invalid payment method is used, THEN THE system SHALL prevent transaction and provide supported methods.

#### Order Tracking/Shipping Errors
- IF tracking number is invalid, THEN THE system SHALL notify user and advise to contact support.
- WHEN order is no longer eligible for address update/cancellation, THE system SHALL deny the action and explain why.

#### Product Review Errors
- IF user attempts to review without purchase, THEN THE system SHALL block submission and explain requirement.
- WHERE review window expired, THE system SHALL disallow submission/update and display window details.
- IF inappropriate content is detected, THEN THE system SHALL reject with clear feedback on policy.

#### Seller Inventory/Management Errors
- WHEN seller edits another seller's product, THE system SHALL deny access and log the event.
- IF trying to update inventory for discontinued SKU, THEN THE system SHALL block update and prompt cleanup.

#### Orders, Cancellation, and Refund Errors
- IF user attempts refund on ineligible order, THEN THE system SHALL reject and display refund policy.
- WHEN duplicate refund/cancellation is requested, THE system SHALL ignore or merge requests, showing explained status.

#### Admin Actions
- IF admin operates outside permission, THEN THE system SHALL block and log action.
- WHEN potentially destructive admin action is requested, THE system SHALL require confirmation and display warnings.

---

### Multi-Actor Error Flows
- WHEN seller receives an order they can't fulfill (out of stock), THE system SHALL allow seller to mark order as "Unable to Fulfill," automatically notify customer, trigger refund process, and alert admin for review.
- WHEN an order dispute is created, THE system SHALL escalate to admin and provide all actors with a dispute status and contact point.

---

### Mermaid: Example Error Handling Flow (Payment Failure)
```mermaid
graph LR
    U["Customer Attempts Payment"] --> G{"Payment Gateway Success?"}
    G -->|"Yes"| O["Order Placed"]
    G -->|"No"| F["Show Payment Failure Reason"]
    F --> R{"Retry?"}
    R -->|"Yes"| U
    R -->|"No"| X["Cancel Checkout & Keep Cart"]
```

---

## User Notifications and Feedback Patterns

### Customer
- Errors are always conveyed in familiar, actionable language, indicating what went wrong and next steps (retry, correct, contact support).
- Recovery actions (links, buttons) are always available for self-service correction, except for legal or administrative escalations.
- WHEN possible, system SHALL auto-correct (e.g., trim spaces, suggest alternatives) and inform user.

### Seller
- Sellers receive notifications for errors/issues with their listings, inventory, or order processing. Clear guidance is provided for necessary actions or escalation paths.
- WHEN error relates to compliance or policy, THE system SHALL provide links to documentation or support resources.
- Seller dashboard SHALL display any unresolved errors for prompt action.

### Admin
- Admins are informed for any process error that cannot be resolved by regular users or sellers, with clear identification of affected records, actors, and recovery tools.
- Error logs and escalation queues are visible in the admin dashboard.
- Recovery or override actions are available per admin role.

---

## Best Practices for Error Transparency and Recovery
- Errors are proactive and user-centric: never expose technical details (e.g., stack traces), but always describe the business context.
- Recovery steps shall be easy, visible, and logged for audit.
- Users must always know their next possible action and estimated resolution time.
- Confirmation and validation steps are presented before irreversible or sensitive actions.
- Edge cases and conflicts (e.g., stock depletion during payment, admin-seller disputes) are handled by escalating to humans with full context.

---

## Summary
Robust error handling is central to the platform’s reliability and reputation. All major error types, user-facing feedback, and recovery flows have been exhaustively documented according to the EARS methodology. Backend systems MUST implement all error messaging and recovery in business terms, never technical jargon, for all actors (customer, seller, admin). Diagrams and structured requirements herein support full transparency and a premium e-commerce experience.

files.content:
# Security and Compliance Requirements for E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

## 1. Account Security and Authentication Policies
### Account Management
- WHEN a new user (customer, seller, or admin) registers, THE system SHALL require secure credentials: unique email and password following complexity standards (minimum 8 characters, including upper/lowercase, number, and symbol).
- THE system SHALL employ email verification before any new account can access privileged features.
- WHEN a user requests a password reset, THE system SHALL verify their identity with a tokenized secure link, expiring within 30 minutes.
- WHEN a user changes sensitive account data (email, phone, password), THE system SHALL require current password confirmation or recent authentication.
- THE system SHALL restrict failed login attempts (e.g., 10 invalid tries in 1 hour), locking the account and notifying the user of suspicious activity.
- IF an account is locked due to suspicious activity, THEN THE system SHALL provide a secure unlocking process via email verification.
- WHERE a user has active sessions on multiple devices, THE system SHALL support single-device logout and full session revocation (from all devices).

### Authentication Flows
- THE platform SHALL use session tokens (e.g., JWT) with short-lived access and securely stored refresh tokens (e.g., httpOnly cookies or secure local storage).
- WHEN a session token expires, THE system SHALL require a refresh token or full re-authentication.
- THE system SHALL invalidate all tokens upon password change or manual session revocation by user or admin.
- WHERE an admin issues a forced logout or disables a user, THE system SHALL immediately terminate all user sessions and block further access until re-enabled.

## 2. Payment Security
- WHEN processing payments, THE system SHALL never store sensitive card data (PAN, CVV) on platform servers.
- THE platform SHALL integrate with PCI-DSS compliant payment gateways and SHALL redirect or tokenize sensitive payment data.
- WHEN a payment request is initiated, THE system SHALL present a secure, encrypted payment interface via the gateway’s solution (hosted form, iFrame, or redirect).
- THE system SHALL never disclose full payment information to any user or staff, including sellers and admins.
- WHERE a payment is unsuccessful or suspicious, THE system SHALL notify the buyer and securely log the attempt for audit compliance.
- WHEN refunds or disputes arise, THE system SHALL handle them within the payment gateway’s secure flow and document the process in the platform’s audit logs.

## 3. User Data Privacy
### Data Collection & Storage
- THE system SHALL collect and retain only the data needed for legitimate business operations (registration, order fulfillment, compliance, etc.).
- WHEN collecting personal data, THE system SHALL present a clear privacy policy and obtain explicit user consent (checkbox, agreement text) before first data submission.
- THE system SHALL store user data in secure, access-controlled databases with encryption at rest and in transit.
- WHERE data is transmitted between services or third parties (payment providers, shippers), THE system SHALL use encrypted protocols (e.g., TLS 1.2+).

### User Rights Management
- WHEN a user requests to view or export their personal data, THE system SHALL provide a timely, complete export in a standard format (e.g., CSV, JSON), ensuring proper authentication of requestor.
- WHEN a user requests partial or complete deletion of their personal data, THE system SHALL process the request within a defined legal timeframe (e.g., within 30 days), except where business or legal retention obligations apply.
- WHEN a user withdraws their consent for data processing, THE system SHALL immediately halt non-essential processing and notify all affected internal systems.
- WHERE required by law (e.g., GDPR), THE system SHALL allow users to access, rectify, erase, restrict, and object to personal data usage in a self-service manner or via admin process.

## 4. Audit Trails
- THE system SHALL keep immutable audit logs of security-critical system activities: login attempts (successful and failed), password changes, permission modifications, financial transactions, data exports, and deletion requests.
- WHEN an admin or seller accesses or modifies sensitive customer data, THE system SHALL log the actor, timestamp, reason (if applicable), and action taken.
- THE platform SHALL ensure that audit logs are tamper-resistant and retained for at least seven years or the minimum required by applicable law.
- IF a security breach, suspicious activity, or dispute is detected, THEN THE system SHALL provide complete audit records for investigation to authorized admins only.

## 5. Compliance Standards (e.g., GDPR, PCI-DSS)
- THE platform SHALL comply with major data protection and payment standards applicable to e-commerce businesses:
    - WHERE users are EU residents, THE system SHALL adhere to GDPR for data processing, including consent, right to access, erasure, portability, and breach notification (within 72 hours).
    - THE system SHALL ensure compliance with PCI-DSS for all payment processing, including non-storage of sensitive cardholder data, strong access control, and annual assessments through the payment processor.
    - WHERE the platform collects or processes information of minors, THE system SHALL obtain affirmative parental consent and implement enhanced privacy measures.
    - THE system SHALL prepare and maintain policies and notice templates to support legal compliance (privacy notice, cookie consent, breach notifications, data subject rights handling).
    - THE system SHALL conduct regular privacy impact assessments and security reviews to identify and mitigate risks.
- WHERE new regulations emerge (local or international), THE company SHALL periodically review and update policies and processes, maintaining compliance as a core operational principle.

## Summary & Success Criteria
- All sections above contain requirements written in EARS format and business-appropriate natural language where applicable.
- Performance, error handling, and user notification requirements for security/compliance are defined as part of the security objectives.
- Backend developers SHALL ensure all system features honor these business policies for account security, payment integrity, data privacy, auditability, and legal compliance throughout the platform lifecycle.

# Integration Requirements for the shoppingMall E-commerce Platform

## Introduction
This document outlines the full set of business requirements for integrating the shoppingMall platform with essential external service providers and partners. It focuses exclusively on the WHAT and WHY of integrations (not technical implementation) to enable backend teams to design, implement, and test integrations that directly enable business operations and user experiences. Each requirement is written in EARS where appropriate and addresses key integration-driven processes critical to the platform's success.

## Integration Summary Table
| Integration Category   | Business Purpose                                               |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Payment Gateways      | Process secure payments and manage refunds                      |
| Shipping/Logistics    | Fulfill, track, and update shipment status                      |
| Notification Partners | Send order/review/payment alerts via email, SMS, etc.           |
| Third-Party Accounts  | Enable easy authentication and data connection (social/login)    |

## Payment Gateway Integrations
### Business Rationale
E-commerce success depends on seamless payment acceptance, refunds, and payment status management. Multiple payment methods (credit/debit cards, e-wallets, bank transfer) are required for customer choice and business agility.

### Requirements
- THE payment system SHALL support integration with at least two leading payment gateways accepted in target markets.
- THE system SHALL support customer payments for orders using credit/debit cards, bank transfer, and at least one e-wallet.
- WHEN a customer places an order, THE platform SHALL initiate payment authorization and handle relevant statuses (approved, rejected, pending).
- IF payment fails or is declined, THEN THE platform SHALL provide clear, actionable instructions and allow order recovery or payment retry.
- WHEN a refund is approved, THE system SHALL trigger refund via the original payment gateway and update order/refund status promptly.
- THE platform SHALL ensure that all payment and refund processes are logged for audit and business analytics.
- THE system SHALL allow sellers to view payment statuses for their transactions but SHALL NOT expose sensitive customer payment details.

### Example Integration Touchpoints
- Payment authorization at checkout
- Payment status polling and update
- Refund initiation, status polling, and completion
- Dispute/chargeback notification workflows

## Shipping and Logistics Provider Connections
### Business Rationale
Customers demand timely delivery and accurate updates. Integration with leading logistics service(s) is critical for real-time shipment handling, tracking, and returns/cancellations.

### Requirements
- THE platform SHALL support integration with at least two recognized shipping/logistics partners providing national coverage and shipment tracking.
- WHEN an order is marked as ready for shipment by a seller, THE shipping connector SHALL transfer order details to the chosen logistics partner and retrieve a tracking number.
- WHEN a package is shipped or status updates (e.g., dispatched, in transit, out for delivery, delivered) occur, THE system SHALL update the customer and seller accordingly in near real time.
- IF a required shipping partner is unavailable, THEN THE system SHALL allow manual update by sellers and inform the customer of fulfillment status transparently.
- WHERE a customer requests order cancellation or return, THE platform SHALL initiate a pickup/return request with the logistics provider and monitor the process through completion.
- THE shipping system SHALL store and display tracking links for all shipped orders for reference by both customers and sellers.

### Example Integration Touchpoints
- Shipping label creation
- Dispatch and in-transit status notifications
- Delivery confirmation and feedback prompt triggers
- Return or pickup request initiation for cancellations/refunds

## Notification and Communication Partners
### Business Rationale
Notifications boost conversion, customer trust, and platform engagement. Integration with major notification/email/SMS providers is essential for timely alerts on critical business events.

### Requirements
- THE notification subsystem SHALL support integration with at least one email provider and one SMS or messaging gateway.
- WHEN events such as order placement, payment status changes, shipping/return milestones, or review requests occur, THE system SHALL trigger appropriate user- or seller-facing notifications via connected partners.
- WHERE communication partners experience outages or failures, THE system SHALL queue, retry, and escalate notification deliveries in accordance with business impact.
- THE notification system SHALL allow admins to configure content templates and toggle channels (SMS, email, push) by event type.
- THE system SHALL allow customers and sellers to opt in/out of specific notification types as required by privacy policies.
- THE platform SHALL log all notification events for audit, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

### Example Integration Touchpoints
- New order confirmation via email/SMS
- Payment success/failure notification
- Shipping update and package delivered announcement
- Review/rating request after delivery
- Admin alert for major system/process events

## Third-Party Authorization and Account Integration
### Business Rationale
Supporting third-party (social or SSO) login increases acquisition, conversion, and user engagement. Integration with major providers enables easy onboarding and account linking.

### Requirements
- THE authentication system SHALL support optional login via major third-party providers (e.g., Google, Facebook, Apple, or domestic equivalents relevant to market).
- WHEN a user registers or logs in with a third-party provider, THE system SHALL receive and validate user identity claims and create/tokenize the account as per platform policies.
- THE system SHALL provide secure account linking and unlinking for users who wish to connect/disconnect social or partner logins in their profile.
- IF third-party authentication fails, THEN THE platform SHALL guide the user through recovery flows and provide fallbacks to standard email/password login.
- THE system SHALL enable sellers and admins to use only standard platform login (not third-party) for increased control and security.
- THE authentication system SHALL log all third-party integration events for security and compliance.

### Example Integration Touchpoints
- Social login/SSO at registration or login
- Account linking/unlinking inside user profile
- Identity verification and consent management flows

## Cross-Integration Business Scenarios
Below are examples of how these integrations enable core platform workflows. For full user journeys, see the [User Flows and Journeys Document](./04-user-flows-and-journeys.md).

- WHEN a customer completes a purchase, THE system SHALL process payment via the integrated gateway, send notifications, and create a shipment order with logistics partners.
- WHEN a package reaches a shipping milestone, THE system SHALL trigger a notification to keep all actors informed.
- IF a payment or shipping update fails, THEN THE platform SHALL escalate via alternate communication channels (e.g., SMS). 
- WHEN a customer requests a cancellation/refund, THE platform SHALL coordinate payment, logistics, and communication flows across integrations, providing status updates to all actors.

## Constraints and Non-Functional Integration Considerations
- THE system SHALL ensure integrated partners (payment, shipping, notification) provide 99.5% or higher monthly uptime, with failover plans in place.
- THE platform SHALL not transmit or store sensitive payment credentials; payment gateways SHALL own PCI compliance.
- THE system SHALL track all integration interactions with full audit logs for compliance and troubleshooting.
- THE system SHALL process normal business events (payment, shipping, notification) and receive confirmation from integrations within 3 seconds for at least 95% of cases.
- THE platform SHALL support addition or replacement of integration partners with minimal downtime and no data loss.

## Mermaid Integration Flowchart

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Checkout Workflow"
    A["Customer Places Order"] --> B["Initiate Payment Gateway"]
    B --> C{"Payment Success?"}
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Create Shipping Order with Logistics Provider"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Notify Failure, Allow Retry"]
    D --> F["Send Confirmation Notification"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["Order Status Updated"]
  end

  subgraph "Shipping Updates"
    H["Logistics Partner Status Update"] --> I["System Receives Update"]
    I --> J["Notify Customer & Seller"]
    J --> K["Order Status Updated"]
  end
```

## Conclusion
All business requirements outlined above must be addressed through integration with proven, trusted external partners. This will ensure secure, reliable payment processing; fast, trackable deliveries; timely communications; and seamless user acquisition. Backend developers have full autonomy in the technical approach, choice of specific vendors, and implementation strategy, provided the above business requirements are satisfied and can be validated through end-to-end workflows.

files.reason: To present business-focused data flow and lifecycle requirements, specifying how information (orders, products, inventory, payments) moves and changes through the platform at a business process level, not technical layer.
constraints: Write all flows in business language, avoid technical details.
files.content:
# Data Flow and Lifecycle Requirements for ShoppingMall Platform

## Introduction

This document defines the comprehensive business flow and lifecycle for the ShoppingMall platform’s core entities: orders, products and inventory (SKUs/variants), payments, and related refunds/cancellations. It clarifies how information moves and changes as each entity progresses through its business life cycle, using natural language and the EARS requirements standard. All references are to business processes and expectations, not technical detail.

## Order Data Lifecycle

### Order Creation
- WHEN a customer confirms checkout, THE platform SHALL create a distinct order record containing all chosen products, SKUs, the delivery address, and payment method.
- THE platform SHALL assign a unique identifier to each order upon creation and set its initial status to "Pending Payment".
- WHEN the customer completes payment, THE platform SHALL change the status to "Payment Received" and reserve/deduct inventory for the SKUs in the order.

### Order Processing and Shipping
- WHEN payment is confirmed, THE platform SHALL mark the order as "Preparing Shipments" and notify the seller(s) to process packing and logistics.
- WHEN a seller marks an item as shipped, THE platform SHALL update the shipment status, record tracking information, and move the order’s status to "Shipped".
- WHEN the order is delivered or the customer confirms receipt, THE platform SHALL record the event and update order status to "Delivered" and then "Completed".

### Multi-Seller and Partial Shipping
- WHERE multiple sellers or items are ordered together, THE platform SHALL track separate shipment statuses for each relevant item/shipment within a single overarching order.

### Order Cancellation and Refunds
- IF payment is not received within a set window (e.g., 30 minutes), THEN THE platform SHALL automatically cancel the order and release reserved SKUs.
- WHEN a customer requests cancellation before shipping, THE platform SHALL cancel the order if no item has yet shipped and revert inventory.
- WHEN a return or refund is requested after delivery, THE platform SHALL mark the order status as "Refund/Return Requested" and trigger a seller/admin action for approval.
- WHEN a refund or cancellation is approved, THE platform SHALL adjust order status to "Refunded" or "Cancelled" as business logic dictates and restore stock appropriately.

#### Order Data Lifecycle Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Order Created"] --> B["Pending Payment"]
    B -->|"Payment Success"| C["Payment Received"]
    B -->|"Payment Timeout/Failure"| D["Cancelled"]
    C --> E["Preparing Shipment"]
    E --> F["Shipped"]
    F --> G["Delivered"]
    G --> H["Completed"]
    F -->|"Customer Cancels before Delivery"| I["Cancelled"]
    G -->|"Refund/Return Requested"| J["Refund Processing"]
    J -->|"Refund Approved"| K["Refunded"]
    J -->|"Refund Denied"| L["Completed"]
```

### Summary for Orders
- All status changes must be audit-trailed for actor, timestamp, and reason.
- Permission to update/view order status strictly follows the system’s permission matrix.

## Product and Inventory State Changes

### Product Listing & Updates
- WHEN a seller lists a product, THE platform SHALL require entry of at least one SKU (variant).
- WHEN product info (title, description, images, price, SKUs) changes, THE platform SHALL immediately reflect the changes and track them in an immutable audit log.

### SKU/Variant Management
- WHEN a SKU’s characteristics (color, size, etc.) change, THE platform SHALL validate SKU uniqueness within the product.
- IF a SKU is deleted, THEN THE platform SHALL prevent new orders for it but maintain historical data for past orders.

### Inventory Management
- WHEN any inventory change occurs (sale, restocking, admin/seller action), THE platform SHALL timestamp and record the new quantity and action source.
- IF a SKU’s inventory reaches zero, THEN THE platform SHALL set "Out of Stock" and prevent new orders for that SKU.

### Unpublishing/Deleting Products
- WHEN a product or SKU is unpublished/deleted, THE platform SHALL remove it from customer listings but retain all records for legal and order history.

#### Product and Inventory State Model
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Product Lifecycle"
        P1["Draft"] --> P2["Published"]
        P2 --> P3["Unpublished"]
        P2 --> P4["Deleted"]
    end
    subgraph "SKU Inventory State"
        S1["In Stock"] --> S2["Out of Stock"]
        S2 --> S3["Restocked"]
        S3 --> S1
    end
    P2 --> S1
```

### Summary for Product/Inventory
- No overselling permitted; changes must be real-time and logged.
- All actions related to product or inventory changes are auditable by admin.

## Payment and Refund Event Flows

### Payment Process
- WHEN customer initiates payment, THE platform SHALL start payment authorization with chosen gateway.
- WHEN payment succeeds, THE platform SHALL update the order and notify the customer and involved seller(s).
- IF payment fails, THEN THE platform SHALL clearly inform the customer and allow them to retry or use alternative methods.

### Refund Process
- WHEN a refund is triggered (by admin/seller after request), THE platform SHALL process refund via the gateway, update all order and payment logs, and notify all impacted parties.
- WHERE a partial shipment/refund situation arises, THE platform SHALL support partial refund and update relevant records per business rule.

#### Payment and Refund Lifecycle
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Order Placed"] --> B["Payment Initiated"]
    B -->|"Success"| C["Payment Confirmed"]
    B -->|"Failure"| D["Payment Failed"]
    C --> E["Order Shipping"]
    C -->|"Refund Requested"| F["Refund Initiated"]
    F -->|"Refund Success"| G["Refund Completed"]
    F -->|"Refund Failure"| H["Refund Declined"]
```

### Summary for Payment/Refunds
- Payment and refund events must be synchronized, reliable, and auditable; failure/recovery flows must be supported end-to-end.

## Data Retention and Archival Practices

### Record Retention Policies
- THE platform SHALL retain all transactional records (orders, payments, refunds, etc.) for at least the legally or contractually mandated time period (default 5 years, or longer as required).
- WHEN products or accounts are deleted, THE platform SHALL preserve historical data for audits and dispute resolution.
- WHEN data exceeds mandated retention duration, THE platform SHALL securely archive or erase it (with audit trail), except where subject to dispute/legal action.
- WHERE disputes or investigations are in progress, THE platform SHALL retain affected data regardless of retention expiration.
- THE platform SHALL provide clear notification to actors about data retention and archival policies at appropriate business interaction points.

## Visual Flows Reference
See above Mermaid diagrams for visual state and data progression across orders, products, SKUs, payments, and refunds. All diagrams use left-to-right orientation and double quotes in all node labels for parsing compatibility.

## Integration and References
For end-to-end lifecycle understanding, refer to:
- [User Flows and Journeys Documentation](./04-user-flows-and-journeys.md)
- [Business Rules and Validation Requirements](./06-business-rules-and-validations.md)

Business requirements above should be implemented in full alignment with referenced process documentation for consistency and completeness.

models.name: shopping_mall_configurations
models.description:
Platform-wide configuration entries managing system parameters, feature flags, and constants.

Allows admin-only CRUD of key-value structured settings that control feature toggles, global options, or business parameters for the entire shopping mall backend. Heavily referenced by all modules, with audit and soft deletion required for traceability.

plainFields.name: config_key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key name, used in service and API lookup. Recommended to namespace with prefixes by category or domain.

plainFields.name: config_value
plainFields.description: String or JSON-serialized value. Raw storage; business logic interprets entry per config_key.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of the configuration's role and effect for admin reference.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: active, inactive, or deprecated—for admin gating and safe rollout/testing.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of row creation (audit trail).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last mutation timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker for removed/legacy entries.

models.name: shopping_mall_categories
models.description:
Product and navigation category taxonomy, supporting arbitrarily deep nesting via self-referencing parent_id.

Each category row is used for user browsing, search filters, and system reference. Parent categories have parent_id = null. Admins manage category CRUD and soft delete for cross-domain stability.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Self-foreign key for category hierarchy—null for root categories. Cascades to build full tree structure.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique category name, as seen in UIs and for API reference.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Long-form description of purpose and coverage for admin/merchandiser context.

plainFields.name: sort_order
plainFields.description: Ordering for navigation and display; lower values first.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: active/inactive/deprecated for admin approval or programmatic use.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Audit trail—creation moment.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last admin/edit update.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete for safe deactivation.

models.name: shopping_mall_external_payment_providers
models.description:
Registered external payment providers for all enabled checkout flows and payment methods.

Defines all payment gateways/platforms (e.g., Stripe, Toss, PayPal) integrated by admin and referenced in order/payment tables. Directly managed by admins for status, audit, and usable methods in commerce flows. CRUD enabled via admin tools; uses status and soft delete to manage reconfiguration and deprecation safely. Uniquely keyed by provider_name and provider_code.

plainFields.name: provider_name
plainFields.description: Display name as shown in checkout UIs—unique for each provider.

plainFields.name: provider_code
plainFields.description: System integration key/code—unique for backend mapping and API orchestration.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: active/inactive/deprecated—controls available methods/platforms in UX.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Legal/business context and integration notes for provider.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp (for audit).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update (admin/edit context).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete—row remains for historical audit/logging.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipping_partners
models.description:
Official platform registry for logistics/shipping partners in buyer and seller flows.

All partners that can be used for order shipments, available for admin CRUD and for use in shipment, order, or tracking-related tables via FKs. Managed for status and audit; supports deprecation via soft delete but keeps historical/inactive partners visible for audit and referencing legacy data.

plainFields.name: partner_name
plainFields.description: Display name (UI/reference); unique.

plainFields.name: partner_code
plainFields.description: Integration code for backend (system use); unique.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: active/inactive/deprecated—admin only control.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Business and operational info about the partner.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation moment (audit).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Mutation/audit update time.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete for legacy/decommissioned partners.

models.name: shopping_mall_customers
models.description:
Registered customer account representing a buyer on the platform.

Holds personal and authentication data, including email for login, password hash, and registration status. Is the actor for all end-customer business flows. Each customer can maintain multiple addresses, and all cart, wish, and order histories are tied to this entity. A unique email is required per customer. Authentication audit enabled via related session table. Soft delete is omitted by business policy (hard delete only via admin action).

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Customer's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all customers.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt hash of the customer's login password. Used for secure authentication; plain passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Customer's legal full name for identification and order fulfillment.

plainFields.name: phone
plainFields.description: Customer's primary phone number for order and support contacts.

plainFields.name: is_email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the customer has completed email verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp in UTC.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last time customer record was updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_sessions
models.description:
Session token records for authenticated customer logins.

Tracks each web or mobile login, holding the session's connection context for audit and security. Linked to customers via customer_id, with composite index for fetch. Expired sessions denote logouts or security expiry. No extra metadata is included for device/user-agent; only core IP/href/referrer for compliance. Subsidiary stance to customer records; maintains audit trail.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: References the customer owning this session. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address for the client initiating the session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Original connection URL when the session was created.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL for the session's origin context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp in UTC.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration UTC time; null if currently active.

models.name: shopping_mall_sellers
models.description:
Registered seller account with legal business identity and verification status.

Holds core authentication and business contact information including unique email, password hash, business name, registration number, status, and compliance flag. Only verified sellers can onboard products. Each seller may have multiple addresses linked by the addresses table. Seller dashboards and product/inventory are strictly partitioned by this entity.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Seller's unique login email. Used for authentication and main point of contact.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt hash of the seller's login password. Plaintext passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: business_name
plainFields.description: Legal business name of the seller. Required for all compliance and public catalog exposure.

plainFields.name: registration_number
plainFields.description: Government-issued business registration or license number. Used for KYC and compliance.

plainFields.name: business_phone
plainFields.description: Official business contact phone number for support and notifications.

plainFields.name: is_email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether seller has verified their email address.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Seller account status: pending, approved, rejected, suspended, etc., as enforced by admin and business workflow.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp in UTC.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last time seller account was updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_sessions
models.description:
Authenticated session records for sellers accessing their dashboard or API.

Logs each session for audit and security tracking. Linked to sellers by seller_id. Key attributes are connection metadata: IP, href, and referrer. Session expiry supports both manual logout and automatic timeout. All business-side actions are traced back to session for compliance. Subsidiary to sellers.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: References seller owning this session. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address for this session's origin.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Source URL of the session creation event.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL for context at login.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiry datetime, or null if still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_admins
models.description:
Platform administrator account with root governance permissions.

Stores admin authentication, contact details, and activation status. Admin creation and updates are allowed only by other admins as per strict business rules. Used for all high-privilege actions including dispute, refund, platform configuration, and moderation. Email is unique per admin.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email for authentication and notification. Required for all admin communication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Admin's password hash for login authentication. Never holds plaintext.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Admin's full name for auditing, contact, and action logs.

plainFields.name: is_email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether admin email was verified/activated.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Admin account status; defines access: active, suspended, revoked, etc.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Datetime when admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Datetime when last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_sessions
models.description:
Session logs for each authenticated admin dashboard/API login.

Every instance records IP, entry URL, and referrer for each session. Session expiry signals logout/invalidation. Indexed by admin_id for audit purposes. Subsidiary to admin with strict linkage; key for compliance and oversight.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin user associated to this session. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Originating IP address for this admin session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Access URL at session start.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL when login occurred.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session created at timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration datetime, or null if still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_addresses
models.description:
Address book entry for shipping, billing, or business association for any user actor.

Each record details the full structured address: full name, street, city, province/state, postal code, country, and phone. Customer addresses are required; sellers may also have addresses for business documentation. Each address is linked to either a customer or a seller (never both), with at least one being non-null. Each user can hold up to 10 addresses. Optionally flagged as the default address. Soft deletes not supported—records are permanent unless directly erased.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: FK to owning customer, if this is a customer address. Nullable if belongs to a seller. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: FK to owning seller, if this is a seller address. Nullable if owned by a customer. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: full_name
plainFields.description: Recipient's name for shipping or billing purposes.

plainFields.name: street
plainFields.description: Street address, including building/unit number as applicable.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City for the address.

plainFields.name: province
plainFields.description: Province, state, or administrative region.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: ZIP/postal code formatted by country.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country name in ISO standard or local language.

plainFields.name: phone
plainFields.description: Contact phone number for delivery issues.

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Indicates if this is the actor's default address.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Address creation timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_verifications
models.description:
KYC/business verification status records for each seller actor.

Stores the state and reason for seller verification processing (e.g., pending, approved, rejected) and reviewer/admin audit trail. Contains all compliance documents and correspondence references submitted by the seller. Required for permission to list products. Each seller has one or more verifications over time, all records append-only. Status, reviewer, and all timestamps included for workflow traceability.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller under verification. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: reviewer_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who reviewed or verified this record. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Verification status: pending, approved, rejected, under_review, needs_more_info, etc.

plainFields.name: compliance_documents
plainFields.description: Documentation references or IDs for KYC or compliance. May be null during initial request.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Notes explaining state, rejection, or administrative requirements. May be null if not needed.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Datetime when this record was reviewed/decisioned.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_role_escalations
models.description:
Records of all privilege/role escalation requests and admin actions for platform actors.

Each record represents a direct request or admin-initiated alteration for increased privileges, e.g., customer-to-seller, seller-to-admin. Stores requestor, target role/status, current processing status, admin/actor attribution, processed result, and action logs for audit. Enables strict privilege boundary enforcement under supervision. Full append-only audit maintained.

foreignFields.name: requestor_actor_id
foreignFields.description: FK to customer, if requestor is a customer. May be null for seller/admin escalations. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: requestor_seller_id
foreignFields.description: FK to seller, if requestor is a seller. Nullable for customer/admin initiated. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: processed_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who processed/escalated this event if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: target_role
plainFields.description: Role requested by the escalator (customer, seller, admin, etc.).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Escalation status: pending, approved, rejected, under_review, revoked, etc.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Notes, justification, or admin comments for this role change request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role escalation request creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: processed_at
plainFields.description: Datetime when request was processed/decisioned.

models.name: shopping_mall_products
models.description:
Top-level catalog entity representing a unique product offered on the platform.

Each product record defines the core business information for listing in the marketplace, including title, description, price, and owner seller reference (as a foreign key to sellers in another domain component already created). Products are assigned to one or more categories via a separate mapping table. Multiple variant SKUs and images are associated with each product, reflecting available purchase options and media assets. The product table includes status fields (e.g., draft, published, archived), audit fields for full lifecycle traceability (created, updated, deleted times), and is the anchor point for all product filtering, search, and analytics.

Soft delete is supported for recovery and moderation workflows.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Owning seller for this product. References the {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Public product name, shown in catalog and search results.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed product description, with rich text and formatting if allowed by system.

plainFields.name: default_price
plainFields.description: Default display price for product overview (actual purchase price may be per SKU/variant).

plainFields.name: business_status
plainFields.description: Workflow status string; valid values: draft, published, archived, blocked, pending_approval, etc.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for product creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for last modification of this product.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker; null if product is active, set when product is deleted/archived.

models.name: shopping_mall_products_categories
models.description:
Junction table mapping multi-category assignments for each product.

Associates each product with one or more marketplace categories, supporting hierarchical or multi-category navigation, search, and filtering. Each row represents the membership of a single product in a single category. Indexes support efficient filtering and common lookup patterns.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Mapped catalog product. References {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_category_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned marketplace category. References {@link shopping_mall_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for mapping creation.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_skus
models.description:
Individual SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) for a specific variant or option of a catalog product.

Each SKU represents a unique variant of a product (e.g., color, size, option combinations), with independent inventory, price, and status. SKUs are linked to the parent product and to their attribute values (via subsidiary mapping table). Inventory, per-SKU pricing, out-of-stock flags, and barcode/business reference codes are managed here. SKUs are included in search and filtering.

Audit, status, and soft delete fields support traceability, operation, and moderation.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Parent catalog product for this SKU. References {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: Unique business SKU/barcode identifier within a product scope.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Sale price for this variant (overrides product default price if present).

plainFields.name: stock
plainFields.description: Inventory units available for this SKU.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Workflow status for SKU (e.g., active, out_of_stock, archived, draft).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for SKU creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for last SKU change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete flag: null if active, set when archived/deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_images
models.description:
Image/media asset records associated with products or SKUs.

Each row stores a single image file or media asset for a specific product or SKU. Images support position-based ordering (e.g., main image, gallery order), alt text for accessibility, CDN/URI reference, and a label for internal management. Can attach images directly to product or specific SKU using foreign key, but never both at the same time (business logic ensures this). 

Audit fields and soft delete are included for digital asset lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product that this image is associated with. Nullable if this is a SKU-specific image.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: SKU variant this image is associated with. Nullable if this is a product-level image.

plainFields.name: cdn_uri
plainFields.description: CDN or publicly accessible URI for the image media.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: Accessibility/text alternative for the image, shown on error/load fail.

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description: Image display position ordering for carousels/galleries. Lower values displayed first.

plainFields.name: label
plainFields.description: System/business management label (not shown to end users).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for asset creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for any update to asset.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker: null if active, set when removed/archived.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_attributes
models.description:
Dictionary of attribute types supported for variant construction in the catalog (e.g., color, size, material, option labels).

Defines the allowed attributes for SKUs under each product, managed separately from global attributes. Provides structure and display name for each attribute type, supports ordering in variant selection UIs, and ties to allowed values in the mapping table. Each attribute is linked to exactly one product.

Audit and soft delete fields for traceability.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product for which this attribute is used. References {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: attribute_name
plainFields.description: Logical name for this attribute (e.g., color, size); visible in variant picker.

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description: Display order for attribute in UI context. Lower appears first.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for attribute creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for last update of attribute.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker: null if active, set for attribute removal.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_attribute_values
models.description:
Link table mapping (for each SKU) the value of a particular attribute (e.g., red for color, XL for size) in variant construction.

Each row records the value of an attribute for a specific SKU, allowing the flexible definition of multi-attribute variants per SKU. Enables full filter and product option selection. Provides value name/label, audit fields, and supports multiple values per attribute/SKU mapping.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: SKU instance for which this attribute value is defined. References {@link shopping_mall_product_skus.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_attribute_id
foreignFields.description: Corresponding attribute type for this value. References {@link shopping_mall_product_attributes.id}.

plainFields.name: value_display_name
plainFields.description: Renderable text for value (e.g., 'Red', 'XL', 'Matte').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for value mapping creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp for any value update.

models.name: shopping_mall_carts
models.description:
Customer shopping cart root entity.

Each cart is directly associated with an authenticated customer and serves as the persistent container for all shopping intents. Only one active cart exists per customer, preventing duplication. Carts are required for all add-to-cart and checkout flows, ensuring end-to-end state tracking and inventory validation within the platform. All items in the cart are managed through subsidiary cart item records. Deleted or checked-out carts are explicitly removed from the system.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Linked customer. References {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Cart creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last updated timestamp for cart state.

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Individual item records within a shopping cart.

Each record represents a single SKU in a customer's cart, including the desired quantity. Cart items are always associated with a parent cart and directly reference the intended product SKU. Only one cart item is allowed per SKU, per cart; duplicates are prevented by a composite unique constraint. This design enforces clean inventory operations, ensures correct add/remove/update logic, and supports multi-SKU carts. Cart items are always managed as part of their cart lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Parent cart reference. {@link shopping_mall_carts.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Target SKU. {@link shopping_mall_product_skus.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Desired quantity for this SKU in the cart. Must be positive and less than or equal to available inventory.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Cart item creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modified timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_wishlists
models.description:
Customer wishlist root entity for persistent product interest.

Each wishlist is owned by a single customer and contains items representing SKUs the customer is interested in but does not intend to purchase immediately. Each customer has at most one wishlist. Wishlists persist through account sessions and device changes, helping customers track and later revisit interesting products. Items in the wishlist are managed as subsidiary records.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Linked customer. References {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Wishlist creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the wishlist.

models.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_items
models.description:
Individual wishlist items attached to a customer's wishlist.

Each wishlist item represents a product SKU the customer is interested in saving for later. Items are linked both to the parent wishlist and the referenced SKU. No duplicate SKUs are allowed within a single wishlist, ensured by composite unique constraint. This enables efficient wishlist management and migration to cart flows when the customer decides to purchase. Item addition and removal is always managed as part of the wishlist lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_id
foreignFields.description: Parent wishlist. References {@link shopping_mall_wishlists.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: SKU referenced by this wishlist item. {@link shopping_mall_product_skus.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Wishlist item creation timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_orders
models.description:
Represents the primary order entity for all purchases made on the platform.

Captures the high-level details of each order submitted by a customer, including references to the customer placing the order, the shipping address, and relevant payment and seller information. Orders serve as the anchor for all associated items, shipments, status changes, and audit logs. Multiple items and shipments may be related to one order, reflecting multi-SKU, multi-seller, and split-shipment scenarios. This model is independently managed and forms the primary lifecycle entity for all order operations. All temporal fields support robust audit trails and soft deletion as needed.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: References the purchasing customer. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_address_id
foreignFields.description: The delivery address for this order. {@link shopping_mall_addresses.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Main seller responsible for this order (single-seller context). {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: Platform-unique business order number, used for external references and customer support. Example: ORD202500001.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current platform order status: e.g., pending, paid, cancelled, shipped, delivered, refunded.

plainFields.name: total_amount
plainFields.description: Final order total amount including all items, taxes, shipping, and discounts if any.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code (ISO 4217). E.g., USD, KRW.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Order creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for this order.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp; null if order is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_items
models.description:
Stores the breakdown of each order into per-SKU, per-product items.

Each record represents a unique product/SKU that is part of a given order, allowing complete normalization of order contents for inventory, fulfillment, analytics, and post-order processing. This model enables accurate tracking of quantities, price per SKU, refunds at item level, and inventory movements. Items are grouped under their parent order but retain individual references for fulfillment and shipment attachment.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order to which this item belongs. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: The ordered product. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: The specific SKU (variant) purchased. {@link shopping_mall_product_skus.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units of this SKU ordered.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Unit price at time of order for this SKU (discounts included, if any).

plainFields.name: subtotal
plainFields.description: Subtotal before order-level adjustments for this item (quantity × unit_price).

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code (ISO 4217). E.g., USD, KRW.

plainFields.name: delivered
plainFields.description: True if this item has been marked as delivered in fulfillment tracking.

plainFields.name: refunded
plainFields.description: True if this item has been refunded through returns/workflow.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Order item creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Order item last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp; null if active.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_shipments
models.description:
Represents a shipment or fulfillment batch associated with one or more items in an order.

Tracks the logistics information for each discrete shipment event—supporting split orders, multi-package delivery, and real-time tracking for both customers and sellers. Shipments reference the order, designated shipping partner, external tracking information, shipped and expected delivery dates, and status. This table enables precise management of complex fulfillment and last-mile delivery workflows.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order associated with this shipment. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_shipping_partner_id
foreignFields.description: Linked shipping partner. {@link shopping_mall_shipping_partners.id}.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Shipping partner/tracking-provided unique tracking number for this shipment.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Shipment status: e.g., pending, shipped, in_transit, delivered, returned.

plainFields.name: ship_date
plainFields.description: Date the shipment was handed to logistics partner; null if not yet shipped.

plainFields.name: expected_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Expected or promised delivery date; may be null if unknown.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of confirmed arrival; null if not delivered.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Shipment creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for this shipment.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp; null if shipment is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_status_histories
models.description:
Historical log of all order status transitions and major business state changes for audit and workflow compliance.

Each entry represents a snapshot of the order's state at a point in time, retaining the entire status, comment, actor (user/admin/system), and timestamp. Enables strict traceability for business, legal, and operational purposes.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order associated with this status transition. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who performed this action, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who performed this action, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who performed this action, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: from_status
plainFields.description: Previous status before transition.

plainFields.name: to_status
plainFields.description: New status after transition.

plainFields.name: comment
plainFields.description: Optional business or workflow comment entered by the actor or system.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of this status transition.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_audit_logs
models.description:
Append-only audit log recording every significant action or update along the lifecycle of orders.

Includes irreversible change events, actor, timestamp, action details, context, and (optionally) snapshot data for business process compliance and security. Ensures all activity affecting order lifecycle can be traced for investigation and legal defense. Not intended for deletion or modification post-recording.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order associated with this audit event. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who performed this action, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who performed this action, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who performed this action, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of audited action (e.g., status_change, address_update, refund_initiated).

plainFields.name: details_json
plainFields.description: Optional serialized details/context for this action in JSON form.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp (UTC) when this audit event was recorded.

models.name: shopping_mall_payments
models.description:
Primary payment record for all customer orders processed by the shopping mall platform.

Represents an initiated or completed payment against one or more orders. Stores amounts, currency, payment method type, status, and provider references. Tracks external payment provider transaction IDs, internal tokens, and acts as the main business entity for all financial flows within the system.

Captures associated actor (customer or seller) and references the payment provider integration. Interaction with refunds, status tracking, and audit log tables are mediated by this entity. Soft deletion supported for audit and compliance.
