### `shopping_mall_reviews`

Product reviews submitted by customers for products they have purchased,
per order item/SKU.

Each review is created by a verified customer and is always linked to a
specific order item and product SKU, ensuring that only actual purchases
can generate reviews. The review includes rating reference, summary, body
text, moderation status, withdrawal tracking, and full traceability to
the session and customer for audit and abuse prevention. Reviews can
exist in draft, published, or withdrawn states and are subject to content
moderation.

Soft-deletion is supported, with moderation and withdrawal tracked via
status history. This model is central to product feedback, search, and
moderation workflows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`
  > Reference to the customer who authored the review. {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `shopping_mall_customer_session_id`
  > Session during which the review was created. {@link
  > shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`: Product that the review is about. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `shopping_mall_product_sku_id`: SKU of the product reviewed. [shopping_mall_product_skus.id](#shopping_mall_product_skus).
- `shopping_mall_order_id`
  > Order in which this review's product was purchased. {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `shopping_mall_order_item_id`
  > Specific order item this review is linked to. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_rating_id`
  > Rating record for this review and SKU. {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_ratings.id}.
- `title`: Short summary/title of the review. Required for all published reviews.
- `body`
  > Body text of the review. Minimum 10 characters, maximum 1000. Editable by
  > customer within allowed window.
- `is_draft`: Indicates if the review is a draft (not yet published).
- `withdrawn_at`
  > Timestamp if the customer withdraws the review (soft delete for
  > user-initiated removal).
- `moderation_status`: Current moderation status (e.g., pending, approved, rejected, flagged).
- `moderation_reason`
  > Optional field indicating the reason for rejection or flagging during
  > moderation.
- `created_at`: DateTime when the review was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Last update time for this review (includes customer edits and moderator
  > actions).
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker (for platform/admin removal or purge).

### `shopping_mall_review_responses`

Seller responses to customer reviews, visible alongside the original review.

Each response is created by the seller of the product reviewed, providing
clarification, acknowledgment, or additional information in response to
customer feedback. Each response is linked to the specific review and the
seller account.

Full traceability to session and seller is maintained for auditing. Only
one response is allowed per review; responses can be edited or withdrawn
by seller or admin. Moderation is supported via status and reason fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`
  > Unique link to the review being responded to. One response per review.
  > [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews).
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`: Seller who wrote the response. [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `shopping_mall_seller_session_id`
  > Session during which the response was written. {@link
  > shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id}.
- `body`: Textual response from seller. Minimum 10, maximum 1000 characters.
- `withdrawn_at`: Timestamp if seller withdraws or deletes their response.
- `moderation_status`: Current moderation status for the response.
- `moderation_reason`: Optional reason for moderation action (rejection/flagging).
- `created_at`: When the response was created.
- `updated_at`: Last updated time.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker (for admin/content removal).

### `shopping_mall_product_ratings`

Standalone product rating entity tied to a specific customer and product
SKU.

Stores the numeric (1–5 stars) rating value that a verified customer
assigns to a product SKU as part of their review. Enforces the rule that
each customer can rate each product SKU only once (per completed
purchase). Ratings are referenced in reviews for search and aggregation;
this separation allows display of rating stats even for unreviewed
purchases and efficient rating aggregation per product/SKU.

Audit trail includes customer and session for verification. Only allows
update by the original customer within the edit window.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`: Customer who provided the rating. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `shopping_mall_customer_session_id`
  > Session when the rating was submitted. {@link
  > shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`: Product being rated. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `shopping_mall_product_sku_id`: SKU of the rated product. [shopping_mall_product_skus.id](#shopping_mall_product_skus).
- `shopping_mall_order_id`: Order associated with this rating. [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders).
- `shopping_mall_order_item_id`
  > Specific order item this rating applies to. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.
- `value`: Numeric rating value (1–5 stars).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of rating creation.
- `updated_at`: Last update time for rating.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker (if rating is removed or replaced).

### `shopping_mall_review_status_histories`

Snapshot table recording all moderation, withdrawal, and status events
for a given review.

Each record represents a point-in-time event (such as publication,
rejection, flagging, withdrawal) with full traceability to the actor
(customer, seller, admin) and session responsible for the change. This
enables a comprehensive audit history for each review, covering all
moderation workflow steps and supporting business auditability and
dispute resolution.

Designed as append-only for integrity, with immutable event data and
related descriptions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`
  > The review affected by this status event. {@link
  > shopping_mall_reviews.id}.
- `actor_customer_id`
  > Optional: Customer who performed this action (if actor is a customer).
  > [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `actor_seller_id`
  > Optional: Seller who performed this action (if actor is a seller). {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Optional: Admin who performed this action (if actor is an admin). {@link
  > shopping_mall_admins.id}.
- `actor_session_id`
  > Optional: Session in which the action was triggered. Session type matches
  > the actor type. [shopping_mall_admin_sessions.id](#shopping_mall_admin_sessions).
- `status`
  > New status set for the review (e.g., created, published, rejected,
  > flagged, withdrawn, deleted).
- `reason`
  > Optional explanation for status change (e.g., admin notes or moderation
  > reasoning).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the status event occurred.

### `shopping_mall_admin_action_logs`

Record of every privileged or system-level action performed by admin
actors across the platform.

Captures the immutable trace of all administrative actions, including
user modifications, order overrides, dispute resolutions, and escalated
interventions. Provides detailed attribution with actor, target entity,
action type, and optional contextual notes.
Crucial for compliance audits, forensic analysis, dispute defense, and
role-based access tracing. Each entry includes timestamp, responsible
admin (FK), contextual references (which may be user, seller, order,
product, etc.), and a required action category/type for grouped analysis.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_admin_id`: Admin actor responsible for action. [shopping_mall_admins.id](#shopping_mall_admins).

  > Categorical type of admin action (e.g., user_suspend, order_refund,
  > role_escalate, config_change). Enables grouped analysis of actions.
- `context_info`
  > Optional JSON-encoded or text data providing additional context (object
  > state, request params, results, etc.).
- `created_at`: Time the admin action was performed.

### `shopping_mall_audit_logs`

Comprehensive audit log capturing sensitive and high-privilege platform
events affecting compliance-relevant data.

Logs changes and accesses for critical operations (e.g., user PII
changes, financial record updates, permission modifications, and security
events). Includes full actor attribution, audit-relevant target entity,
change type, risk classification, compliance tag, and immutable create
timestamp.
Indispensable for regulatory reviews, incident response, and integrity
verification of privileged or risky operations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Admin actor responsible for audited event. Nullable if external system or
  > automated (system process). [shopping_mall_admins.id](#shopping_mall_admins).
- `actor_seller_id`
  > Seller actor if the audited event is seller-performed. Nullable if not
  > relevant. [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `actor_customer_id`
  > Customer actor if the event was customer-performed. Nullable if not
  > relevant. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `change_type`
  > Nature of audited change (e.g., access, update, delete,
  > permission_change, data_export).
- `risk_level`
  > Risk classification by business/policy (e.g., low, medium, high,
  > critical).
- `compliance_tag`
  > Compliance tag or business rule identifier justifying audit entry (e.g.,
  > GDPR_ARTICLE5, PCI_LOG, SOX_ACCESS).
- `audit_detail`
  > Detailed info about the change; may be structured JSON or plain text
  > depending on event type.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when audit entry was recorded.

### `shopping_mall_escalation_queues`

or require investigation. Each entry tracks the initiating actor,
responsible role/queue (e.g., admin, compliance), current status,
escalation reason, priority, and resolution timestamps. Supports advanced
filtering by status, queue, reason, and time for operational management
and workflow automation.

Properties as follows:

  > ID of seller initiator for cases started by a seller. Optional if not
  > applicable. [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `initiator_actor_customer_id`
  > ID of customer initiator for cases started by a customer. Optional if not
  > applicable. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).

  > ID of assigned admin handling the escalation. Null if auto/unassigned.
  > [shopping_mall_admins.id](#shopping_mall_admins).
- `escalation_type`
  > Business category for escalation (e.g., refund_dispute, policy_violation,

- `reason_detail`
  > Detailed explanation of why the event is escalated. Full business context

- `status`
  > Current state in workflow (e.g., open, investigating, resolved, closed,
  > rejected, admin_pending, compliance_review).
- `priority`
  > Priority classification for triage (e.g., low, normal, high, urgent,

- `created_at`: Timestamp when escalation was created.
- `resolved_at`: Time when escalation was closed/resolved (nullable until resolved).

### `shopping_mall_refund_requests`

Customer-initiated refund requests for orders or items within the
shopping mall platform.

Each record represents a formal refund request made by a customer for an
eligible order or order item. The table tracks request reasons, status,
requested and actual refund amounts, associated actors (customer, seller,
admin), and links to any associated dispute. It is integral to the
resolution workflow for cancellations, returns, or disputes. All changes
and outcomes are auditable and support regulatory compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`
  > Foreign key linking refund request to the affected order. {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`
  > Customer who submitted the refund request. {@link
  > shopping_mall_customers.id}.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Seller responsible for the transaction in dispute. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

  > Admin involved in processing or decision for this refund request, if
  > applicable. Nullable. [shopping_mall_admins.id](#shopping_mall_admins).

  > Current status of the refund request (pending, approved, rejected,

- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last modification (status update, note, etc.).
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp for soft-deletion. Nullable: present only if entity is
  > logically deleted.

- `created_at`: Timestamp when this history record was created.

### `shopping_mall_dispute_messages`

All direct messages exchanged between actors (customer, seller, admin)
within the context of a specific dispute.

Each row represents an individual message, including sender/receiver,
message content, role, temporal data, and linkage to the dispute.
Supports threaded, auditable communication as part of the escalation and
negotiation process.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_dispute_id`
  > Link to parent dispute for this message. {@link
  > shopping_mall_disputes.id}.
- `shopping_mall_sender_admin_id`: Admin user who sent this message (nullable if another actor).
- `shopping_mall_sender_seller_id`: Seller who sent this message (nullable if another actor).
- `shopping_mall_sender_customer_id`: Customer who sent this message (nullable if another actor).
- `shopping_mall_receiver_admin_id`: Admin user receiving this message (nullable if another actor).
- `shopping_mall_receiver_seller_id`: Seller who received this message (nullable if another actor).
- `shopping_mall_receiver_customer_id`: Customer who received this message (nullable if another actor).
- `role`: Role of sender (admin, seller, customer) for easy filtering.
- `content`: Body of the message as exchanged within the dispute.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when message was sent.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp. Present only if message is logically deleted.

### `shopping_mall_shipments`

Shipment records for order fulfillment and logistics event tracking.

Captures all shipment detail for order items shipped via any integrated
partner, including references to orders, order items, the selected
carrier, label/tracking numbers, shipping status, and API/provider result
codes. Used for both platform-initiated and manual shipments by sellers
or admins.

Provides full auditability with actor attribution (who
created/updated/cancelled), label/manifest data, and timestamps for each
shipment event.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key.
- `order_id`
  > Order this shipment is part of. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `order_item_id`
  > Specific item in the order that this shipment fulfills. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.
- `shipping_partner_id`
  > Shipping/logistics provider handling this shipment. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_shipping_partners.id}.
- `created_by_admin_id`
  > Admin who created this shipment record, if automated. Nullable; present
  > if admin assigned the carrier.
- `created_by_seller_id`
  > Seller who created or fulfilled this shipment, if not auto-assigned.
  > Nullable; present if the seller itself handed off to carrier.
- `carrier_tracking_code`
  > Carrier-assigned or external shipment/tracking code/number for reference
  > to shipping label or manifest. Nullable for shipments where code is not
  > yet issued.
- `status`
  > Current shipment status. Valid values: pending, ready, picked_up,
  > in_transit, delivered, cancelled, returned. Status transitions follow
  > fulfillment and return lifecycle rules.
- `manifest_url`
  > Optional download URI for shipping label or manifest provided by the
  > carrier. Nullable if not supported.
- `provider_response_code`
  > Last received status code/result from the API provider
  > (success/fail/integration result, if any). Nullable if no API call made
  > yet.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the shipment record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to the shipment record.
- `delivery_at`
  > Timestamp when the shipment was marked as delivered by the carrier or
  > customer. Nullable if not yet delivered.
- `cancelled_at`: Timestamp if/when this shipment was cancelled. Nullable if not cancelled.

### `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories`

Chronological tracking updates and carrier event logs for each shipment.

Captures a complete, append-only history of carrier-side/warehouse-side
shipment updates from dispatch to delivery. All status changes, tracking
location events, and relevant carrier messages with actors, timestamps,
geo-coordinates, provider event codes, and free-form tracking text are
stored here.

Serves as an audit trail and full shipment journey visibility for
platform users and admins. Accessible only via the parent shipment, never
directly edited or deleted by users.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key.
- `shipment_id`
  > Shipment that this tracking event belongs to. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_shipments.id}.
- `event_time`: Timestamp of the tracking event as provided by the carrier or system.
- `location`
  > Reported location (e.g., city, depot, or delivery point) for this event.
  > Nullable if not provided by carrier.
- `latitude`: Latitude coordinate attached to the event, if available. Nullable.
- `longitude`: Longitude coordinate attached to the event, if available. Nullable.
- `event_code`
  > Provider-specific event code (e.g., OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, DELIVERED, HELD,
  > etc.). Nullable for free-form events.
- `status`
  > Status code at this event step (e.g., pending, in_transit, delivered,
  > exception, returned). Used for shipment status timeline.
- `tracking_message`
  > Full carrier or system-provided message as shown to both admins and
  > customers for shipment progress updates.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this tracking event record was created in the platform DB.

### `shopping_mall_return_requests`

Return, pickup, and shipment reverse logistics request records.

Captures customer- or seller-initiated requests to return or pick up
delivered items, including reason, status, actor attribution, scheduled
pickup, and all carrier/shipment integration info. Enables tracking of
the full lifecycle of returns from customer submission to carrier pickup,
delivery to warehouse, and completion/cancellation.

Return requests are linked to specific order items and can be referenced
in refund or dispute management. All requested actions are audit-trailed
including user/actor IDs and timestamps for resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key.
- `order_id`
  > Order this return request refers to. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_orders.id}.
- `order_item_id`
  > Order item being returned or picked up. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.
- `requested_by_customer_id`
  > Customer requesting the return or pickup. Nullable if request was not
  > customer-initiated.
- `requested_by_seller_id`
  > Seller requesting return/pickup (for defective goods, etc.). Nullable if
  > not applicable.
- `shipping_partner_id`
  > Shipping partner assigned to the return/pickup. Nullable until carrier is
  > selected.
- `reason`
  > Free-form reason for return or pickup provided by the actor (customer,
  > seller, or admin). Displayed in detail views and tracking.
- `status`
  > Current status of the return/pickup request. Valid values: pending,
  > approved, scheduled, picked_up, delivered, completed, rejected,
  > cancelled. Required for workflow state machine.
- `pickup_address`
  > Address where the item should be picked up (defaults to order delivery
  > address if omitted). Nullable if carrier not yet assigned.
- `scheduled_pickup_at`
  > Scheduled date/time for the carrier to pick up the item (timezone:
  > Asia/Seoul). Nullable if not scheduled yet.
- `provider_tracking_code`
  > Tracking code or RMA from the shipping partner for this pickup/return.
  > Nullable until assigned.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the return request was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update to the return request record.
- `completed_at`
  > Timestamp when this return/pickup request was fully completed (goods
  > delivered to warehouse/refund processed). Nullable until finished.
- `cancelled_at`
  > Timestamp if/when this return/pickup request was cancelled. Nullable if
  > not cancelled.
- `deleted_at`
  > Nullable; when present, marks this record as soft deleted, for
  > audit/history recovery.

The operation verifies credentials against stored records, handling all error states for incorrect password, missing account, or locked/disabled seller statuses using only those fields present in schema.

On success, it issues JWT access and refresh tokens as described by the IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized DTO. This is the canonical login entrypoint for all seller account activity.

Security controls include throttling on repeated failed login attempts, secure password transmission, and ensuring only required data fields (as per schema and DTO) are accepted in the request body. No extraneous profile or non-auth fields are accepted.

Login is a public operation (authorizationActor: null) but all subsequent authenticated business operations require valid tokens, linking this operation to the seller login session lifecycle and session storage if schemas for session or audit logs exist.

All referenced credential fields must be verified to exist in the shopping_mall_sellers table, and the login handler may NOT assume standard fields if they are absent from the schema.
operations.summary: Authenticate a seller and issue a JWT token pair using schema-defined login credentials.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials (schema-defined)

responseBody.description: Authentication result object

operations.name: login

operations.specification: This operation refreshes expired or near-expiry JWT-based tokens for an authenticated seller actor. It accepts a refresh token and, if valid, issues a new access/refresh token pair as per the authentication DTO. The operation requires that a valid seller session exists, and the refresh token matches the appropriate structure and signing rules. Only schemas referencing seller session or token management (if present) should be referenced here. Do NOT assume refresh session storage if no session table is present in Prisma; simply validate token cryptographically. Errors are clearly reported for expired, malformed, or tampered tokens following security policy. The returned type follows the authorized DTO standard for sellers. This endpoint is actor-agnostic in path structure, and authentication context is established solely from the provided refresh token. Token refresh is essential for seamless session continuity and secure token lifecycle management for sellers. Only real schema support should be referenced in prerequisites or operation logic.
operations.description:
This API accepts a valid refresh token, as defined in the authentication DTO for sellers, and issues a new JWT access/refresh token pair if the refresh token is valid. It implements token rotation and advanced security controls such as issued-at/expiration checks, scope/claim verification, and rotation logics if a refresh session table exists in the schema.

On success, it returns the new tokens as IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized response. Token renewal is critical for seamless authentication retention by seller actors using long-lived dashboard/API sessions, and the implementation should not go beyond schema support for session/token storage.

The operation fails with clear errors on attempt to use expired, reused, or cryptographically invalid tokens. This endpoint does not require an authenticated context (authorizationActor: null) because authentication is performed via cryptographic token validation.

Security notes: all refresh token logic uses only schema-supported session/token features, with no reference to features unsupported by the schema. This ensures security policy alignment and DTO compatibility.

For sellers, refresh is required for persistent session management and security; it is a mandatory part of the authentication lifecycle.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for seller, issuing new access/refresh token pair if the refresh token is valid.

requestBody.description: Refresh token request body for seller

responseBody.description: Authentication result object

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification:
This operation enables platform administrators to register an admin account on the platform and receive initial authentication tokens. It directly relates to the 'shopping_mall_admins' Prisma table, supporting the onboarding of new admin users. The endpoint collects required registration credentials (such as username and password fields defined in the admin schema) and provisions an admin user record with all necessary default fields. Upon successful registration, the operation responds with JWT tokens referencing the 'IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized' type.

This join flow ensures that all required fields (from the schema, e.g., email, password, admin_name, etc.) are validated and stored appropriately. The system applies strict validation according to field constraints (such as unique email or required password complexity specified in the Prisma schema or business rules). After successful creation, the response includes the necessary authentication payload for subsequent operations using the issued token pairs.

This operation is public, allowing onboarding of authorized platform administrators. Security controls prevent mass registrations or unauthorized elevation. The operation only provisions fields available and specified in the 'shopping_mall_admins' table.

Error handling covers duplicate registration, validation failures (including schema-level unique fields, e.g., email), and system errors. Related operations include admin login and token refresh flows.
operations.description:
This API operation allows registration of new admin accounts into the system by collecting required credentials such as username, email, and password, as specified in the 'shopping_mall_admins' Prisma schema. All input fields are validated strictly according to the schema's constraints (such as unique email, password policy, and required primitive fields). The admin account is created and the administrator receives both an access token and a refresh token in the response.

Implementation leverages the available schema fields to bind each input field directly to the database, ensuring that only present fields are requested and stored. Only the fields available in the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema can be used for registration (with additional features omitted if they are not defined in the schema).

This operation is tied to admin onboarding business logic, with registration being reserved for authorized actors and limited in frequency to mitigate abuse. The authentication tokens returned enable the admin to log in and maintain authenticated sessions in subsequent requests.

Security consideration: Registration abuse is prevented by business logic limitations and auditing. All write operations are transactional, and rollback is triggered for any unique constraint or business logic violations based on schema specification.

Related: login (credential authentication via /auth/admin/login) and refresh (JWT/authorization token renewal via /auth/admin/refresh).
operations.summary: Register a new platform admin in the shopping_mall_admins table and issue JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Payload for admin registration (join) operation. Maps all registrable fields from the shopping_mall_admins schema, such as email, password, username, and any other required primitive fields.

responseBody.description: JWT tokens and authenticated session details for the admin actor, as per business security policy.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This operation authenticates platform admin credentials (such as email and password, per the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema) and issues new authentication tokens on successful verification. It queries the 'shopping_mall_admins' table, checks all login credentials, validates them via secure routines matching schema constraints, and returns a fresh access token and refresh token upon success.

All input credentials must strictly correspond to available fields in the Prisma schema (e.g., 'email', 'password' if those fields exist). Authentication is performed in full compliance with configured security policies, including password hashing and lockout on repeated failures. The operation only supplies fields that exist in the schema—no assumptions are made about non-existent columns.

A successful response contains a newly issued JWT token set using the 'IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized' type. Authentication failures due to invalid credentials, locked accounts, or validation errors return appropriate error responses. Security and audit requirements leverage logging and anti-abuse rules per the requirements analysis.

This login flow complements the join and refresh operations for full admin session lifecycle management. Credentials and session tokens are never exposed in logs or error messages.
operations.description:
This API authenticates an admin account using credentials such as email and password (or only those that exist in the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema). It validates admin credentials against the stored database record, using secure password hashing and comparison as appropriate for the schema fields. On successful authentication, the admin receives new authentication tokens (access and refresh), formatted per the unified security model and response schema conventions.

Only schema-defined fields are eligible for authentication. Rate limiting, login failure tracking, and administrator lockout are enforced to prevent brute-force and enumeration attacks, as specified by security requirements. Admin sessions are established securely, never exposing sensitive information in error conditions.

This is a public endpoint, accessible to admin users attempting to log in. After authentication, the JWT tokens conform to the required output DTO. Related operations: admin token refresh (/auth/admin/refresh) and admin registration (/auth/admin/join).
operations.summary: Authenticate admin credentials and issue new JWT tokens via the shopping_mall_admins table.

requestBody.description: Payload with all necessary admin login credential fields derived from the shopping_mall_admins Prisma schema (e.g., email, password).

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and session details for admin actor.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation issues new authentication tokens for a currently authenticated admin user by verifying a valid, non-expired refresh token. It is associated with the session management logic for platform administrators, specifically built on the 'shopping_mall_admins' table/session store. The endpoint accepts a refresh token in the request body (or via secure cookie transport, as specified in security requirements), validates the token's issuer and validity, and issues a new access/refresh token pair upon success.

Validation rules follow schema-based and business constraints: only tokens issued for valid, existing admin users in the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema are accepted. The entire session renewal process enforces constraints from the database (e.g., soft-deleted users, revoked/admin-terminated accounts). Only fields/schema support verified are used.

The response type is 'IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized', containing updated tokens. This operation is part of the standard secure session management flow, complementing join (registration) and login for a complete administrator authentication lifecycle.
operations.description:
This API receives a valid refresh token for a platform admin, validates the token against the session context and the 'shopping_mall_admins' schema, and issues a new authentication token set. The token rotation logic is schema-driven, supporting only what is present in the database. If the admin is inactive, deleted, or fails other schema-level conditions, an error is returned.

The operation strengthens security by enforcing strict validation of the refresh token, user identity, and compliance with session management requirements. It enables persistent platform admin authentication without requiring re-entry of credentials, as long as the existing session remains valid and the admin record exists in the database.

This endpoint is accessible to authenticated admins presenting a valid refresh token. Related operations include admin login (/auth/admin/login) and admin registration (/auth/admin/join).
operations.summary: Renew admin JWT tokens via secure token refresh using the shopping_mall_admins table.

requestBody.description: Payload with the refresh token for admin JWT token rotation.

responseBody.description: Newly issued access and refresh tokens for the admin actor.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of shopping mall platform-wide configuration entries from the 'shopping_mall_configurations' table. It enables admin users to search, filter, and manage configuration key-value pairs that govern global system parameters, feature flags, and business constants. The operation supports advanced search by key, status, or description, and returns each configuration's audit metadata for compliance. This endpoint is essential for maintaining dynamic control over system-wide options and business logic without requiring code deployments.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of all shopping mall configuration entries defined in the system.

This operation allows platform administrators to search, filter, and manage global configuration settings that control platform behavior, feature toggles, or critical constants. Each configuration includes a unique key, its value (as string or JSON-serialized data), a descriptive purpose, status (such as active or deprecated), and audit information including creation, update, and deletion timestamps. The endpoint provides advanced filtering and sorting by configuration key, status, and full-text search on the description for efficient system governance.

Security is enforced by restricting access to admin actors only. All results include traceability metadata to support audit requirements, and business logic interprets configuration values according to the specific "config_key". Only platform admins should use this operation; changes to configurations impact system-wide behavior and may affect all actors and business flows.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping mall configuration entries (shopping_mall_configurations table).

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for administrative listing and filtering of configuration entries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of configuration entry summaries matching admin search criteria.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of a specific configuration entry from the 'shopping_mall_configurations' table, identified by its globally unique config_key. Admin users call this endpoint to inspect the current value, status, description, and audit metadata of a given configuration parameter. The operation strictly enforces platform integrity—configuration values govern feature flags and critical system behaviors, and any changes should be reviewed for impact. This endpoint is fundamental for system maintenance, auditing, and feature rollout tracking.
operations.description:
Retrieve the complete details of a specific shopping mall configuration entry by its unique configuration key.

This endpoint allows platform administrators to review the value, status (active, inactive, or deprecated), descriptive purpose, and complete audit trail for any given configuration. Designed for compliance and safe platform operation, the operation ensures only authorized administrators have access, and returns all relevant fields as stored on the platform (including value, key, status, and full audit metadata). This read-only operation is vital for reviewing current configuration in effect before making system changes.

Security is strictly enforced to ensure that only admin users may query sensitive configuration details. System criticality of most keys means changes can impact multiple system modules or business logic, so admins are expected to validate configuration integrity using this endpoint.
operations.summary: Retrieve details for a specific shopping mall configuration entry by unique config_key (shopping_mall_configurations table).

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique configuration key name identifying the target entry (global scope).

responseBody.description: Full configuration entry details for the specified config_key.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation allows a platform administrator to create a new configuration entry for the e-commerce shopping mall platform. The configuration entry is stored in the shopping_mall_configurations table, which manages system-wide key-value parameters, feature flags, or constants required for runtime control of platform features. Each configuration consists of a unique config_key (used for lookup), config_value (can be string or JSON-serialized), a human-readable description explaining the configuration's effect, and a status to enable safe rollout and gradual feature gating. This operation supports the addition of new platform settings by admins, with validation and audit requirements for traceability as described in the corresponding business and requirements documentation.
operations.description:
Create a new system configuration entry for the platform-wide shopping mall backend. This operation enables administrators to register global configuration options—these may include feature toggles, business constants, or other system parameters that must be controlled centrally by admins.

When this endpoint is called, it validates the uniqueness of the config_key field (no two entries can share the same key) and requires all critical fields: config_key, config_value, description, and status, which must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Validation logic checks the non-null/non-empty state of these fields, with config_key uniqueness ensuring there will be no key collision at runtime. Successfully created configuration entries are immediately effective (if status is 'active') and are propagated across platform services on next refresh or polling cycle.

Only authenticated platform administrators can invoke this operation, as the ability to modify system-wide parameters is a sensitive permission. All creation events are logged for audit compliance, and soft deletion will be required for eventual removal as per schema design.
operations.summary: Create a new platform configuration entry in shopping_mall_configurations table.

requestBody.description: A new configuration entry for the shopping mall platform. Requires unique config_key, a serializable config_value, a description, and a status ('active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated').

responseBody.description: Detailed information for the newly created configuration entry, including meta fields and audit timestamps.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation allows a platform administrator to update an existing platform-wide configuration entry identified by its unique config_key. It operates on the shopping_mall_configurations table, enabling controlled modification of configuration values, textual description, and status (i.e., active/inactive/deprecated). Admins use this to safely adjust configuration values, rollout business logic changes, or retire deprecated feature toggles. Audit and soft deletion logic comply with requirements for sensitive administrative actions, ensuring traceability for all updates to platform configuration.
operations.description:
Update an existing configuration entry for the shopping mall platform. This endpoint allows administrators to change the value, description, or status of a specific configuration entry identified by its unique config_key in the database.

For each update operation, the endpoint first resolves the configuration by config_key. The admin can then provide new config_value, an updated description, or set the status among 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. The previous values are preserved by audit logging and updated_at timestamps, per compliance requirements. This endpoint enforces schema validation, including non-null and uniqueness constraints on config_key, and value validation for status.

Only users with administrator privileges can invoke this operation, as configuration settings are critical to platform operation. All changes are logged. If a configuration entry is soft-deleted (marked by deleted_at), updates are rejected to avoid modifying obsolete or legacy settings. Related admin dashboard interfaces may need refresh or polling to present updated values in near real-time.
operations.summary: Update a platform configuration entry in shopping_mall_configurations table by config_key.

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique configuration key name used to identify which platform configuration entry to update (global scope).

requestBody.description: Updated configuration values. Accepts new config_value, updated description, and new status (must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated').

responseBody.description: The updated platform configuration entry, reflecting new values and meta fields.

operations.name: update

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a platform-wide configuration entry from the shopping_mall_configurations table based on its unique config_key. Configurations are crucial system-level parameters, feature flags, and key-value pairs that drive platform logic, toggles, and settings. This API allows admins to clean up deprecated, invalid, or unused configuration keys while maintaining audit and traceability through the deleted_at field.

The operation enforces that only the target configuration entry identified by config_key is affected and marks the entry as deleted (soft deletion) by setting the deleted_at timestamp rather than physically erasing the database row. This supports safe rollbacks, audits, and preserves historical records of effective settings over time. Only highly privileged platform admins can perform this operation.

Care must be taken since configuration changes can impact multiple system modules relying on config_key-value pairs for feature rollouts or critical logic toggles. Downstream services and clients referencing these configurations must have appropriate fallback behaviors in place.
operations.description:
Permanently (via soft-delete) remove a configuration entry by its unique config_key from the platform settings.

This endpoint enables administrators to decommission configuration flags, global constants, or system toggles that are no longer needed. Rather than truly deleting the row from the database, it reliably sets deleted_at, conforming to historical audit and rollback requirements as described in the Prisma schema.

Only users with admin-level authorization can invoke this operation, as changes to the configuration subsystem can have major cross-system effects. Proper authorization and audit trailing are enforced. Attempting to remove a non-existent or already deleted configuration returns a clear error message. Related operations for creating, updating, or listing configuration entries should be used to view or manage the active set.
operations.summary: Soft-delete platform configuration entry in shopping_mall_configurations by config_key.

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique configuration key name of the platform setting to be soft-deleted (global scope).

operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of all product categories for navigation, browsing, and search options. It is based on the shopping_mall_categories table, supporting arbitrarily deep category hierarchies (via parent_id) and enabling admin or merchandiser workflows to review, search, and manage the taxonomy structure.

The result includes active, inactive, and deprecated categories, with filter options for name, status, and parent_id to allow refinement for display or batch management. Complex queries enable understanding category placement, usage, and navigation ordering for catalog or UI-building purposes. Large installations should leverage the status and sort_order indexes for fast retrieval.

This endpoint supports workflow needs for category management, catalog planning, and cross-reference for inventory operations and product assignments. Category browsing is public, but advanced querying and full taxonomy management are available to admins and authorized merchandisers. The result format returns category summaries with pagination metadata for efficient frontend rendering and management.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of product categories and their metadata for navigation, display, and management purposes.

This endpoint supports hierarchical taxonomy exploration, focused category searches (by name, parent, or status), and efficient listing for catalog/admin panel usage. It exposes all key fields—including relationships and status—from the Prisma schema.

The API is designed both for public use (navigation and product browsing) and for admin/merchandiser tooling (advanced querying, batch updates, or audits). Security and rate-limiting considerations should be configured according to usage context. Data returned conforms to the category summary and pagination standards for frontend consumption.
operations.summary: Search and list product categories (shopping_mall_categories) with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

requestBody.description: Filtering, search, sorting, and pagination parameters for category list management or frontend taxonomy exploration.

responseBody.description: Paginated set of category summary records with metadata and navigation fields for the list view.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single shopping mall category by its unique name for reference, navigation, or display. It operates on the shopping_mall_categories table, which maintains a hierarchical taxonomy for product and navigation categories. The endpoint supports deep category trees via a self-referencing parent_id field, and the name parameter must correspond to a unique category, as enforced by the unique constraint in the Prisma schema. This operation is intended for both user interface display (such as category pages and filter menus) and admin panel category lookups.
operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed information of a shopping mall category by its unique name.

This operation allows clients to fetch the complete details for a single product or navigation category within the shopping mall system. Categories are uniquely identified by their name field, which is strictly enforced as unique in the database.

The operation returns all relevant fields for the category, including its full description, parent-child hierarchy (through parent_id), navigation sort order, current status (active/inactive/deprecated), and audit fields for traceability. If the specified category name does not exist, a not found error is returned.

No authentication is required: this endpoint is public and meant for general user/navigation use as well as for integrations needing trusted category lookups. The operation does not require a request body, and only the name parameter in the path.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single shopping mall category by its unique name from shopping_mall_categories table.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Unique category name of the shopping mall category (global scope). Required for locating the specific category. This must match exactly with a unique category name, as enforced by the @@unique([name]) constraint in the database.

responseBody.description: Detailed information of the shopping mall category with its hierarchy, status, and audit fields.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A shopping mall category must be created before it can be retrieved by name. The POST operation ensures the category exists in the database and has a unique name, which is the key for this retrieval operation.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new product or navigation category in the shopping mall by inserting a row into the shopping_mall_categories table. The table supports arbitrarily deep nesting via the parent_id field for hierarchical classification, and enforces a unique constraint on the name for each category. The operation exposes full category management for administrative clients or system integrations, allowing creation of categories for user navigation, search filtering, and cross-service taxonomy.

Required input fields are: name (must be unique), description, sort_order (integer sorting field), status (such as active/inactive/deprecated), and optionally parent_id for nested/child categories. Audit trail fields like created_at and updated_at are managed automatically by the system.
operations.description:
Create a new shopping mall category for products or navigation taxonomy.

This operation enables system administrators or trusted API clients to add new categories to the shopping mall platform. Each category can be a root node (no parent_id) or a child (nested) category for hierarchical navigation, filtering, or presentation. All category names must be unique, as enforced by the @@unique([name]) constraint.

The request body must provide all required category details except system-managed fields (like created_at); the parent_id is optional if the category is a root node. The system will enforce data validity, such as required fields, correct status values, and unique names. Attempting to add a category with a duplicate name will result in an error. The response contains full newly created category details for confirmation and further management.
operations.summary: Create a new product or navigation category in shopping_mall_categories table.

requestBody.description: Full input for creating a new shopping mall category. Includes name (unique), description, sort order, status, and optional parent_id for hierarchy. System managed fields (created_at, updated_at, etc.) are omitted—these are handled automatically.

responseBody.description: Details of the newly created shopping mall category, including its unique id and any system-managed fields set by the database.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing shopping mall category within the product and navigation taxonomy system. The operation targets the 'shopping_mall_categories' table, allowing administrators to modify properties such as description, display order, status, or other business metadata for the category identified by its unique name. The API ensures conformity to unique constraints, hierarchical parent linkage, and manages proper status transitions, including audit trail updates for administrators.
operations.description:
Update properties of a product or navigation category present in the shopping mall's taxonomy. The category is uniquely identified by its 'name' field, enforcing the unique business identifier constraint set in the schema.

This operation is typically used by admins to modify metadata such as the category's description, display order (sort_order), parent category, and activation status (active/inactive/deprecated). Updates to audit trail timestamps (updated_at) are automatically applied upon successful modification.

Permissions: Restricted to admin actors. Attempts to modify immutable fields (such as creation date or soft-deleted status) are rejected. Category names remain globally unique, as enforced by unique index.

The response returns the updated category details. Related endpoints include creation, detail retrieval, category listing, and deactivation operations. The operation maintains system consistency across all usages of categories in browsing, filtering, and referencing flows.
operations.summary: Update an existing mall category in the shopping_mall_categories table.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Unique category name, as seen in UIs and for API reference (global scope).

requestBody.description: Update information for the mall category; only the updatable fields are used (e.g., description, sort_order, status, parent_id).

responseBody.description: Full details of the updated mall category after modification.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation marks a product or navigation category in the shopping_mall_categories table as deactivated (soft delete) by setting its deleted_at timestamp. It uses the unique category 'name' as the identifier. This preserves history and non-destructive data flows for safety, ensuring that related data such as product assignments and hierarchy can be maintained and audited. Admin users are authorized to execute this operation, which places the inactive category logically outside active browsing/filtering without physical record deletion.
operations.description:
Deactivate (soft delete) a category in the shopping mall system by setting its deleted_at field. This operation prevents the deleted category from appearing in standard browsing, filter, and reference flows, maintaining referential data safety and reversibility.

The API is restricted to admin users and requires the unique category name as input. Attempts to deactivate already-deleted or non-existent categories return clear error responses, supporting robust auditability and safety mechanisms.

This operation is essential for stable business logic, ensuring that deactivated (soft deleted) categories are retained in the database for compliance and rollback. Related operations include creating new categories, listing all categories, and restoring/deactivating entities.
operations.summary: Deactivate (soft delete) a mall category identified by unique name in the shopping_mall_categories table.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Unique category name, as seen in UIs and for API reference (global scope).

responseBody.description: Complete details of the category, including deleted_at field set upon deactivation.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of all direct child categories for a given product or navigation category in the shopping mall taxonomy. It operates on the shopping_mall_categories Prisma table. The parent category is uniquely identified by its 'name' (which is unique per the schema). The operation supports searching, filtering, and paginating category children for use in the user interface, merchandising, or admin tools.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of direct child categories under a specific parent category, identified by its unique name.

This operation supports use cases such as building category navigation trees for the shop UI, assisting admins in managing hierarchical category structures, and enabling merchandising workflows that require knowledge of category organization.

The request must include filtering and pagination criteria as defined by IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest. Only categories with parent_id mapped to the specified category 'name' will be included. The response is a paginated list of category summaries, supporting scalable UI rendering and efficient browsing for large category trees.

Note: Only active or admin-visible categories are included unless otherwise specified in the request. Results are sorted by 'sort_order' by default. Security and visibility are enforced based on actor role and API configuration.
operations.summary: List child categories of a specific parent category by unique name (shopping_mall_categories).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Unique category name of the parent category (global scope).

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination parameters for listing category children.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of direct child category summaries under the specified parent category.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of registered external payment providers for the shopping mall checkout and payment flows. It operates on the shopping_mall_external_payment_providers Prisma table, which maintains all external gateways/platforms (e.g., Stripe, Toss, PayPal) available to the platform. Results may be filtered and paginated for admin tools, API consumers, or service UI purposes.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of registered external payment providers, supporting filtering by provider name, integration code, status (active/inactive/deprecated), and business context.

This operation is intended for both administrative configuration dashboards and platform features that expose available payment options to users. It supports advanced query, sort, and search features via IShoppingMallExternalPaymentProvider.IRequest, including keyword and field filters.

The response is a paginated set of payment provider summaries, showing status, display names, integration codes, and additional business notes. Security and business context are enforced at the provider service layer. Only necessary fields are exposed in summaries to protect sensitive integration data.
operations.summary: Paginated, filterable list of external payment providers (shopping_mall_external_payment_providers).

requestBody.description: Filtering, search, and pagination options for retrieving external payment providers.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of external payment provider summaries matching search criteria.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information for a single external payment provider registered in the shopping mall integration registry. It operates on the 'shopping_mall_external_payment_providers' table in the Prisma schema. The operation allows querying by provider_code, which is a unique system integration key for backend mapping and API orchestration. The response includes the display name, status, description, relevant audit timestamps, and soft delete status of the external payment provider. This endpoint is crucial for displaying integration status, troubleshooting payment issues, and supporting admin or system workflows that validate payment integrations.

Key security: This is a read-only endpoint and can be made public or restricted based on platform visibility policy, but typically no sensitive data is exposed through provider metadata. It does not expose any credentials, tokens, or system secrets. For troubleshooting or administrative scenarios, this can be filtered by tracing audit fields such as created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

Validation rules: providerCode must match a registered provider_code as recorded in the Prisma schema. If the code is not found, the response should indicate a not-found or business error based on platform conventions. This endpoint is commonly used in dashboards and operational diagnostics.
operations.summary: Get external payment provider details by providerCode (shopping_mall_external_payment_providers)
operations.description:
Retrieve complete metadata for a specific external payment provider using its system integration key (providerCode). This includes the display name, unique code, status (active/inactive/deprecated), legal and integration notes, timestamps for audit, and soft-delete status based on the 'shopping_mall_external_payment_providers' schema.

This operation is useful for administrative dashboards, diagnostics, integration status checks, and for enabling or disabling payment options in the commerce UI. Security context depends on platform policy—some platforms may expose this information publicly for informational purposes, while others may require authentication. This operation removes a specific session record for a customer, effectively logging them out of the given session on all platforms (web, mobile, etc.). It operates on the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table, which maintains authenticated login record for each customer. Hard deletion (non-reversible) is enforced by policy, as there is no soft delete column in the schema. Both the sessionId and owning customerId are required in the path for precise targeting and access control.

This action is permitted only for the session owner (the customer) or authorized admin actors. When invoked, it terminates the targeted session, revokes any related JWT tokens, and deletes the session record for compliance. The operation does not create, update, or issue authentication tokens—it is solely for invalidating/removing existing records. Attempts to remove sessions belonging to other customers, or sessions that do not exist, are denied. There is no recovery for deleted sessions; all audit and compliance logic should use immutable logs defined elsewhere.

Relationship and referential integrity between shopping_mall_customers and shopping_mall_customer_sessions are strictly enforced as per the Prisma schema. Any related business events, such as customer-initiated logout or security response, may utilize this endpoint. No session metadata is returned on successful deletion.
operations.description:
Delete or revoke a session record for a specific customer, thereby invalidating their login session for that device, browser, or context. 

This operation is commonly used for customer-initiated logout (e.g., from account settings or security center), as well as by admin actors enforcing security policy or handling fraudulent activity. It permanently removes the session record from the system, with no recovery capability. The deletion is strictly limited to the session's owner or an administrator; unauthorized attempts are rejected and logged. 

Notes: This operation NEVER issues or refreshes authentication tokens; it strictly removes session records as defined in the session table. Associated events (such as removing active JWT tokens) should be handled by the authorization infrastructure, not the API itself. The operation is compliant with current data retention and security requirements specified by the business and schema.
operations.summary: Delete a specific customer session from shopping_mall_customer_sessions (hard delete only).

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target customer who owns the session.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the session to be deleted from the customer's records.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of address records belonging to a specific customer. It is based on the shopping_mall_addresses table, which consists of structured address data for shipping, billing, and other purposes. The primary use is for customers to view their saved addresses, but this can also be managed by admins. The operation is designed to support advanced filtering, searching, sorting, and pagination, as required for address book management features in customer account dashboards. The parent entity is shopping_mall_customers, and the operation leverages a path parameter to restrict the result to the addresses of a single customer. All constraints from the Prisma schema, such as a maximum of 10 addresses per customer and required relationships, are respected.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of address records for a specific customer.

This endpoint is accessible to authenticated customers (for their own addresses) and admins (for platform oversight). The operation enables customers to view all of their stored addresses (up to the business maximum of 10). Query capabilities allow for search by name, city, or status, and results are paginated for efficient display in user interfaces. Security and ownership checks ensure that only the owner/customer or platform admins may access this data.

Returned records cover all structured address fields, including recipient name, full address breakdown, contact phone, whether it is the default, and address creation time. Results conform to the business schema, omitting fields that do not exist in shopping_mall_addresses (such as deleted_at). Error conditions include access violation if an actor requests another customer's addresses without admin privileges.

Related operations include address retrieval and modification (GET, PUT, DELETE /customers/{customerId}/addresses/{addressId}), which allow management of individual address entries. This operation only lists the current user's addresses, never those of sellers or other actors.
operations.summary: List all addresses belonging to a given customer, paginated and filterable (from shopping_mall_addresses).

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target customer whose addresses will be listed.

requestBody.description: Search, filtering, and pagination parameters for querying the address list of a specific customer.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shopping mall addresses matching the query parameters, including all structured address fields required for display.

It operates on the shopping_mall_addresses table and is intended for account management features, such as viewing or editing address entries during checkout or in a user profile. The operation uses two path parameters: customerId (UUID of the parent account) and addressId (UUID of the target address).

The endpoint ensures strong ownership validation, permitting only the account owner (customer) or a platform admin to access the specific address. It returns all structured fields: recipient name, address breakdown, contact phone, default address flag, and timestamps. The operation respects the business logic of address linkage—each address must belong to the specified customer (not to sellers or other actors)—and enforces the maximum-per-customer as required in business requirements.

The returned data covers full address structure in line with schema guidelines, ensuring only user-manageable data is present. This is commonly used for editing addresses in personal profile sections and for reviewing address details prior to order checkout.

If an address does not belong to the given customer, or the actor lacks sufficient permissions, an authorization error is triggered. Related endpoints include the paginated address list and update/delete operations for the same resource.

This operation updates an existing SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) variant belonging to a specific product in the shopping mall catalog. It is associated with the 'shopping_mall_product_skus' Prisma table, which defines SKU variants for catalog products. Each SKU record holds unique inventory, price, status, and referencing its parent product. The SKU is uniquely identified within a product's scope via the composite key of product ID and sku_code. A SKU can only be updated if it exists and the parent product ID matches; all relevant audit and workflow fields are handled. Changes to price, stock, status, and code can be performed through this endpoint.

SKU update requires authenticated seller permission, as only a product's owner can modify its variants. Data validation includes status rules (e.g., cannot update to invalid business status), inventory/price integrity, and prevents updates to SKUs of deleted or archived products. This operation builds on the relationship to the parent product in 'shopping_mall_products', ensuring SKU and product linkage. The specification aligns with Prisma field comments and best practices for catalog variant management.

It ensures that SKUs cannot be updated independently of their associated product, maintaining data consistency. All input is validated against allowed status values and business rules for inventory and pricing as defined in the schema.

This endpoint implements full auditability, tracking who updated the SKU and when, via the updated_at timestamp. Only sellers who own the product may perform updates, and business logic will prevent updates to SKUs that have been deleted or whose parent product is no longer active. Appropriate error responses are returned for access violation or nonexistent SKU/product references.

Use this endpoint to efficiently manage catalog variants without disrupting historical sale or review data. For bulk updates, use corresponding batch management tools or endpoints. Related operations: SKU creation, product updates, and product detail retrieval.

operations.specification:
This operation deletes an existing SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) variant belonging to a specific product in the shopping mall catalog. It acts on the 'shopping_mall_product_skus' Prisma table, leveraging its soft delete support for recovery and moderation workflows. The SKU is uniquely identified within the context of a parent product via the SKU's own ID and its parent product's ID, ensuring multi-tenant catalog isolation for sellers. SKUs are archived (soft deleted) rather than physically removed, preserving audit trails—which is compliant with the schema's 'deleted_at' soft delete marker field. Referential integrity is maintained with the parent product entry in the 'shopping_mall_products' table.

SKU deletion is restricted to authenticated sellers who own the parent product. The operation validates the existence of both product and SKU, confirms seller authority, checks SKU status to prevent deletion of non-removable variants (e.g., already deleted or locked), and updates the deleted_at timestamp. Related inventory, review, and order references are retained for historical and business intelligence purposes. This specification aligns with comments and validation in the Prisma schema.
operations.description:
Soft delete a SKU variant associated with a given shopping mall product. Rather than permanently removing SKU records from the database, this operation sets the 'deleted_at' field, marking the SKU as archived. This ensures traceability and enables SKU recovery for moderation, review, and data analytics.

Only the authenticated seller who owns the product may perform this action. The API will validate references to both the parent product and the target SKU to ensure they exist and the user has authorization. SKUs already marked as deleted or belonging to deleted/archived products cannot be deleted again and result in appropriate errors.

This operation is foundational for catalog management, particularly when adjusting available variants without losing business intelligence or jeopardizing order/review consistency. Use corresponding endpoints for listing or restoring SKUs as part of seller workflows. Related operations: SKU update, product detail retrieval, and recovery endpoints.

Upon receiving this request, the system validates the parent product and SKU exist, both are active, and that image attachment is allowed. Field-level validation is enforced for `cdn_uri` (must be a valid URI), display position (unique among all images for the SKU), optional alt text (for accessibility), and optional label for admin management. operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a specific product attribute from a given product in the shopping mall catalog. It operates on the shopping_mall_product_attributes table, which defines attribute types (such as color, size, material) that allow sellers to construct product variants under a catalog product. The operation is designed for cases when a seller or admin needs to remove an attribute from a product, for instance, stopping support for a particular variant option.

Removing a product attribute is only allowed if doing so will not break data integrity. If there are dependent SKUs or attribute value mappings that reference this attribute, those must be handled according to business policies before permanent deletion. The operation is soft-delete enabled: setting the attribute's deleted_at field instead of hard removal to support undo and moderation workflows, as documented by the schema. Proper authorization is required; normally, sellers can only update their own catalog, while admins may remove any attribute as part of catalog housekeeping or moderation.
operations.description:
Remove a product attribute (such as color, size, or material) from the attribute list available for constructing SKUs under a specific product.

This operation performs a soft delete by updating the deleted_at field for the given attribute record, so attribute removals may be recovered or moderated later. Sellers are allowed to remove their own product's attributes if none of the SKUs depend on the attribute, while admins can override this policy for platform data hygiene or moderation. Permission validation ensures that only the owning seller or authorized admin can invoke this endpoint.

Before actual deletion, the system checks for dependent attribute values or related SKUs that may be affected, blocking the operation and returning an error if active dependencies exist. Audit logs should track both successful and failed delete attempts for compliance and traceability purposes.

This endpoint works alongside the attribute creation, product editing, and SKU variant update APIs, and should be referenced when managing product catalog evolution or cleaning up catalog data.

The operation supports advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination to help administrators or system users query wishlists efficiently across different customers or creation times.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated, filterable list of shopping mall wishlists (shopping_mall_wishlists table).
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of all customer wishlists in the system.

This operation is intended for administrative or reporting features where a platform user (typically an admin) needs to review wishlists held by customers. It supports advanced filtering based on creation time, customer ID, or other business-defined criteria, as well as pagination and sorting options for large data sets.

The results respect the structure and constraints of the shopping_mall_wishlists table, returning only basic wishlist information. Sensitive data is excluded to preserve customer privacy unless higher privileges are granted. When used with other endpoints, this operation supports data-level audit, customer behavior analytics, and reporting on product interest trends.

operations.summary: Retrieve all detailed information of a single shopping mall wishlist (shopping_mall_wishlists table) by ID.
operations.description:
Retrieve all available details for one specific customer wishlist by its unique identifier.

This operation is intended for administrative users or backend systems requiring in-depth review of a customer's wishlist for troubleshooting, analysis, or support. The wishlistId path parameter corresponds to the primary key (UUID) for the shopping_mall_wishlists table. Related records (such as the owning customer and wishlist items) may be retrievable through composed or subsidiary endpoints, but this response focuses on the main wishlist entity only.

Security is crucial, as this endpoint usually contains sensitive customer interest data, so access should be restricted to users with administrative privileges. This operation is typically used in conjunction with the list/search endpoint to investigate or manage specific customer records.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new shopping mall wishlist for a customer. The operation is designed to instantiate a persistent product interest list, associating it to a single customer. It operates on the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table, which limits one wishlist per customer for a consistent and simple user experience. Upon creation, this entity may persist across user sessions and devices and is used for tracking products of interest for later consideration.
operations.description:
Create a new wishlist for a customer in the shopping mall platform.

This API operation is essential for persistent customer product interest tracking across sessions and devices. A wishlist acts as the root entity for a customer's saved items. Each wishlist is associated with a single customer by design, and per the schema, only one such list can exist for any given customer (enforced by a unique index on the `shopping_mall_customer_id` field). Duplicate creation requests should be handled gracefully, either by returning the existing wishlist or providing an appropriate error response.

Upon creation, metadata such as `created_at` and `updated_at` are automatically registered. Ownership is linked to the customer initiating the request, and the wishlist will later serve as the parent entity for subsidiary wishlist items representing concrete products or SKUs the customer is interested in.

Security: This endpoint must ensure the customer is authenticated and has not already created a wishlist. If a wishlist already exists for a customer, a clear error or existing wishlist reference should be returned. Sensitive to privacy and consistency, only the owner should be able to create their own wishlist.
operations.summary: Create a new customer wishlist (shopping_mall_wishlists)

responseBody.description: The newly created wishlist entity for the customer.

It targets the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and allows customers to modify updatable metadata (such as timestamps), but not to change its ownership or the underlying structure. Modifications are typically limited to non-relational attributes, as items are managed through a separate operation on the wishlist items entity.
operations.description:
Update a customer's wishlist in the shopping mall system.

This API operation allows modification of a customer's existing wishlist record. According to the schema, only certain fields (such as metadata fields) are likely updatable—relationships and the wishlist's owner must be immutable. The method targets lists identified by the `wishlistId` path parameter, which uniquely references the wishlist to be updated.

Ownership and authorization checks must ensure that only the authenticated customer can update their own wishlist. Data integrity is preserved by restricting changes to valid wishlist entities and not permitting reassignment of customer ownership or manipulation of subsidiary list items, which are managed in a separate domain (wishlist items).

Related operations may include list item management (adding/removing products) and wishlist deletion (if supported).
