operations.specification: Permanently removes a customer's wishlist entity and all its associated wishlist items from the shopping mall platform. Directly operates on the shopping_mall_wishlists table, which represents a persistent aggregation of product interest for a customer. This operation ensures the complete deletion of the wishlist root and subsidiary records, preventing orphaned wishlist items. The user invoking this action must own the wishlist or have appropriate privileges, and after deletion, any saved SKUs in the wishlist become inaccessible. All subsidiary shopping_mall_wishlist_items belonging to the wishlist are automatically cascaded and deleted from the database. No soft delete is performed—records are irreversibly removed.
operations.description:
Execute the removal of a customer's wishlist from the database, along with every item it contains. 

Once this operation is invoked, the root wishlist (shopping_mall_wishlists) and all of its subsidiary wishlist items (shopping_mall_wishlist_items) are deleted in a single transaction. This ensures there are no orphaned records, maintaining referential integrity. 

Only the owner of the wishlist or an administrator may invoke this endpoint, as the wishlist is considered sensitive, persistent state for the user. The operation checks ownership based on the authenticated user's ID. If an unauthorized user attempts to erase a wishlist, the system will deny the request and return an error response. 

This behavior is irreversible, and all shopping-mall product SKUs referenced in the wishlist will simply become untracked for the customer. There is no recovery possible after deletion. Related API endpoints include wishlist item management (add/update/remove items) and viewing wishlists for the current user.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a customer's wishlist and all its items in shopping_mall_wishlists.

parameters.name: wishlistId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist to be deleted.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of all items within a customer's wishlist as stored in the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table, scoped to a particular wishlist. This operation enables customers to view and manage their saved product SKUs (not currently in their cart) for future purchase consideration. The feature is implemented by joining the wishlists table with its subsidiary wishlist_items, allowing rich filtering by SKU, product, or category, and supporting pagination and sorting. Only accessible to the wishlist owner or an administrator.
operations.description:
Fetch the complete contents of a given wishlist in a paginated, searchable fashion, leveraging the shopping_mall_wishlist_items subsidiary table. 

Customers may use this endpoint to view all saved SKUs across devices or sessions, and may filter items by product details, SKU characteristics, or category. Supports pagination (page/limit), keyword search, and sorting (e.g., most recently added first). 

Security checks ensure that only the authenticated owner or an administrator can access wishlist details for privacy. Attempts by unauthorized users are refused. This operation is commonly used as the initial step in displaying a user's wishlist before options to move items to cart or remove from wishlist. 

Related operations include adding/removing wishlist items, wishlists root retrieval, and SKU/product detail fetches.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of wishlist items for a specific wishlist (shopping_mall_wishlist_items).

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific item within a customer's wishlist. It is associated with the 'shopping_mall_wishlist_items' table, which records each SKU a customer has marked for later consideration. The operation allows users to view information for an individual wishlist item, such as the product SKU reference and timestamps, by specifying the wishlist and the item. This enables the frontend to display extended details about a saved product, support item management features, and tie wishlist visualizations to database records accurately.
operations.description:
Retrieve information for a single item within a customer wishlist using specified wishlist and item identifiers.

This endpoint is essential for enabling customers to see details about a particular product they have saved to their wishlist. Since each wishlist item references a SKU and is tied to a parent wishlist, this operation utilizes both the parent wishlist and the specific item ID to ensure precise retrieval and access control.

Relationship to schema: The 'shopping_mall_wishlist_items' table enforces a composite unique constraint pairing wishlist and SKU, preventing duplicates. Security is enforced by ownership at the application level: customers can only retrieve items from their own wishlist. If an item does not exist or belongs to another customer's wishlist, an appropriate error is returned. The response structure mirrors the 'IShoppingMallWishlistItem' type.

Related operations include retrieving all items in a wishlist, adding/removing wishlist items, and listing products available for addition. For detailed item info, this endpoint covers the primary use case for managing persistent customer interest lists.
operations.summary: Get details of a specific shopping mall wishlist item for a given wishlist (shopping_mall_wishlist_items table).

It is used for adding a product SKU that the customer wants to save for future consideration. The endpoint requires the wishlist context (typically tied to the customer) and the data for the new wishlist item (such as the referenced SKU). Duplicate SKUs within a single wishlist are prevented by a composite unique constraint on the table. The operation ensures correct linkage between the wishlist and SKU, supports later transitions to cart, and provides a seamless interface for wishlist management features.
operations.description:
Add a product to a customer's wishlist by creating a new wishlist item under the specified wishlist.

This operation enables authenticated customers to persist product interest for later purchase decisions by adding a SKU to their wishlist. The wishlist ID specifies the parent wishlist context (which must belong to the authenticated customer). The operation validates that the SKU is not already in the wishlist (enforced by the composite unique constraint) and that both the wishlist and SKU exist. On success, the new wishlist item is returned with all relevant database fields and references. Security is enforced so that a customer cannot add items to another customer's wishlist. Upon duplication (e.g., SKU already present), an error is returned according to business logic.

This endpoint integrates with the 'shopping_mall_wishlists' and 'shopping_mall_wishlist_items' schemas, supports advanced wishlist interaction features, and is fundamental for persistent ecommerce bookmarking.

operations.specification: This operation updates an individual wishlist item that is attached to a customer's wishlist, operating on the shopping_mall_wishlist_items Prisma table. It allows modification of properties of a single item within a wishlist, such as the referenced product SKU, if the business requirements allow (usually this is limited in practice; see core comment below). The operation requires both the parent wishlist ID and the target item ID to correctly address the item to update, respecting the composite unique constraint (shopping_mall_wishlist_id, shopping_mall_product_sku_id) for proper linkage and disambiguation. The request body should contain all updatable fields as defined in the IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IUpdate DTO, and the response will return the updated IShoppingMallWishlistItem DTO object. Designed for scenarios where customers want to adjust product SKUs or related metadata in their wishlist, if such updates are allowed by requirements.
operations.description:
Update the details of a specific wishlist item in a customer's wishlist.

This operation enables modifications to a wishlist item—such as changing the referenced product SKU, if allowed—by identifying the target using both the parent wishlist's ID and the item's own ID. The operation strictly enforces correct linkage to ensure updates only affect the intended wishlist and item pair, leveraging the relationship between shopping_mall_wishlists (parent) and shopping_mall_wishlist_items (subsidiary), as detailed in the Prisma schema.

Security is enforced so that only the owning customer, authenticated and authorized, may update their wishlist items. Attempts to update a wishlist item with an ID not owned by the customer will result in an authorization error. Validation includes ensuring referenced SKUs exist and are not duplicated within a single wishlist, as per the composite unique constraint. The operation returns the fully updated wishlist item object.

Related operations include: removing an item from the wishlist (DELETE /wishlists/{wishlistId}/items/{itemId}) and adding a new item to a wishlist (typically POST /wishlists/{wishlistId}/items). Error responses cover not found, unauthorized, and business rule violations regarding SKU duplication or non-existent products.

The composite reference to both the wishlist and the item ID ensures correct and safe removal of only the targeted record. When a customer removes an item from their wishlist, it is deleted from persistent storage, and will no longer be visible or accessible within the wishlist. This operation enforces strict authorization rules to ensure that only the owning customer may remove items from their own wishlist.
operations.description:
Remove (delete) a specific item from a customer's wishlist.

This operation allows authenticated customers to permanently delete a wishlist item by specifying both the wishlist's ID and the item ID, ensuring that only an item truly belonging to the user's wishlist can be deleted. The relationship between shopping_mall_wishlists and shopping_mall_wishlist_items, as described in the Prisma schema, is enforced so an orphan or incorrectly referenced removal cannot occur.

Security and authorization checks prevent customers from deleting wishlist items they do not own. Attempts to delete a non-existent item or an item not associated with the given wishlist result in appropriate error responses. Additionally, this endpoint is typically paired with operations for updating (PUT) and creating (POST) wishlist items, enabling a complete management lifecycle. Upon successful deletion, the item is permanently removed and cannot be recovered.

It operates on the shopping_mall_orders Prisma DB table, supporting advanced search and sort features for business order management, customer support flows, and order analytics. Clients can specify multiple search criteria including order number, customer reference, seller, status, date ranges, and platform-wide or seller-specific filters. Full page-wise navigation is supported, and response structure is optimized for management dashboards and operational reporting.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of all orders submitted on the platform.

This operation exposes robust search and filter capabilities to allow administrators or authorized users to efficiently locate orders by multiple criteria, including order number, customer, status, date placed, and the responsible seller. It is ideal for order management systems, customer support back offices, and analytical query panels that require dynamic querying, sorting, and operational batch processing.

Security considerations: Only users with proper access may retrieve full order lists with all details. Depending on the requirements and implementation, sensitive details may be filtered or restricted at the DTO level for certain actors. Related operations include detailed order retrieval and item listing for individual orders by order number.

Validation logic ensures that page searches include well-formed query inputs (such as ISO 8601 datetimes, correct status values, and optional seller/customer codes). In case of input errors or excessive result count, the system should provide appropriate error messages and guidance on filter restrictions.

Supporting external customer use-cases and internal administrative management, the operation provides comprehensive detail including status, timestamps, references to the customer and seller, and all associated item and shipment breakdowns, subject to field-level access controls.
operations.description:
Fetches the complete details for a specific order identified by its globally unique business order number.

This endpoint is used for both customer and back office contexts requiring a deep dive into an order's financial, fulfillment, and status details. Data returned includes all order metadata, primary references to customer, seller, address, and summarized item breakdowns. The order number parameter uniquely identifies the target order across the entire platform, as enforced by the database unique constraint.

Appropriate access controls and audit logging must be in place to track access and prevent unauthorized information disclosure. Related endpoints include order search and order item operations for per-item details and workflow processing. Input validation ensures that the order number follows the correct business format and refers to an existing, non-deleted order. Error handling provides clear messages for missing/invalid references or restricted information access.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new order record in the shopping mall platform. It targets the shopping_mall_orders table, a primary lifecycle entity capturing all essential details of purchases made on the platform. The operation requires well-structured input, referencing the customer, delivery address, seller, and including all necessary high-level order details. The order_number must be a unique business identifier (e.g., ORD202500001) and will be strictly validated against existing records to ensure platform-wide uniqueness. Relationships to customer, address, and seller are set via their respective UUIDs. Initial status, currency, total amount, and necessary temporal fields must be provided. Soft deletion and audit trails are managed via created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields, but deleted_at is not required at creation. Business logic enforces that referenced foreign keys exist, and the total_amount is a non-negative value matching the sum of related order items. After creation, the order will act as the anchor for additional items, shipments, and audit log records.
operations.description:
Create a new shopping mall order on the platform.

This operation enables customers (or system actors on their behalf) to place a new order for one or more products, referencing a specific customer, shipping address, and seller. The endpoint requires all business-critical identifiers to be specified, including the unique order_number, and ensures all relationships (such as customer and address) are valid and active.

Before an order can be created, the provided order_number will be validated to ensure global uniqueness. The platform will also check that the referenced customer, address, and seller exist and are eligible for ordering. The total_amount must reflect the sum of all itemized values plus shipping and discounts, and currency codes must comply with ISO 4217 standards. On success, the API returns the complete order details, including status and creation timestamps.

Initial order status is set as provided by the client, and further status changes (cancelled, paid, shipped, etc.) are tracked by separate endpoints and event records. This creation endpoint does not handle order item creation, payment authorization, or shipment initiation, which are handled in subsequent workflow operations. The created order will be visible in customer and admin dashboards for order management and fulfillment.
operations.summary: Create a new order record in shopping_mall_orders.

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing order entity in the shopping_mall_orders table by its globally unique business order_number, allowing modification of key high-level order fields. Updates are typically required for changes in status, address, or other customer-service-driven adjustments. The operation enforces strict validation on order_number uniqueness according to business and database rules. The target order is looked up using the provided order_number, not the technical UUID. Only orders that have not been deleted (deleted_at is null) are eligible for updates. Modifiable fields include status, address, seller references, and non-finalized amounts. The operation does not update child order items or audit logs, which are managed by related endpoints. All updates trigger automatic timestamp and audit trail entries for compliance and tracking purposes.
operations.description:
Update the details of an existing shopping mall order identified by its business-unique order_number.

This endpoint enables authorized actors, such as customers (up to certain business-imposed rules) or customer service agents, to adjust certain fields of an order. Typical modifications may include changing the delivery address (before shipment), correcting order status, updating the assigned seller, or modifying the total_amount and currency if no payment has yet been finalized.

The provided order_number is enforced as a globally unique identifier for lookup. If no active (non-deleted) order matching the order_number exists, the update is rejected. The update does not allow changes to the business order_number itself, nor to any associated child entities (such as order items, shipments, audit logs). Security logic ensures only eligible users (such as the original purchaser or an admin) may make updates. All changes will be tracked for audit and compliance, with updated_at reflecting the modification time.
operations.summary: Update an order in shopping_mall_orders by order_number.

parameters.description: Platform-wide unique business order number for the order to update (global scope).

requestBody.description: Order fields that can be updated, including status, seller, address, and other high-level order fields as allowed by business rules.

responseBody.description: The updated order entity reflecting the post-update state of all high-level order fields.

operations.name: update

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a shopping mall order from the system. It operates on the shopping_mall_orders table, using the 'order_number' field—which is globally unique per order—as its primary business identifier. This endpoint supports order deletion for cases such as error correction, test data clean-up, or critical administrative actions. The operation enforces hard deletion by removing the record from the database, with verification that the supplied orderNumber matches an existing entry. This operation should only be accessible to administrative actors—order removal by standard users is strictly prohibited for compliance and audit reasons.

This operation's permissions are scoped for sensitive administrative intervention given the potential impact on financial records and audit trails. It is tightly coupled with the integrity of the business process, ensuring that dependent records (e.g., order items, audit logs, shipments, and refunds) are validated before allowing removal, in accordance with business rules. Soft deletion is implemented via the deleted_at field, and the operation updates this timestamp to mark the order as deleted, instead of physically removing the row.

Related operations include order detail retrieval and order item list access, which should be invoked to validate data dependencies prior to invoking deletion. Thorough error handling is implemented for missing, already deleted, or dependent-locked orders.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a shopping mall order by its unique business order number.

This API is designed for use by administrators and auditors. It ensures that the specified order has no critical dependencies that would block deletion, such as active shipments or unresolved payments. The order deletion logic is implemented as a soft delete by updating the deleted_at field, indicating the order is no longer active in the system, but retaining the record for compliance purposes.

Security and audit standards are enforced on this operation, including event logging and restricted access. If the order is already deleted or cannot be found, the operation will fail with an appropriate error message. Pre-execution of order item and attachment list retrieval is recommended before performing deletion to ensure no business locks are in place.

All related tables—including order items, shipments, and logs—are checked before deletion to avoid broken references. Only actors with administrative privileges should be granted this capability. All deletion events are auditable, and the deleted order is excluded from all future business workflows.
operations.summary: Soft delete a shopping mall order by its unique business order number (shopping_mall_orders table)

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Platform-unique business order number identifying the target order (global scope)

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated and filterable list of items associated with a particular shopping mall order. It operates on the shopping_mall_order_items table, filtered by the unique order_number of the parent shopping mall order (shopping_mall_orders). The endpoint supports advanced filtering, pagination, and summary data for all SKUs included in an order. Item-level inventory, delivery, refund, and product/SKU information can all be retrieved in a consolidated view for customer service, fulfillment review, and analytics workflows.

The operation expects a valid orderNumber as a path parameter, ensuring that the list returned is specific to a single order. It supports complex searches over item fields such as SKU, quantity, price, status (delivered/refunded), and more. Filtering and sorting are supported in the request body, and the output is paginated for performance and usability. Relationship to the parent order is enforced by backend join/validation logic. The pagination and query request structure adheres to platform list/search conventions.

Error handling includes validation of order existence, appropriate authorization, and empty result sets if the order has no items or does not exist. Standard response and access patterns are used.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, searchable list of all items for a specified order using its unique business order number.

This endpoint is particularly useful for customer support, order fulfillment, financial reconciliation, and analytics. It allows querying order items based on multiple criteria—including SKU, quantity, price, delivery, and refund status—enabling refined and efficient item-level reporting.

The operation only returns items belonging to the order specified by orderNumber and will validate both the existence and the logical status (not deleted) of the parent order. If the order is not found or has been deleted, an error is returned. All item records provided conform to the IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary DTO format for consistency with frontend rendering and business logic needs. Only administrative users may access this detailed item list for compliance and privacy reasons.
operations.summary: Search and paginate items belonging to a specific shopping mall order (shopping_mall_order_items table)

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Platform-unique business order number identifying the parent order (global scope)

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria for order items attached to the specified order. Supports filtering by SKU, status, price, and other fields as defined in the summary DTO.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary list of items for the order, conforming to IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a specific item from a shopping mall order by order number and item UUID. It is associated with the shopping_mall_order_items table, which represents each per-SKU, per-product item within an order. This endpoint allows an external or internal actor to fetch detailed item-level information, including quantity, SKU reference, fulfillment and refund status, pricing at purchase time, and other item attributes. The operation requires both a business order number (globally unique per order) and the item's unique UUID within the order to identify the precise item and ensure there is no ambiguity.

Path parameters strictly comply with the composite context: orderNumber (business order number, globally unique, from shopping_mall_orders) and orderItemId (UUID for order item from shopping_mall_order_items). operations.specification:
This operation creates a new item within an existing order, as managed through the shopping_mall_order_items table. It supports the addition of a new per-SKU, per-product entry into an order, allowing correct breakdown and normalization for inventory, fulfillment, and subsequent processing. To associate correctly with the intended order, the order is referenced by its business order number (orderNumber), ensuring alignment with order context and proper linkage from external or integration systems.

Input data must conform to the IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate DTO, providing all required fields for product selection, SKU, pricing at purchase, and initial fulfillment/refund states. Validation logic must verify parent order existence, that the product/SKU is valid and active, and that inventory levels are sufficient for the requested quantity. If any invariant is not satisfied, a descriptive error is returned. Upon success, the operation creates the new order item and returns full detail as in IShoppingMallOrderItem (including all item and linkage fields).

This operation must enforce strict authorization: only users with a legitimate interest in the order (customer, authorized seller, or admins) are permitted to add items. Typical flows include order amendment prior to checkout/payment or admin-driven adjustments. Redundant or conflicting item entries should be prevented per unique constraints applied at the schema layer.

The request body must follow IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate—defining product/SKU to be added, purchase quantity, price, and any other required detail as defined by the shopping_mall_order_items model.

To maintain business and data integrity, the system must ensure the target order exists, the product and SKU are valid, and inventory constraints are enforced. Only actors who own the order, are fulfilling it, or are authorized as platform admins may perform this operation. Response returns the detailed newly-created order item. If uniqueness or business rules are violated (e.g., duplicate SKU for order), operation must fail with a suitable error and not modify any data.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new product review in the shopping_mall_reviews table for a product the customer has purchased through an order item/SKU. The request must provide all mandatory fields for a valid review, including references to the customer, session, product, SKU, the purchased order item, as well as content fields like rating association, title, and body text. The endpoint enforces validation rules such as purchase verification, minimum/maximum body length, and rating presence, and sets initial moderation/draft status. This operation is central to user-generated content capture and robust product feedback workflows.
operations.description:
Create a new product review for a purchased product SKU via this endpoint. The request must specify the customer, session, product, SKU, related order and order item (to ensure the reviewer actually purchased the product), associated product rating, and all review content fields (title, body). Status fields (is_draft, moderation_status, withdrawn_at) will be set based on default values and business validation.

The endpoint enforces that the customer matches a valid, completed purchase of the SKU and order item and that the same order item can only be reviewed once (uniqueness constraint). Validation covers mandatory content, body length (min 10, max 1000 characters), moderation business rules, and security for session and customer identity. On successful creation, the full review record is returned including all system/populated fields.

Error scenarios are communicated for invalid purchase, duplicate review, moderation rejection, or request body violations. This endpoint references the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma schema and is integral to authentic customer feedback and platform transparency controls.
operations.summary: Create a new review entry in shopping_mall_reviews for a purchased product/order item.

requestBody.description: Information necessary to create a new product review, including customer, session, product, SKU, order/item, rating, and content fields.

responseBody.description: The complete created review record with all populated and assigned fields.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing shopping mall product review identified by its unique review ID. The operation is based on the shopping_mall_reviews table, which holds product reviews submitted by verified customers, linked to specific order items and SKUs. The update can modify summary (title), body, draft/publish state, moderation status, withdrawal information, or related moderation fields. Review updates are subject to business rules governing edit periods, moderation status changes, and traceability for audit and abuse prevention. All modifications are recorded with full traceability, reflecting the latest updated_at timestamp and maintaining compliance with review and moderation policies.
operations.description:
This API endpoint allows updating of a product review in the shopping mall platform, targeted by its unique identifier. The endpoint supports modifications to core review fields such as the title (summary), body text, draft status, and moderation information. Only actual customers who purchased the product can update their reviews, and all changes must comply with minimum/maximum content length, moderation policy, and withdrawal rules.

Security is enforced—users can only edit reviews they have authored and only within the allowed edit window, except for moderation changes by platform staff. All changes are tracked in the audit log with full traceability (via updated_at and session/customer IDs). Review updates may enter the moderation queue if required, and review status transitions must follow business-defined state machines (e.g., draft → published → withdrawn or pending moderation, etc.).

This operation references the shopping_mall_reviews schema, respecting the integrity of foreign keys to customer, session, order item, product, SKU, and rating. Related fields not supplied in the request remain unchanged. Error handling covers invalid states, forbidden access, and periods where no modifications are allowed.
operations.summary: Update a product review (shopping_mall_reviews) by reviewId with new data.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product review to update.

requestBody.description: Fields of the review to update, such as title, body, is_draft, withdrawn_at, moderation_status, or moderation_reason.

responseBody.description: The updated product review entity.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes (or soft deletes depending on business logic) a shopping mall product review identified by reviewId, acting on the shopping_mall_reviews table. Product reviews are centrally important for feedback and moderation in the platform. The operation ensures that removal is correctly handled according to system policies: either setting deleted_at (soft delete), marking as withdrawn (user-initiated removal), or permanent record removal (if allowed and compliant). Only authorized customers (authors within conditions) or platform administrators may erase a review, and all removals are logged for audit/compliance.
operations.description:
This API endpoint removes a specific product review from the platform database, based on its unique reviewId. Depending on the business and moderation rules, this may entail soft-deleting the review (setting deleted_at or withdrawn_at), or permanent physical deletion if platform policy allows it. The response confirms removal by returning the deleted entity for compliance and API contract.

Security rules strictly enforce access: only the original review author (customer) within the review edit/removal period, or a privileged platform administrator or moderator, may delete reviews. All delete operations are logged for traceability, including the session, customer, and moderation context. Relationships to the review's associated product, SKU, order item, and rating are respected, and orphaned entities are prevented by foreign key enforcement.

This operation ensures compliance with shopping_mall_reviews business rules, with error handling for invalid access, not found, forbidden state, or non-removable reviews (due to moderation freeze, dispute, or time window expiration).
operations.summary: Delete (erase or soft delete) a product review (shopping_mall_reviews) by reviewId.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product review to delete.

responseBody.description: The deleted product review entity (for compliance tracing).

operations.specification:
This operation provides a filtered and paginated list of seller responses to a specific product review submitted by a customer. It reads from the shopping_mall_review_responses table, which stores seller replies directly linked to individual customer reviews in shopping_mall_reviews. Each response is uniquely linked to one review (one-to-one relation via shopping_mall_review_id) and includes fields such as body, moderation status, withdrawn_at, created_at, and updated_at. Advanced search, filtering, pagination, and sorting must be supported through the request body (IShoppingMallReviewResponse.IRequest). This operation helps moderators, sellers, and admins efficiently locate and review seller responses for a given review, with options to filter by moderation status, creation date, and seller identity.

This operation enforces access controls so that only users with legitimate rights can view seller responses. Adequate audit logging and abuse monitoring are recommended. The response type is a paginated summary (IPageIShoppingMallReviewResponse.ISummary) suited for displaying multiple seller responses in tabular or list form for a selected review. This is crucial for moderation, dispute handling, and transparency workflows.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of seller responses associated with a specific product review.

This operation enables users to search, filter, and page through all response entries written by sellers in reply to the specified customer review. Results can be filtered by moderation status, withdrawal date, seller identity, and date range of creation or update.

Strict access controls are enforced: only authorized actors (primarily admins and moderators) may inspect all seller responses, while sellers and customers may only see responses relevant to their own products or reviews. The system must redact sensitive or non-public data for unauthorized actors.

The underlying table, shopping_mall_review_responses, supports full auditability, with all responses traceable to their review, authoring seller, and session. This operation is fundamental for moderation panels, seller dashboards, and customer notification flows.
operations.summary: Search and paginate seller responses tied to a specific customer review (shopping_mall_review_responses table).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of summary seller response objects matching the given filters for a specific review.

Each seller response is uniquely associated with a review (reviewId) and can be accessed via its unique responseId. The response includes body, status, withdrawal date, created/updated timestamps, moderation info, and author/seller metadata.

Access is restricted to actors meeting required permissions, such as platform admins, moderators, involved sellers, and original review authors, with sensitive fields appropriately scoped. This operation is primarily used in moderation workflows, seller dashboards, and customer engagement features where detailed view of a seller's response is necessary. Data is retrieved in full detail using the IShoppingMallReviewResponse DTO, without including large children arrays for efficiency.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full detailed information of a seller's response to a specific customer review, based on the given review and response identifiers.

This operation fetches all relevant fields, including the response body, moderation status and reason, creation/update timestamps, withdrawal info, and traceability links (such as seller and session references). It ensures audit and moderation requirements are met, showing additional diagnostic info for privileged actors.

Access is enforced according to user actor and relationship to the review or seller—admins and moderators may view all, other actors only their own. This operation uses the shopping_mall_review_responses table for lookup. It is critical for transparency, dispute resolution, and platform trust.
operations.summary: Retrieve the detailed information for a specific seller response related to a customer review (shopping_mall_review_responses table).

It operates on the shopping_mall_review_responses table and enables a product's seller to reply (once) to a specific customer review. Only one response can exist per review, and each response is linked to the corresponding review and seller account. The request body must supply the required response body text. Moderation status is managed at creation. On successful creation, the full response entity is returned.
operations.description:
Create a new response to a customer review, allowing a seller to publicly address and clarify feedback on their product. This fosters dialog and transparency between customers and sellers.

The seller must be authenticated and be the actual owner of the relevant product. The operation enforces strict ownership validation, ensuring that only the seller associated with the product reviewed can respond. Each review can have no more than one seller response; attempts to create additional responses are rejected.

Moderation status and reasons are managed at creation according to platform policies. Created responses are linked directly to the review and are visible alongside the original review, supporting customer service and brand reputation efforts. The response includes traceability to the seller account and session for compliance and auditing. Related API operations include updating or withdrawing a response and retrieving review with associated seller replies.

operations.description:
Update an existing seller response for a specific product review. This enables the seller to edit their original reply for clarification, correction, or content improvement.

The seller must be authenticated, and only the owner of the response (or an authorized admin) can update it. The operation performs strict verification of seller identity and editability, disallowing unauthorized updates or edits after moderation lock. Any changes to moderation status or withdrawal timestamp must comply with policy.

Updates are fully audited, maintaining a history of changes for compliance and trust. The updated response is returned with all fields, supporting auditability and transparency. Related operations include creating a new response and withdrawing or moderating responses.

operations.specification: This operation permanently removes a seller's response to a customer review from the database. It operates on the shopping_mall_review_responses table, which stores a single seller-authored textual response for each product review. This DELETE action is used by the seller or authorized admin to erase an inappropriate, outdated, or unwanted review response. It enforces that only one response exists per review, and ensures full traceability by requiring both the reviewId and responseId as path parameters, corresponding respectively to the unique customer review and the associated seller response. The operation is subject to validation against moderation status, business rules (withdrawn_at/deleted_at timestamps), and access permissions for sellers and admins. The underlying soft-deletion logic is implemented via the deleted_at field, marking the record as logically removed while retaining for audit and moderation workflows. This ensures review-discussion integrity while providing for eventual physical deletion as part of platform data retention policies.
operations.description:
Delete a specific seller's response to a customer review.

This endpoint is used when a seller, or an admin on their behalf, needs to remove their response to a product review, for reasons such as moderation, policy violation, or upon request. The DELETE operation targets the shopping_mall_review_responses table, which enforces a single seller response per customer review and ties responses to both seller and review records.

User authentication is required. Sellers may only delete their own responses, while admins may delete any response for moderation and oversight. The record is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at field with the current timestamp, allowing audit retention and potential recovery within the platform's review/dispute process. Attempts to delete already-deleted or non-existent responses will return a not found or gone status. Deleting a response does not affect the visibility or moderation status of the original review. Related operations include: creating a response (POST), retrieving a response (GET), and updating a response (PUT).

It enables both platform admins and sellers to analyze product feedback, identify highly/poorly rated items, and audit customer engagement with individual product SKUs. This operation retrieves a specific product rating from the shopping_mall_product_ratings table using the unique identifier of the rating. It provides the complete details of a standalone product rating that is associated with a customer, a specific product SKU, and an order item. The shopping_mall_product_ratings table enforces the rule that each customer can rate a given product SKU only once per completed purchase, and this API operation exposes all rating details including relationships to customer, SKU, and order item for full traceability.

By referencing this Prisma schema, the operation delivers all relevant fields including the numeric value, audit trail fields, and the soft delete marker. The retrieved rating can be used for customer review display, statistical aggregation, or verifying rating history for moderation. Related operations may include creation (POST /productRatings) and search/listing, which use similar schema compositions for request/response body definitions.

Retrieve full details for a standalone product rating record identified by its unique ID.

This API operation returns all properties of a product rating, including the numeric value (1–5 stars), linked customer, product SKU, associated order, and audit trail such as the customer session and timestamps. The description field in the Prisma schema clarifies that this rating is always tied to a specific customer, SKU, and order item, and updates are only allowed by the original customer within the permitted edit window.

Security: Access may be restricted based on requester permissions—customers may view only their own ratings, sellers may view ratings for their products, and admins may have broader access. The soft delete field (deleted_at) is included for completeness, and consumers of this API should check for this marker before presenting the rating in user-facing applications.

Use this operation in conjunction with the creation endpoint for new ratings, and aggregation endpoints for overall product rating statistics. Error scenarios include not found (invalid ID), unauthorized access, or ratings that have been soft deleted and filtered by business policy.

When invoked, this API records the provided value, establishes all audit trails—including session and timestamps—and references to related entities for traceability.

Product ratings support advanced review workflows and statistical aggregation. This create operation validates all business rules (such as ensuring the customer is eligible to rate, the order item has not been rated before, and the value falls within the allowed range). It also initializes all audit fields for further moderation, statistics, or rating calculation endpoints.
operations.description:
Create a new standalone product rating entry linked to a given customer, product SKU, and order item.

This API endpoint accepts a structured request containing all necessary fields to define a rating, including the value (1–5 stars), audit and relationship references, and creates a new record adhering to the composite unique constraint (customer, SKU, order item). The operation automatically populates audit fields such as timestamps and session identifiers, enforces value range limits, and checks eligibility (for example, that a customer has purchased the item and has not already reviewed it). If all conditions are satisfied, it creates the rating and returns the full record for confirmation.

Security and permissions are enforced to ensure that only eligible customers can create ratings for products they have purchased. Appropriate error handling is implemented for duplicate ratings, foreign key mismatches, and values out of range.

The operation can be paired with retrieval (GET /productRatings/{productRatingId}) and statistics endpoints for complete product rating management workflows.

operations.description:

Only the original customer who submitted the rating can perform this update, and only within a limited time window specified by business policies. The system will verify the customer's session and enforce all validation checks, including confirming that the rating remains associated with a valid, non-deleted order item and product SKU. Attempting to update outside of the allowed timeframe, or by unauthorized customers, will result in an error.

This API uses the shopping_mall_product_ratings Prisma table as its underlying database model, referencing all relevant foreign key relationships for integrity and audit trail. Updates are timestamped to reflect the latest modification, and all changes are subject to audit logging for security compliance.

Ratings are not physically deleted but rather marked as deleted using the deleted_at soft delete column, protecting system integrity and historical tracking. Subsequent queries will exclude ratings marked as deleted unless explicitly requested via admin operations.

All removals are logged for compliance monitoring and security reasons. Related API calls, such as search or get-by-ID, will not include ratings flagged as deleted, ensuring accurate end-user experiences.

Security is critical: only authorized admin or moderator actors can access this sensitive moderation/audit history. All queries are rate-limited and auditable for compliance. Results are governed by RBAC rules defined in the requirements and enforced at the provider level. The response includes summary information suitable for list and dashboard views, optimized for audit and moderation team workflows.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new dispute record in the shopping mall's dispute management module. It operates on the shopping_mall_disputes table in the database, which tracks cases arising from refund requests, order problems, or any escalated disputes involving customers, sellers, or admins. The operation expects all required dispute information, ties to any linked refund request if applicable, and captures the actors (customer, seller, and optionally admin), the status, subject, root cause, and resolution notes. All submitted data must match the schema constraints and support full dispute lifecycle and workflow integration for compliance and governance.
operations.description:
Create a new dispute case linked to customer, seller, and optionally an admin actor in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows authenticated users to initiate a dispute by submitting the necessary details about the dispute's subject, root cause, and any related refund request. All required actor IDs must be specified according to relationships in the shopping_mall_disputes schema. The 'status' should reflect the starting dispute state (e.g., open).

Upon creation, the dispute will be entered into the platform workflow for mediation and compliance tracking. Security: Typically restricted to admins or customer service staff for audit and platform integrity reasons. Successful creation logs the current state and actor context for later audit trail histories.

If a refund request is applicable, its primary key must be provided and the dispute will be linked to the request for traceability. The operation validates that referenced actor records exist and that business logic for allowed dispute creation paths is enforced.

It allows resolution status updates, modification of subject/root cause, assignment changes, or resolving/rejecting the dispute with decision notes. The primary key of the dispute to update must be specified in the path parameter. The request body must conform to the IShoppingMallDispute.IUpdate structure, enabling proper control and audit over the lifecycle of the platform dispute. The system ensures only allowed updates according to business rules and state transitions for dispute management/workflow compliance.
operations.description:
Update details, status, or resolution notes of an existing shopping mall dispute by specifying the dispute's ID and the new data.

The operation allows the assigned admin actor (or authorized platform staff) to modify the state of a dispute record as it progresses through investigation, mediation, or resolution. This may include changing the status (open, resolved, closed, etc.), updating subject/root cause, or adding a final resolution note once a decision has been made.

Strict validation is applied on allowed status transitions and that referenced actors and refund requests are valid according to the business logic. All updates are logged for auditability. Security is enforced such that only designated actors can mutate dispute records, maintaining integrity across the complaint lifecycle.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a dispute record from the shopping mall platform. It operates directly on the shopping_mall_disputes table as defined in the Prisma schema. Deleting a dispute is only allowed under strict administrative controls and typically represents the final step in dispute lifecycle management, such as compliance-driven data removal or correction of erroneous entries.

The operation targets a specific dispute identified by its unique ID. All references and historical records related to the dispute (such as dispute histories and audit logs) should be handled according to platform data retention and audit requirements—typically, child records are retained for compliance even after the dispute record is deleted (refer to 03-functional-requirements.md and the schema's soft-deletion behavior via deleted_at).

The operation will require elevated permissions (admin role). It strictly checks for existing dispute references and only allows deletion if business rules (such as no open compliance dependencies) permit. This endpoint complements advanced platform data lifecycle controls for dispute and audit management.
operations.description:
Permanently deletes a dispute from the shopping mall platform using its unique identifier.

This operation enforces strict administrative permissions: only platform admins are authorized to perform permanent dispute deletion. The request is verified against business rules and database constraints to prevent accidental or unauthorized removal of disputes that are still relevant to platform legal or compliance requirements.

All child records, such as dispute histories, are generally retained under audit policy; the operation centers on removing the root dispute entity (from shopping_mall_disputes table). The operation uses a soft-deletion via the deleted_at field, compliant with audit and regulatory retention policies. This approach ensures that data is hidden from active business workflows but available for legal review and historical analytics as required.

Attempting to delete a non-existent or already deleted dispute returns a suitable error message. The endpoint ensures transactional consistency, integrating with related API operations for dispute workflows, such as dispute resolution and audit log inspection.

This operation retrieves the full historical audit trail and workflow status changes for a specific dispute, drawing from the shopping_mall_dispute_histories snapshot table. Each record in this table documents an event in the dispute's lifecycle—including status changes, actor actions (admin/customer/seller), timestamps, and any attached notes. The endpoint enables admins to perform comprehensive incident review for compliance, investigation, or retrospective analysis.

Accessing the histories for a dispute provides a chronological sequence of all material workflow events, supporting platform accountability, security, and trust in dispute management practices. The response is paginated and returns detailed event records, facilitating advanced review of dispute resolution processes and supporting legal or regulatory documentation when required.
operations.description:
Returns a paginated list capturing the entire audit trail of status changes, actions, and notes for a specific dispute's lifecycle.

This endpoint is restricted to admin users to maintain strict confidentiality and integrity of the dispute resolution process. The operation queries the shopping_mall_dispute_histories table for all entries associated with the given disputeId—and returns the results in descending order by created_at (latest first for review efficiency).

Returned data includes the status at each stage, involved actor roles (admin, seller, customer), timestamps, and any contextual notes. The endpoint supports pagination to allow efficient review of long-running or complex disputes with extensive history. Combined with the main dispute record, this audit trail provides the foundation for compliance, governance, and forensic analysis in the shopping mall platform.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a specific historical status record related to a given dispute in the shopping mall platform. It is based on the 'shopping_mall_dispute_histories' Prisma table, which serves as an append-only historical audit log for all significant status changes and actions during the dispute lifecycle. Each history record includes status at that stage, actor IDs (admin, customer, or seller), timestamps, and an optional note.

The endpoint requires both the parent Dispute ID and the History ID, ensuring the returned history record is accurately linked to the target dispute. This operation enables traceability, forensic investigation, and compliance visibility for all parties involved in any dispute escalation.

Security-wise, only authorized actors linked to the dispute (customers, sellers, admins) or compliance personnel can view its audit trail. The response contains full details from the audit snapshot, supporting workflows in customer support, legal review, or platform compliance monitoring. Errors are returned when records are missing, mismatched, or access is not permitted.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single historical status or audit snapshot for a dispute.

This operation fetches a specific record from the shopping_mall_dispute_histories table, which logs every notable event, transition, or actor action throughout the lifecycle of a dispute (such as status changes, escalations, notes, and administrative interventions).

Useful for customer support, sellers, admins, or compliance teams needing to check a specific transition or note associated with the dispute. The operation enforces that only users with proper linkage to the dispute or administrative visibility can access this data.

The operation requires the disputeId (identifying the parent dispute) and the disputeHistoryId (identifying the history entry). Both must be valid UUIDs, and the endpoint will return detailed audit information or a suitable error if not found or not authorized. The response object contains the complete snapshot as stored in the history log, supporting review and traceability.

This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of all messages exchanged between actors (customer, seller, admin) within the context of a single dispute. It is based on the 'shopping_mall_dispute_messages' Prisma model, which tracks direct communications, message content, sender/receiver roles, and timestamps linked to a dispute case record.

The operation accepts a complex search/filter request body for advanced querying: filter by sender, receiver, message content (GIN-indexed), creation date ranges, role, and can sort or paginate results. It's intended for customer support, dispute mediation, legal review, or compliance, to provide a complete communication transcript for the dispute case.

Authorization ensures only actors with a direct relationship to the dispute (customer, seller, admin) or with platform compliance authority can query associated messages. Errors are returned for invalid dispute references, unauthorized access, or malformed queries. The response is a paginated list of message summaries for efficient review.

Powerful search and filter options are supported in the request body, including sender/receiver ID, role, partial content match, and date range filtering, as well as standard pagination and sorting.

Access control ensures only legitimate participants in the dispute (customer, seller, or admin) and compliance officers can view messages. This supports customer support, mediation, compliance documentation, and forensics. The response contains paginated message summaries, aiding transcript review and dispute management.

The API operates on the shopping_mall_dispute_messages table, enabling an authorized actor (such as customer, seller, or admin who participated in the dispute) to modify the message content. operations.description:
Update a specific dispute message within the context of a shopping mall dispute.

This endpoint allows authorized senders (admin, seller, or customer) to modify the content of their own message during an active dispute. Only messages that have not been deleted are eligible for updating. The primary use case is correction of typographical errors or clarifying message contents prior to resolution or closure of the dispute.

The operation verifies the identity and role of the actor to ensure only permitted edits. Edits to messages after the dispute is resolved may be restricted based on platform policies. The database model ensures an audit trail is maintained through timestamps and, where appropriate, administrative override logs.

Error handling includes permission checks, validation of message existence, and restriction after logical deletion (soft delete via deleted_at field). Related APIs include message creation, message erasure, and dispute state retrieval.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new shipment record for order fulfillment and logistics event tracking in the shopping mall system. It operates on the shopping_mall_shipments Prisma table, which captures all shipment detail for order items shipped via any integrated partner. The created record includes references to the order, specific order item, shipping partner, optional carrier tracking information, shipment status, and any provider integration result codes. This operation also logs full auditability with actor attribution and delivery/cancellation timestamps as applicable.

The operation ensures that referenced order, order item, and shipping partner IDs are valid and exist in their respective tables. It supports creation by either a seller or an admin, enforcing that at least one actor is attributed. The status must follow valid workflow values (pending, ready, picked_up, in_transit, delivered, cancelled, returned). If a shipping label or tracking code is not yet available, the corresponding fields are nullable. Provider API response codes may be logged if available at creation. Comprehensive validation rules ensure the integrity of the shipment creation process.
operations.description:
Create a new shipment record for an order item, referencing a specific order and assigning fulfillment responsibility to a shipping partner. This operation requires that the target order and order item are valid and not yet fulfilled or cancelled. Optionally, a carrier tracking code, initial shipment status, shipping label manifest link, and provider response code can be provided.

Actor attribution must be provided: either an admin (for administrative platform-initiated shipments) or a seller (for manual or self-fulfilled shipments). The actor fields are mutually exclusive, but one must be set. The shipping partner ID must reference a registered and active shipping/logistics provider. Appropriate status transitions will be enforced by the business logic depending on whether this is a pre-fulfillment, pickup, or immediate delivery event.

All shipment records include full audit trail with creator attribution, and timestamps are managed for creation, updates, delivery, or cancellation as relevant. Edge cases such as missing tracking information, label non-issuance, or delayed carrier integration are handled gracefully, with nullable fields indicating missing data at creation time. The payload allows storing of partner label URLs and the current shipment status. Related shipment update and cancellation operations are available for later status modifications and logistics event handling.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing shipment record's detail and status for the given shipmentId in the shopping mall system. It operates on the shopping_mall_shipments Prisma table, supporting modifications such as shipping status changes, label/manifest URI assignment, tracking information updates, delivery or cancellation logging, and provider result code adjustment. The operation enforces that status transitions adhere to order fulfillment and return lifecycle rules and that actor-based update attribution (admin or seller) is documented for each modification event.

To perform an update, the operation requires the unique shipmentId as the path parameter, referencing the existing shipment entry. The request body includes only updatable fields: shipping status, optional new carrier tracking code, manifest URL, timestamps for delivery or cancellation, and provider response update. This protects immutable foreign key relationships after creation (e.g., order, order item, shipping partner remain unchanged). Whenever the shipment status is set to 'delivered' or 'cancelled', the corresponding timestamp must be updated. Actor attribution for updates is supported for both admin and seller users with full audit logging.

Comprehensive validation ensures valid status workflow (pending, ready, picked_up, in_transit, delivered, cancelled, returned), that updates are only performed by authorized actors, and that no out-of-order state transitions occur.
operations.description:
Update shipment details—such as status, carrier tracking, manifests, delivery/cancellation timestamps, or API provider result—by specifying the shipmentId of the target shipment record. This operation allows status updates for both administrative and manual (seller-driven) shipment workflows, but does not permit changes to the base order, order item, or shipping partner fields after creation.

Acceptable status transitions are enforced in accordance with fulfillment and return business rules. If updating status to 'delivered' or 'cancelled', the corresponding delivery or cancellation timestamp must be included in the request, ensuring proper auditability. Carrier tracking and manifest/label links are modifiable as the shipment progresses, and provider API result codes can be updated when available. Actor attribution for the update (admin or seller) must be provided. All update operations are fully auditable and time-stamped, with proper integration to logistics or return flows as relevant.

If validation fails due to invalid status transition or unauthorized actor attempt, descriptive errors will be returned indicating the business rule violation. Shipment state updates should be coordinated with related shipment tracking history records for full event lifecycle management.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a shipment record from the shopping mall platform's order fulfillment system. It is based on the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma table, which maintains shipment details for each shipped order item. The operation allows authorized actors to remove a shipment entry, including references to tracking codes, manifest data, and all audit information related to the shipment event. Deletion is only permitted when the shipment is eligible for removal according to business rules, such as when it is not in a delivered or in-transit status, and no dependent tracking history must exist. This ensures platform data consistency and compliance with logistics and audit requirements.
operations.description:
This endpoint deletes a shipment record from the system by its unique identifier. Deleting a shipment is an irreversible operation and should only be performed when the shipment has not been delivered, is not in transit, or when allowed by platform business rules.

Security controls ensure that only actors with explicit permission (platform admins or the owning seller when applicable) can perform a deletion. The system validates shipment status prior to deletion and returns a descriptive error if the shipment cannot be removed due to business constraints or logistical events already processed. Related audit and tracking data will be evaluated for deletion or retention according to regulatory compliance requirements.

If dependent tracking histories exist or the shipment has progressed beyond a cancellable state, the system will deny the request and provide details in the error response. Related shipments for the same order or order item will not be affected by this operation.

This endpoint allows authorized system components (automated integrations), sellers, platform admins, or customers to report discrete shipment tracking updates, recording precise timestamps, statuses, event codes, optional geolocation, and free-form progress messages. This event becomes part of the shipment's official audit trail.

Security and permissions: Only the shipment owner or authorized platform actors can append tracking events, and all event data must be validated for injection, duplication, and timestamp ordering. Proper cross-checks ensure only valid events are written to the shipment's chronology. Automated and manual insertions must be clearly attributed for audit purposes.

This operation enforces the parent-child relationship between shopping_mall_shipments and shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories, and should be invoked by integrations, admin actions, or platform workflows when new events are received from carriers or manually logged.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent shipment (shoppingMallShipments) to which this new tracking event will be appended.

requestBody.description: Information required to create a new shipment tracking event record for the given shipment.

responseBody.description: The created tracking history event for the shipment.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: The parent shipment must exist before a tracking event can be created for it. This ensures a valid shipment record in shopping_mall_shipments with its shipmentId is available to link the tracking event to the correct shipment. Use the seller-side create shipment operation as prerequisite for shipment creation.

operations.specification: Creates a new shipment tracking history event beneath a specific shipment in the shopping mall platform. It is critical for maintaining an accurate, immutable progression of shipment events for auditing, support, and customer experience. Input data must strictly follow the schema for event creation, and linkage to the parent shipment is enforced through the shipmentId path parameter. The system may accept events from both automated provider integrations and manual admin/seller entry, subject to business rules.

operations.specification:
This operation updates the details of a specific shipment tracking history record in the context of shopping mall shipments, based on the shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories Prisma table. It allows authorized actors to amend the event information, such as time, location, status, or tracking messages, after initial receipt from the shipping carrier. This is essential for administrative corrections, integration fixes, or handling operational exceptions arising from logistics partners. Only shipments and tracking histories that exist within the platform's records can be updated, ensuring referential integrity and full auditability.

The update requires both the parent shipment's UUID (shipmentId) and the tracking history event's UUID (trackingHistoryId) to ensure the correct linkage and scope of modification. The structure of both shipment and tracking history is enforced by the underlying Prisma relationship, and all mutations are subject to strict validation according to business rules and schema constraints. Typical use cases include correcting erroneous tracking messages, reclassifying status codes, or refining geo-location data when carrier integrations provide incomplete or incorrect data.

Related operations include creation of new tracking events, which should be executed via dedicated endpoints. This operation should not be used for appending tracking events, but strictly for correcting existing entries.
operations.description:
Update an existing shipment tracking history record.

This operation enables authorized users to amend details of a previously recorded shipment tracking event. The typical use cases include fixing data integration errors, refining a carrier's event record, or handling business corrections after the fact.

Both the shipment ID and the tracking history ID are required to unambiguously identify the target record, reinforcing the parent-child relationship where tracking histories are always accessed via their parent shipment.

All updates must adhere to the data structure and business logic defined in the Prisma schema for shipment tracking histories, including status value constraints and field type expectations.
operations.summary: Update a tracking history record in shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories.

parameters.name: shipmentId
parameters.description: UUID of the parent shipment which owns this tracking history. Must correspond to shopping_mall_shipments.id.

parameters.name: trackingHistoryId
parameters.description: UUID of the specific shipment tracking history record to update. Must correspond to shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories.id within the specified shipment.

requestBody.description: New values for the tracking event to be updated. Only mutable fields from IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingHistory.IUpdate are accepted.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment tracking history record after modification.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A shipment must be created before its tracking history can be managed or updated, as each tracking record belongs to a parent shipment. This ensures shipmentId references a valid entity.

The tracking history event record must already exist before it can be updated. This guarantees that the trackingHistoryId provided for updating references an existing tracking event entry beneath the given shipment.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a specific shipment tracking history record from the shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories table. It is designed for administrative or correctional actions to remove erroneous, duplicate, or system-injected tracking events that should not have been recorded. All deletions are scoped strictly through both the parent shipment's UUID (shipmentId) and the tracking history event's UUID (trackingHistoryId) to guarantee accurate identity and preserve referential integrity on the platform.

The underlying shipment and its associated tracking histories are linked according to the Prisma schema. Deletions performed by this operation are hard deletes – the record is removed from the database and is no longer accessible after execution. This is a sensitive operation: only actors with appropriate administrative permissions may invoke it, due to its impact on the shipment's audit trail and event history integrity.

Business logic enforces auditability and validation of actor permissions prior to actual data removal. Related APIs include creation and updating of tracking histories. This endpoint must not be used for bulk deletions or for removing shipment records themselves; it applies solely to individual tracking events within a shipment.
operations.description:
Delete (erase) an existing shipment tracking history record.

This operation enables authorized administrators to irrevocably remove a specified tracking history record for a given shipment. Typical use cases include rectification of duplicate entries, removal of spurious events, or administrator-initiated data cleansing for compliance or operational integrity.

The operation requires both the shipmentId (the UUID of the parent shipment) and the trackingHistoryId (the UUID of the specific tracking event to delete), ensuring precise targeting of records for deletion.

As a hard delete operation, this API permanently removes the chosen tracking history record from the database. No soft delete or archiving occurs, and once deleted, the data is unrecoverable.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a tracking history record in shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories.

parameters.name: shipmentId
parameters.description: UUID of the parent shipment which owns this tracking history. Must correspond to shopping_mall_shipments.id.

parameters.name: trackingHistoryId
parameters.description: UUID of the specific shipment tracking history record to delete. Must correspond to shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_histories.id within the specified shipment.
