operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated and filterable list of return, pickup, or shipment reverse logistics requests from the shopping mall platform. It is based on the shopping_mall_return_requests Prisma table, which tracks all customer- or seller-initiated requests for returns or pickups, including their full lifecycle: creation, status transitions, carrier assignment, and audit-trail details. This search interface lets authorized staff, customer service, or fulfillment users query returns by status, date, requesting actor, order information, or fulfillment state, leveraging advanced filtering and sorting. This endpoint is critical for operations teams to manage large volumes of return and reverse logistics workflows, ensuring every request is tracked, managed, and resolved according to business rules and compliance needs.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, searchable index of all return, pickup, and shipment reverse logistics requests filed with the shopping mall platform.

This endpoint allows staff and authorized partners to search return requests with flexible filters including request status, creation and scheduled pickup dates, return reason text search, order/line item, and requesting actor (customer or seller). It also supports fine-grained sorting (e.g., by status, most recent requests, scheduled pickups) and paging for operational efficiency when reviewing or processing large volumes.

Comprehensive security controls ensure only authorized actors (operations, fulfillment center, or customer-service staff) can access this endpoint. Audit trails ensure every query can be reported for compliance. This index view enables proactive customer support and timely reverse logistics management. Additional details or lifecycle events for each request may be retrieved via the detail view endpoint.
operations.summary: Search, filter, and page through return requests via the shopping_mall_return_requests table.

requestBody.description: Filter and search parameters for retrieving return requests, including status, requesting actor, order/item, date ranges, and pagination controls.

responseBody.description: Paginated index of summarized return requests matching filter criteria and pagination, formatted for efficient operations review and next-action handling.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the full detailed record for a specific return, pickup, or shipment reverse logistics request, using the shopping_mall_return_requests Prisma table as the authoritative source. The operation looks up and returns a singular return request record by its unique identifier, with all pertinent business fields, status, and associations, including the order/item, actor attribution, lifecycle timestamps, carrier and tracking data, and audit metadata. It is essential for fulfillment, customer service, or admin staff to view every log and update associated with the reverse logistics process for a specific request.
operations.description:
Retrieve the complete detail of a single return, pickup, or shipment reverse logistics request.

This endpoint provides the full set of information for a single return request, including its status, associated order/item, customer or seller attribution, reasoning, all logistics/carrier details, audit fields, as well as lifecycle timestamps for submission, update, completion, or cancellation. The detailed record enables authorized staff to view the request's entire history and current disposition.

Strict authorization ensures only platform support or logistics staff can retrieve sensitive request details. This operation is commonly used after searching or listing via the index endpoint, and is critical for root-cause analysis, refund/dispute investigation, or direct customer communications about a return event.
operations.summary: Retrieve full detail for a specific return request in shopping_mall_return_requests using its unique ID.

parameters.name: returnRequestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the return or reverse logistics request to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Full detail record for a single return, pickup, or shipment reverse logistics request.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A return request must first be created before its details can be retrieved using its unique ID. This ensures that the record exists in the system.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new return, pickup, or reverse logistics request in the shopping mall platform. It operates on the shopping_mall_return_requests table, which captures customer- or seller-initiated requests to return or pick up delivered items, including fields for reason, status, actor attribution (customer or seller), scheduled pickup, carrier/shipment integration, and audit trail fields.

Submission of a return request is linked to a specific order item and references the related order, item, and requesting actor (customer or seller). The request captures the reason for return, target pickup address, as well as any initially known carrier/tracking details. Only actors with an active order item can initiate such a request. Upon submission, the initial status should be set according to workflow configuration (typically 'pending'), and subsequent workflow events (such as approval, scheduling, pickup, and completion) are managed through separate operations.

The primary business logic ensures that either requested_by_customer_id or requested_by_seller_id is provided and that the referenced order/order item are valid. Address and carrier information are optional until the request is advanced to scheduling/pickup. All timestamps and lifecycle events are audit-trailed for compliance and visibility. The creation endpoint enables the full reverse logistics flow for customer- and seller-driven returns.
operations.description:
Create a new return, pickup, or reverse logistics request associated with a specific order item in the shopping mall platform.

This operation enables either a customer or a seller to initiate a return or pickup for a delivered item, specifying a free-form reason, selecting the related order and item, and providing any known address or carrier information. The request is validated to ensure only valid order items can be referenced and only one actor (customer or seller) is marked as the requestor.

The operation supports capturing the reason, pickup address (which may default to the delivery address if omitted), and allows initial input of shipping partner information and tracking codes if already available. The lifecycle status is set to an initial workflow state, and auditing metadata is managed automatically.

Additional workflow actions, such as approval, pickup scheduling, completion, and cancellation, should use separate endpoints that update relevant status and audit fields. This operation establishes the root entity for all subsequent reverse logistics processing related to returns and pickups.
operations.summary: Create a return or pickup request in the shopping_mall_return_requests table.

requestBody.description: Input parameters for creating a new return or pickup request, including order and item references, reason, initial status, and optional address or carrier fields.

responseBody.description: The newly created return or pickup request entity with all audit, workflow, and linkage data.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing return, pickup, or reverse logistics request within the shopping mall platform. It targets the shopping_mall_return_requests table and supports modifications to request fields such as reason, status, scheduled pickup, tracking code, and actor-shipped metadata, subject to workflow and business validation.

An update may be performed by the actor who initiated the request, an admin, or by designated workflow roles (e.g., pickup scheduling staff or shipping partner). Fields that can be altered include the reason for the request, current workflow status, scheduled pickup date/time, assigned shipping partner, and tracking code. Some fields, such as audit trail timestamps (created_at, updated_at), are managed automatically by the system.

Business rules enforce that state changes conform to allowable workflow transitions and that at least one actor is associated with the operation. Attempting to update restricted fields or violate workflow progression logic (such as moving from completed to pending) results in a validation error. The operation is foundational for managing the lifecycle of the reverse logistics process for returns.
operations.description:
Update the details or workflow status of an existing return or pickup request in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows updates to any mutable property of the return/pickup request, including status transitions, reason updates, scheduled pickup modifications, or changes to shipping and tracking information. Validation logic enforces proper workflow progression and authorized actor roles in managing each field. Only valid status transitions are permitted.

The update action records updated_at timestamps and retains full audit details for each modification. Triggering of business events such as scheduling, pickup assignment, or request completion/cancellation may be dependent on proper use of this update endpoint in tandem with workflow policies. It is critical that client apps and workflow automations adhere strictly to business rules when invoking this operation.
operations.summary: Update a return or pickup request in the shopping_mall_return_requests table.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the return or pickup request record to update.

requestBody.description: Modifiable fields of the return or pickup request including status, scheduled pickup, carrier info, and reason.

responseBody.description: The updated return or pickup request record reflecting all field changes and workflow state progression.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently erases a return or pickup request record from the 'shopping_mall_return_requests' table. It is designed to allow administrative actors to perform a hard delete of an existing return request, including all its status, logistics, and audit information. This endpoint is used in scenarios where a return request must be completely removed from the system—such as for error correction, data cleanup, or compliance-based data purges—rather than marking it as deleted (soft delete) via a nullable 'deleted_at' field. The operation ensures that all references to specific order items, related customer or seller information, carrier and tracking details, and audit trail information associated with the request are wiped from the database, and the record is unrecoverable through normal means. 

It is essential to note that while the schema allows soft deletion by using 'deleted_at', this API operation forces a permanent record removal. All dependent business logic, foreign key constraints, and system auditing must be respected to mitigate data integrity risks and ensure that removal is permitted only for actors with proper governance permissions, such as admins or designated compliance officers.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a return or reverse logistics request from the system database. This operation completely deletes the targeted return/pickup request record from the platform, eliminating all status, shipment, actor attribution, scheduling, and carrier/tracking fields for the specified request.

Only administrators and actors with elevated governance privileges are permitted to execute this permanent erase action, due to its irreversibility and potential compliance implications. The targeted record is gone from the 'shopping_mall_return_requests' table and cannot be recovered by normal means; related audit trails and referential links should be checked by the system to prevent orphaned references.

This hard deletion is differentiated from soft deletion (where 'deleted_at' is set) because it physically removes the underlying row, instead of marking as deleted. Use this operation only when business policy calls for actual tombstone record destruction or irreparable data removal, such as for error correction or sensitive personal data purges.
operations.summary: Permanently erase a return request entry from the shopping_mall_return_requests table.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target return or pickup request.

authorizations.name: customer
authorizations.description: A registered buyer who can browse products, manage addresses, place orders, track shipments, maintain carts and wishlists, write reviews, and request cancellations or refunds. Standard member authentication.

authorizations.name: seller
authorizations.description: A registered merchant who can manage their product catalog, inventory, SKUs, process and update orders, track sales statistics, and handle customer feedback. Uses member authentication.

authorizations.name: admin
authorizations.description: Platform administrator with full access. Can view and manage all products, orders, users, categories, sellers. Handles escalations, resolves disputes, manages refunds/cancellations, and has platform-wide control.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

pages.description:
Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

IShoppingMallCustomer.ICreate.description:
Object schema for registering a new customer in the shopping mall platform.

Used as the request body for customer join/registration API. Contains all required business fields for customer identity creation, as defined by business rules and shopping_mall_customers Prisma schema. Does not accept authentication context fields (id, created_at, updated_at), nor the hashed password column directly. Accepts only the plain password for registration, which is securely hashed server-side per security policy. Field validation, such as required uniqueness and password format, is enforced by backend logic.

email.description: Customer's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all customers. Subject to validation for proper format and domain.

password.description: Raw password string for customer registration. Must meet business rules for minimum length and complexity (at least 8 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, digit, symbol). Never stored directly; will be hashed to password_hash server-side.

name.description: Legal full name of the customer. Required for identification and order fulfillment. Subject to name format and length validations.

phone.description: Customer's primary phone number for communications. Format: digits, may include dashes, spaces or parentheses, 8-20 characters.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized.description:
API response schema for successful customer authentication (join/login/refresh).

Delivered following successful join, login, or token refresh operations for customer actors. Contains identity and session context. Always includes id (UUID format) of authenticated customer and issued JWT tokens via a standard token object. May include additional authentication or customer identity fields in future variants.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated customer. Maps directly to the id column in shopping_mall_customers schema.

email.description: Customer's email address for authentication and notifications. Must be unique across all platform customers.

name.description: Legal full name of the customer.

phone.description: Primary phone number for this customer, used for contact and order communications.

is_email_verified.description: Whether the customer's email address has been verified. Used for regulatory compliance and communication reliability.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp for when the customer account was created.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp for the last time the customer account was updated.

IShoppingMallCustomer.ILogin.description:
Schema for customer login request. Used for authenticating a registered customer via email and password according to shopping mall authentication policy. Includes connection context (href, referrer, ip) for audit trail per security requirements.

All fields are strictly defined:
- 'email': required; must match registered unique email in shopping_mall_customers
- 'password': required; plain text password (will be securely compared to hash)
- 'href': required; connection URL for session context tracking
- 'referrer': required; previous page or referrer context
- 'ip': optional; client's IP address, can be provided by client or inferred by backend. Nullable for cases where server logic applies.

This schema enables secure authentication flows and session management as described in requirements and business rules.

email.description: Customer's registered email address. Must match unique value in shopping_mall_customers. Used for authentication and communication. Validated per RFC 5322.

password.description: Plain text customer password. Compared securely against the stored 'password_hash'. Never stored, visible, or returned. Minimum 8 characters, complexity enforced (see security policies).

href.description: Connection URL representing the page or location where session was initiated. Required for security and audit trail per privacy/compliance.

referrer.description: Referrer URL identifying originating page or site before initiating session. Required for session context and audit compliance.

oneOf.description: Client's IP address in IPv4 or IPv6 form. Used for audit, suspicious login detection, and privacy compliance.
Client's IP address in IPv4 or IPv6 form. Used for audit, suspicious login detection, and privacy compliance.

ip.description: Client's IP address in IPv4 or IPv6 form. Used for audit, suspicious login detection, and privacy compliance. Optional (nullable); may be provided by client or inferred on server.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh.description:
Schema for customer token refresh request. Used to securely refresh JWT tokens for an existing authenticated customer session. Requires refresh token for session validation.

- 'refresh_token': required; cryptographically secure token issued at login and tied to a session tracked in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. Must be valid and unexpired.

Session tracking and security logic (expiration, rotation, audit) are based on the session record (shopping_mall_customer_sessions).

This schema provides the minimum required context for secure token rotation and reuse according to platform authentication policies.

refresh_token.description: Cryptographically secure, unpredictable token value provided to the client at login or registration. Required for refreshing JWT session. Must match an active, non-expired session row in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.

email.description: Seller's unique login email. Used for authentication and main point of contact. Must be unique and comply with platform validation as defined in the database schema and business rules.

password.description: Seller's account password, submitted in plain text for registration. Will be hashed and stored as password_hash in the database. Must meet password policy for strength and character requirements. Not stored or returned in plaintext after submission.

business_name.description: Legal business name of the seller. This is required for compliance and will be publicly shown on the product catalog. Must match official business registration as verified by platform policies.

registration_number.description: Government-issued business registration or license number. Required for regulatory compliance and Know Your Customer (KYC) verification. Must be unique on the platform per legal requirements.

business_phone.description: Official business contact phone number for support and notifications. Must be a valid phone number per business validation requirements.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) for session context tracking. Required for authentication context and audit trail.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) used for session context and security audit. Required for compliance with session context pattern.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking. Used for security analysis and auditing. May be null or omitted if not provided by client, as server may extract it from connection context.

IShoppingMallSeller.ICreate.description:
Seller registration data transfer object for creating new seller accounts.

Contains all business and authentication fields as required by the shopping_mall_sellers database schema, as well as session context fields for auditing and security. Ensures all data required for onboarding, KYC compliance, and initial session creation is present.

Passwords must be submitted in plain text for initial registration; the system will hash before storage. Email and registration number must be unique. See business rules document for validation, error responses, and onboarding flows.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated seller, corresponding to the id field in shopping_mall_sellers.

email.description: Seller's unique login email. Used for authentication and the main point of contact as defined in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma model. Uniqueness is enforced at the database layer. Visible to admins for identification and communication.

business_name.description: Legal business name of the seller, required for platform usage and public catalog display. Reflects the official registration with authorities. Enforced as not-null in the database.

registration_number.description: Government-issued registration/license number. Used for platform KYC, compliance, and legal reporting. Uniqueness enforced. May be cross-verified by admins or compliance bots.

business_phone.description: Official business contact phone for admin, customer support, and platform notifications. Registered with the seller account and modifiable by authorized actors. Not-null required.

is_email_verified.description: Indicates whether seller has completed email verification. Set by system during onboarding or password recovery; enforced for compliance and product listing eligibility. Boolean flag as defined in the Prisma schema.

status.description: Current seller workflow/account status such as: pending, approved, rejected, suspended, etc. Used in admin workflows for onboarding, compliance, and business lifecycle. Required string as described in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma model.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when the seller account was created in the platform. Used for audit, reporting, and business logic.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp for the last update to the seller account. Reflects last admin modification or business-initiated change.

seller.description: Authenticated seller account data, excluding sensitive fields such as password_hash. Used to establish dashboard or API identity and session context.

IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized seller authentication result object returned after registration, login, or token refresh.

Contains issued JWT authentication tokens and summary seller account details, omitting all sensitive/credential fields. Used for all workflow steps requiring authenticated seller context.

Do not expose the seller's password_hash or sensitive information.

IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary.description:
Summary object representing a shopping mall seller for business context in platform displays, dispute resolution, and list/reference scenarios.

Always exposes the business_name exactly as recorded in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma DB schema, ensuring consistent business/legal identity across both admin-facing and customer-facing workflows. This summary guarantees buyers, admins, and platform automation can reliably resolve seller entities to their registered legal identities for auditing, communication, and regulatory compliance.

Use this summary anywhere a reference to seller identity is needed, such as in dispute messages, order fulfillment, or product listings. Always synchronize the business_name property with the official business record as defined in shopping_mall_sellers.

id.description: Unique identifier for the seller. This is the database entity's primary key and is required for any seller reference throughout the platform, dispute logs, compliance checks, and order flows.

business_name.description:
Legal business name of the seller as registered in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma DB schema. This value is the official business identity required for regulatory, auditing, display, and messaging use-cases. Always matches the value in the database—do not substitute arbitrary display names or personal names.

Use this property for all UI displays that show seller details, legal notices, dispute parties, or catalog attributions. Consistency is required for business/legal integrity across platform operations.

email.description:
Seller's unique login email. Used for authentication and main point of contact.

This value is required for credential-based authentication for seller actors. The email address submitted here is matched against the primary email in the shopping_mall_sellers database table. All login attempts should be case-insensitive and should follow RFC 5322 standard email format. Duplicate or unregistered emails will result in login failure.

password.description:
Seller's login password in plain text, provided by the user for verification.

On submission, the password is compared securely against the bcrypt hash stored in the Prisma schema column password_hash. Minimum complexity and length is enforced per security policy, with a recommended minimum of 8 characters. Never accept pre-hashed passwords in this DTO—hashing is performed on the server-side only. The password is not persisted or returned in any API response.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and suspicious login detection.

If provided, must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 string. This value is optional—backend extracts it if omitted—but clients are encouraged to provide it if possible, especially for server-side rendered flows or where proxies/intermediaries obscure the connection source.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) for session audit trails.

Represents the actual URL/location from which the login request was initiated. Required for risk analysis, audit logging, and context establishment for suspicious activity detection.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL or empty string if direct access).

Used to identify how the seller navigated to the login page and to support fraud analysis and consistent session context. Required for logging and security analytics.

IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.description:
Seller login credential DTO for authenticating to the platform.

Represents the minimal, schema-backed set of authentication fields accepted by the /auth/seller/login endpoint. This DTO is strictly limited to credential fields (email, password) that actually exist in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema. Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included to establish audit logs and security context, and must follow field requirements as outlined.

Passwords here are never persisted—only used transiently for credential verification and hashing on the backend. Extra fields or business/profile data must not be present in login requests.

refresh_token.description:
Refresh token originally issued during login, required to renew JWT access for continued authentication.

Must be a secure, random string conforming to the platform's token issuance protocol. Used to validate session authenticity, enforce rotation/invalidation if session log tables exist, and to prevent replay attacks. Submission of a valid refresh token is required to successfully obtain a new access/refresh token pair from the /auth/seller/refresh endpoint.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh.description:
Seller token refresh DTO for renewing JWT authentication.

Used by the /auth/seller/refresh endpoint to request a new access and refresh token pair. Accepts only the refresh_token field for seller session continuity. Validation checks must align with cryptographic and session management policies as defined on the platform. Only actual session fields supported by the backend should be referenced or persisted.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ICreate.description:
DTO for platform administrator registration (join) operation.

Provides the required fields for new admin account onboarding, corresponding to columns in the shopping_mall_admins table. This includes unique email, plaintext password (to be securely hashed), and display name. Applies all validations as per schema, including password complexity and uniqueness of email. Does NOT expose or accept fields like password_hash, which are handled by backend only. Used strictly for admin join endpoint; never for login or other contexts.

email.description: Unique email address for admin authentication and platform notifications. Must be unique, non-null, and pass all standard and business email validation checks.

password.description: Admin account registration password in plaintext. Must satisfy complexity rules (minimum 8 characters, mixed case, at least one digit and symbol). Will be securely hashed and never stored/transmitted in plaintext after this operation.

name.description: Administrator's full display name. Used for audit, contact, and admin platform attribution. Must be non-empty.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Response DTO for successfully authenticated or refreshed administrator sessions.

Returned after a successful shopping mall admin login or refresh operation. Contains the admin's core account identifier and the issued authentication tokens for client use. All properties are required for downstream authenticated access and must be securely stored or transmitted per security policy.

For security and token lifecycle management, only fields specified here will appear in responses. Passwords and other sensitive account information are never included.

id.description: The unique UUID identifier for the platform admin actor account. This value maps directly to shopping_mall_admins.id and is used as the primary key for all admin-level services and auditing.

email.description: Unique admin email address for authentication and contact. Must be unique per administrator and is required for account communications.

name.description: Full name of the administrator for auditing, contact, and action logs.

is_email_verified.description: Whether the admin's email has been verified and the account is fully activated. Controls access to privileged functions.

status.description: Current account status, such as active, suspended, or revoked. Controls the admin's platform access and privileges.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created. System-managed for audit history.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update to the admin account. System-managed for audit and rollback.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin.description:
Admin login credentials request DTO for authentication.

Used to submit platform administrator credentials for authentication against the shopping_mall_admins user table. All properties directly correspond to columns in the Prisma model. Input fields are strictly limited to the schema—password sent in plaintext for hashing and authentication. Account status, lockout, and email validation are enforced at the service layer per security requirements. This DTO is not used for registration—only for login and authentication.

Security: Password is provided plain for comparison only, never stored or returned to the client. Rate limiting and anti-abuse measures apply to this DTO.

Session fields: ip, href, and referrer are not present because this login operation is for privileged admin actors, not public or end-user registration flows. They are tracked server-side in the admin session log.

email.description: Unique email for authentication and notification. This property is required for all admin account authentication and must match an existing account from the shopping_mall_admins table. Validated as an RFC 5322-compliant email address. Each admin's email is unique. Used for login as the primary credential.

password.description: Platform administrator password to authenticate the login request. The client sends the plain (unhashed) password, which is never logged or returned. The server will hash and compare this value with 'password_hash' from shopping_mall_admins. The password must conform to the organization's length and complexity requirements. See admin registration and security policies for detailed password rules.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRefresh.description:
DTO for refreshing or rotating current authentication tokens for an admin account.

Used in the admin session management flow. A valid, non-expired refresh token must be provided, which is validated and, if legitimate, used to issue new access/refresh tokens. The refresh token property is required and must be a secure, JWT-compliant token generated during admin login and stored securely.

This DTO is strictly for authentication/session token renewal and does not support any other operations or properties. The token value is server-validated per authentication and security subsystem policies.

refresh_token.description: A valid, previously issued refresh token for an authenticated administrator. The token must be a secure JWT value that proves the admin session's authenticity. Used to rotate authentication tokens for continued access. Must not be expired or revoked. Accepted only if generated for an admin account in good standing and present in the corresponding session table.

page.description: Page number for pagination when retrieving configuration entries. Starts at 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of configuration entries to return per page. Typical values are 10, 20, 50, or 100.

sort_by.description: Field for sorting results. Must be one of 'config_key', 'status', 'created_at', or 'updated_at'.

order.description: Sort direction for results. Accepts 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

status.description: Optional filter to include only configurations with status 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'.

search.description: Optional keyword or phrase for full-text search on the configuration key or description.

IShoppingMallConfiguration.IRequest.description:
Request query for searching and retrieving a paginated list of shopping mall configuration entries.

Used by admin actors to filter, sort, and paginate through the list of platform-wide configuration settings. Includes optional filters for status, advanced full-text search, and result ordering. The query parameters align with standard list operations for management UIs.

id.description:
Primary key for the configuration entry. Uniquely identifies each platform configuration record.

Critical for reference and lookup in all system modules referencing this setting.

config_key.description:
Unique configuration key name for the system setting.

Used for service and API lookup. Enforced unique by constraint. Namespaced with category/domain prefixes when possible.

config_value.description: String or JSON-serialized configuration value for platform logic. This field is raw storage, with value semantics determined by the business logic for each config_key.

description.description: Detailed, admin-facing explanation of this configuration's purpose and platform effect. Documentation aid for maintenance of global options.

oneOf.description:
Configuration state - controls feature rollout, testing, or deprecation. Must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'.

Active means the config is currently in effect. Inactive disables the config without removal. Deprecated marks for pending removal.

Configuration state - controls feature rollout, testing, or deprecation. Must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'.

Active means the config is currently in effect. Inactive disables the config without removal. Deprecated marks for pending removal.

Configuration state - controls feature rollout, testing, or deprecation. Must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'.

Active means the config is currently in effect. Inactive disables the config without removal. Deprecated marks for pending removal.

status.description:
Configuration state - controls feature rollout, testing, or deprecation. Must be one of 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'.

Active means the config is currently in effect. Inactive disables the config without removal. Deprecated marks for pending removal.

created_at.description: Timestamp this configuration entry was created. Used for audit logs and traceability.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update for audit logging.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete marker - if null, the record is active. Otherwise records when entry was retired/removed.

IShoppingMallConfiguration.description:
Platform-wide configuration entry recording system parameters, feature flags, and constants for the e-commerce shopping mall backend.

Enables admin-only CRUD of settings affecting global platform behavior. Used for rollout, feature gating, and special runtime logic control. Each config entry is uniquely identified and fully auditable.

config_key.description: Unique configuration key for the new system setting. Namespaced for domain/category if possible and must be globally unique among all platform settings.

config_value.description: Raw configuration value - can be string or JSON-serialized. The meaning is determined by business logic referencing each config_key.

description.description: Detailed admin-facing explanation of the effect and purpose of this configuration.

oneOf.description: Desired configuration state on creation. 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Used to control rollout or testing. 'active' enables immediately.
Desired configuration state on creation. 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Used to control rollout or testing. 'active' enables immediately.
Desired configuration state on creation. 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Used to control rollout or testing. 'active' enables immediately.

status.description: Desired configuration state on creation. 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Used to control rollout or testing. 'active' enables immediately.

IShoppingMallConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Request to create a new global configuration entry for the e-commerce shopping mall platform. Only accessible to admin users.

Must provide key, value, purpose description, and initial status. Uniqueness of config_key is enforced. Use for registration of platform options, feature flags, and system parameters.

config_value.description: Updated value for the configuration setting. Can be string or JSON-serialized according to the business logic bound to config_key.

description.description: Revised, admin-facing explanation of this configuration's purpose, feature gating, or system effect. Enables improved auditability and clarity for global options.

oneOf.description:
New configuration state.

Must be 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Use for enabling/disabling feature toggles or flagging deprecations.

New configuration state.

Must be 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Use for enabling/disabling feature toggles or flagging deprecations.

New configuration state.

Must be 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Use for enabling/disabling feature toggles or flagging deprecations.

status.description:
New configuration state.

Must be 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Use for enabling/disabling feature toggles or flagging deprecations.

IShoppingMallConfiguration.IUpdate.description:
Request to update a global configuration entry in the shopping mall backend system. Allows admin to modify value, description, and operational status for critical settings.

Field availability reflects platform rules: all fields required to ensure complete configuration state is always specified. Update is only allowed for non-deleted (active) entries.

name.description: Filter for categories with a name matching this value. If omitted, all names are considered. Useful for admin search or UI navigation filter.

status.description: Category status filter—use 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated' to limit results to categories with that status.

parent_id.description: Optional filter for categories with a specific parent. Provide the UUID of the parent category, or null for root categories. Used for hierarchical queries.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. 1-based index.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page for results. Controls pagination window size.

oneOf.description: Direction for sorting: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Direction for sorting: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Direction for sorting: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering, searching, and paginating product or navigation categories in the shopping mall taxonomy.

Enables fine-grained control for UI builders, admin interfaces, or batch API clients. Supports filtering by name, status, or parent category (hierarchy), as well as custom sorting and paging for scalable taxonomy management.

id.description: Primary Key for the category. Uniquely identifies each product or navigation category in the taxonomy.

name.description: Globally unique name of the category. Used in UI display, path generation, and for unambiguous API reference. Must be unique as per @@unique([name]) in the schema.

description.description: Human-readable, long-form description of this category's purpose and scope. Used by admins and merchandisers for management context. Indexed for full-text search.

sort_order.description: Integer value to determine ordering in navigation or display. Lower values display earlier. Optimized with an index for large category sets.

status.description: Category status: indicates availability and admin workflow state. Valid values are 'active', 'inactive', or 'deprecated'. Used for UI, filtering, and programmatic use.

parent_id.description: Optional UUID referencing the parent category for hierarchical structure. Null if this category is a root node.

created_at.description: Timestamp recording when this category was created. System-managed.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update to this category. System-managed; used for audit trails.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion field. If set (non-null), the category is inactive and excluded from standard browsing. Used for safe deactivation.

IShoppingMallCategory.description:
Detailed entity representing a single product or navigation category in the shopping mall taxonomy.

Based on the shopping_mall_categories table, supports arbitrarily deep nesting (through parent_id), system-managed audit fields, and soft deletion for safe workflow. Used by both catalog browsing UIs and admin management tools. Ensures uniqueness and stable reference for inventory, product assignment, and navigation.

IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for a shopping mall category entity. Used for administrative or trusted API client calls to register a new category for product or navigation taxonomy.

This type enables hierarchical category creation: to create a root category, omit parent_id; to nest a category, supply parent_id referring to another category's id. The name field must be unique across all categories, as enforced by the database unique constraint. sort_order determines UI listing order; lower values sort earlier. status controls visibility and usage in the system.

System-managed fields such as created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are handled automatically by the platform and must not be supplied by clients. This DTO should be used with create endpoints only. parent_id is optional for root categories.

name.description: Unique category name as it will appear in client UIs and references. Must be globally unique by database constraint.

description.description: Long-form text describing the purpose, scope, and context of this category. Required for clarity in admin UI and merchandising tasks.

sort_order.description: Ordering value for navigation menus or category lists. Lower numbers will result in the category being displayed earlier in lists.

status.description: Administrative status flag. Allowed values are: active, inactive, or deprecated. Used for approval workflows, deactivation, or programmatic filtering.

parent_id.description: ID of the parent category for hierarchical nesting. Omit or supply null for root-level categories with no parent.

IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for the shopping mall category entity. Used by admins or system clients to modify an existing product/navigation category.

The name of the category is supplied in the URL path as a unique identifier and must not be included in the request body; it cannot be changed after creation. Clients can update the description, display order, status, and hierarchical parent assignment. All fields are optional to allow PATCH-like flexibility: omit fields to leave them unchanged.

System-managed fields and the name must not be changed. Only allowed to update business metadata, sort order, status, and parent category linkage.

description.description: Long-form text describing the purpose, scope, and context of the category.

sort_order.description: New display order value for UI listing; lower sorts earlier.

status.description: Administrative status. Allowed values: active, inactive, or deprecated. Used for activation, deactivation, or phasing out categories.

parent_id.description: Category ID to change parent for nesting. Supply null to make the category a root node.

IShoppingMallExternalPaymentProvider.description:
Represents a registered external payment provider integrated with the shopping mall platform. Each provider defines an available payment gateway (such as Stripe, Toss, or PayPal), maintained by administrators and referenced in checkout and payment flows for the entire commerce platform.

Includes provider display name for UI, a unique provider code for system integration, a status flag for operative state (active/inactive/deprecated), integration/legal notes for compliance, and audit fields. Supports soft deletion via `deleted_at` for historical records and compliance without data loss.

This type does not expose any sensitive secrets or credentials. Directly matches the `shopping_mall_external_payment_providers` table in the Prisma schema. Used in detailed provider queries and admin/management scenarios.

id.description: Primary key: Unique identifier for this external payment provider. Used to reference this record in all business, audit, and configuration contexts. Generated on provider registration.

provider_name.description: Display name of the payment provider as shown in checkout UIs and admin dashboards. Must be unique system-wide for clarity and ease of management.

provider_code.description: System integration key/code for the payment provider. Globally unique string used for backend payment orchestration, API communication, and reference in all order/payment records. Enforced unique per platform in the database.

status.description: Current status of the payment provider within the system. Typical values: active, inactive, deprecated. Determines if the provider is available for new transactions and visible in UIs.

description.description: Integration, legal, or business context notes for the payment provider. Used by admins for compliance, troubleshooting, or integration setup documentation. May be used by dashboard and audit tools.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the provider was first registered in the platform. Used for compliance, audit, and chronological management.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this record. Used for audit trails, configuration management, and UI display of modification history.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of soft deletion (deactivation) for the provider. If null, the provider is currently active (not soft deleted). Used for historical retention, business audit, and compliance.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion (deactivation) field. When set, indicates that the provider has been logically removed from active use but is retained for audit/compliance.

IShoppingMallExternalPaymentProvider.IRe.description: Schema for search, filter, and pagination parameters when requesting a paginated list of external payment providers for the shopping mall platform. Enables advanced query of available providers for admin tools or public UI integration setting screens. Fields match provider codes, names, statuses, and support business context search. Extensible for future filtering on integration type or usage statistics.

provider_name.description: Filter by provider display name, supports partial or exact text match for search UI.

provider_code.description: Filter by provider integration code, supports partial or exact match for admin or troubleshooting tools.

status.description: Filter by payment provider status. Acceptable values: active, inactive, deprecated. Used to restrict results to only active providers or include those pending deprecation.

q.description: Free-text search of provider name, code, and description fields for all-purpose search UI. Optional field.

page.description: Request pagination page number (1-based index). Defaults to 1 if not supplied.

limit.description: Page size: Number of providers to return per request. Used for pagination UX and server resource management. Sensible default recommended if not specified.

IShoppingMallExternalPaymentProvider.ICr.description:
Data Transfer Object for creating a new external payment provider entry in the shopping mall platform registry.

Captures all required metadata needed to register a new payment integration, such as a payment gateway or provider, which can be referenced throughout payment flows and checkout orchestration.

Only admin users may invoke operations accepting this DTO. Backend logic enforces uniqueness for provider_name and provider_code, and audit fields are managed automatically.

provider_name.description: Display name of the external payment provider, as shown in checkout UIs. Must be unique per provider.

provider_code.description: System integration key/code — unique backend identifier for the external payment provider. Uniqueness is enforced for backend API orchestration and mapping.

status.description: Operational state of the payment provider—must be one of: active, inactive, or deprecated. Controls whether the provider is available in checkout and payment method selections.

description.description: Business/legal description of the payment provider, including context for integration and compliance. Required for audit.

IShoppingMallExternalPaymentProvider.IUp.description:
Data Transfer Object for updating an existing external payment provider's configuration and metadata in the registry table.

Permits an administrator to change properties such as the display name, backend integration code, legal/business description, and operational status (active/inactive/deprecated).

All updates are tracked in audit fields for compliance. The unique 'provider_code' (used as a path parameter) identifies the target record and is not included in the body. Only admin users are authorized to invoke operations using this DTO.

provider_name.description: Updated display name for the provider, as shown in checkout UIs. Must remain unique.

status.description: Updated operational state: active, inactive, or deprecated. Determines visibility and usability for payment orchestration.

description.description: Updated business/legal description or integration notes. Required for compliance logging.

id.description:
Primary Key.

A unique identifier for this shipping partner entry. Ensures every partner can be consistently referenced in internal FKs and by external integrations.
Used for all CRUD, lookup and audit operations referencing this partner.

partner_name.description:
Display name (UI/reference); unique.

Visible to all admin and user actors when selecting or identifying this shipping partner.
Must be unique across all partners, used for business reporting as well as end-user UI presentation.

partner_code.description:
Integration code for backend (system use); unique.

Used by integration logic, platform API identifiers, and for all FKs in related shipment/order/fulfillment tables.
Must be unique across all partners. This is the primary lookup field for external system integrations and partner selection.

status.description:
active/inactive/deprecated—admin only control.

Indicates whether this partner can be selected for shipments, is temporarily disabled, or is deprecated for future use (but still visible for legacy/audit reasons).
Admin controls this field to manage available partners for operational or compliance reasons. This field is indexed for fast queries.

description.description:
Business and operational info about the partner.

Full description of business context, operational notes, or instructions regarding this shipping partner. Used by admins and users to distinguish between similar partners, review operational capabilities, or identify compliance status.
Supports search/keyword filter in API operations.

created_at.description:
Creation moment (audit).

Timestamp indicating when this partner entry was created in the registry. Used for audit, compliance, and lifecycle history.

updated_at.description:
Mutation/audit update time.

Timestamp tracking the last time any data field for this partner was modified. Supports system audit logs and consistency checks.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete for legacy/decommissioned partners.

If present, indicates this partner has been soft-deleted and is no longer active in operational workflows. Kept for audit/history but not selectable for new shipments.
Nullable—null means partner is active or officially inactive, but not deleted.

IShoppingMallShippingPartner.description:
Official platform registry for logistics/shipping partners in buyer and seller flows.

Each partner is registered with business display name, system integration code, status, operational notes, and audit timestamps.

Partners may be active, inactive, or soft-deleted (deprecated) for compliance and lifecycle management. The registry enables both active use in shipment flows and complete audit/history for all past partners. Uniqueness constraints are enforced for both name and code.
Referenced in all order, shipment, and tracking records, and available to admin and business users for configuration, lookup, and audit.

The entity is used for CRUD, list, and config operations in platform admin UIs and APIs. Supports keyword search and status/category filtering for operational and compliance use.

partner_name.description:
Partial or complete match on the shipping partner's display name.

Supports keyword-based searching and filtering, used to find partners by business name in admin UIs and automation scripts.

partner_code.description:
Exact or partial match on system integration code.

Allows admins to filter by backend codes when debugging integration issues or batch-renaming/managing codes across partners.

status.description:
Operational status filter. Accepts one of: active, inactive, deprecated.

Restricts listing results to partners matching the selected operational state.

description.description:
Keyword filter against the business/operational partner description field.

Used to find partners whose documentation or notes match search terms. Enables complex ad-hoc queries in admin reporting UIs.

page.description:
Results page (for pagination).
Must be >= 1. Defaults to 1 if unspecified.

limit.description: Maximum results per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 if unspecified.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort by – e.g., partner_name, partner_code, created_at.

Determines primary ordering of paginated result set.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

Works in conjunction with sort_by field to control result ordering.

IShoppingMallShippingPartner.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination fields for listing registered shipping partners.

Supports matching by business display name, integration code, status (active/inactive/deprecated), and keyword matches in business/operational description. Includes platform-standard pagination/sorting fields for use in admin/grids and automation.

partner_name.description: Display name (UI/reference) of the shipping or logistics partner. Must be unique within the platform. Used in the admin interface, order flows, and as a selection in shipment-related APIs.

partner_code.description: Internal integration code for backend and system use. Must be unique across the platform. Used for system references and to index partners in integrations.

status.description: Operational status indicator for this shipping partner. Supported values are: active, inactive, or deprecated. Admin-only controlled, and determines whether users can select this partner for order fulfillment.

description.description: Business and operational description of the shipping partner. Provides information about their services, regions covered, or special requirements.

IShoppingMallShippingPartner.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new shipping/logistics partner entity in the shopping mall platform.

Each partner must be uniquely identified by both name and code. Registration is restricted to admin actors, with all fields validated for uniqueness and business requirements. Status is controlled by the platform admin, and proper validation is enforced to prevent duplicate partners. Creation and audit fields are managed automatically by the system.

partner_name.description: Display name (UI/reference) for the shipping or logistics partner. Must remain unique within the platform. Used in admin interfaces, order and shipment management; can be updated by admin operations.

partner_code.description: Integration code used by system backend and for partner identification. Uniqueness is enforced globally. Used to select or update a partner in integrations and audit logs.

status.description: Operational/logistics status for the shipping partner. Acceptable values: active, inactive, or deprecated (admin controlled). Used in workflows to filter available partners for order and fulfillment assignments.

description.description: Detailed business and operational information about the shipping partner. Can be updated to reflect changes in services, coverage, or structure.

IShoppingMallShippingPartner.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating a registered shipping/logistics partner in the shopping mall platform by admin staff.

Allows modification of display name, integration code, status, and descriptive information. All updates are strictly performed by authorized admin actors with system-enforced uniqueness checks for codes and names. Changes are audit-logged and trigger an update to the last modified timestamp.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest.description:
Advanced search and pagination/filter criteria for querying shopping mall customers in the administrative interface.

This DTO is used as the request body for admin-facing search endpoints that provide filtered, paginated, and sorted customer lists. Supports complex multi-criteria searching on customer attributes (email, name, phone, registration date, and email verification status) and pagination controls for result navigation.

The structure enables flexible admin dashboard customer management workflows, efficient fraud review, and regulatory compliance. It provides optimized querying while hiding sensitive or internal system fields.

email.description: Filter by customer email address (partial or exact match). Useful for locating customer records by business or personal email. Ignores case sensitivity.

name.description: Filter by customer legal full name (partial or exact match). Supports case-insensitive matching as per the system's indexed configuration.

phone.description: Filter by customer primary phone number (partial or exact match). Phone format is country code + number, but can be partial for general search.

is_email_verified.description: Filter for email verification status (true for only verified, false for only unverified). Enables searching by regulatory compliance status.

registered_start_at.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for creation date/time in ISO 8601 format. If specified, restricts results to customers registered after this timestamp.

registered_end_at.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for creation date/time in ISO 8601 format. If specified, restricts results to customers registered before this timestamp.

oneOf.description: Determines which customer field to sort results by. Supported values: email, name, phone, created_at, updated_at.
Determines which customer field to sort results by. Supported values: email, name, phone, created_at, updated_at.

sort_by.description: Determines which customer field to sort results by. Supported values: email, name, phone, created_at, updated_at.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction for listed customers. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort order direction for listed customers. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be >= 1. Controls the starting page for result navigation.

limit.description: Maximum number of customer results to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100.

IShoppingMallCustomer.description:
Full detail representation of a registered customer account (buyer) on the shopping mall platform.

This response DTO is used in profile retrieval and account management APIs, supporting user dashboard, order flows, and administrative review features. It exposes all business-visible customer attributes—name, email, phone, verification status, registration and last update timestamps—directly from the database, while omitting all authentication secrets and sensitive internal fields.

Strictly compliant with platform privacy and security policy: password hashes and authentication secrets (e.g., password_hash) are never present in this structure. Ownership is uniquely identified by a UUID. The model enforces a unique email address and immutable account creation time. Changes to business profile fields are permitted only via secure, audited mechanisms. Related session and audit records are accessible via subordinate APIs, not directly embedded here. Deletion is handled via admin action only (hard delete).

Relationship: This type may be linked via customer_id references in session, address, cart, wish, and order-related entities. No reverse relation arrays or sensitive subfields present in this DTO.

id.description: Unique identifier for the customer account (UUID). Primary key as set in the database.

email.description: Customer's email address for authentication and notifications. Must be unique across all platform customers.

name.description: Legal full name of the customer.

phone.description: Primary phone number for this customer, used for contact and order communications.

is_email_verified.description: Whether the customer's email address has been verified. Used for regulatory compliance and communication reliability.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp for when the customer account was created.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp for the last time the customer account was updated.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating an existing customer profile. This type enables modification of editable fields in the shopping_mall_customers table (such as name, phone, and email), enforcing business rules for unique email validation and field constraints. Password hash is strictly excluded and must be changed only via dedicated authentication flows.

All changes using this type are logged for audit trail compliance. Only the customer themselves or a platform admin may use this schema, aligning with strict business and security requirements identified in requirements analysis documents. Timestamps and system-managed identifiers are excluded as they are not modifiable by the client.

Immutable fields and sensitive authentication/actor fields are always excluded from this update DTO. Care is taken not to introduce any properties not present in the actual Prisma schema.

email.description: New email address for the customer account. Must be unique across all customers. Changing this email requires email verification as per business policy.

name.description: Updated legal full name for the customer. Must meet validation rules from the shopping_mall_customers schema and be geared for proper identification/order fulfilment.

phone.description: Updated primary phone number for the customer. Required for order and support contacts. Must meet format/validation rules enforced at the database level.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for advanced lookup of customer session records (shopping_mall_customer_sessions table).

Enables admin users to specify session search criteria and pagination options when querying customer session history. This schema supports fields such as search terms, filter constraints (such as created_at, expired_at, ip), sort order, and pagination configuration. Restrictions and options are aligned with the business requirement that only authorized admin actors may use this search/filter interface to audit user authentication activity. No system-managed or sensitive fields are included here.

page.description: Page number for paginated session retrieval. Default is 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to return per page.

search.description: Free text search string to match against connection context, such as IP or href/referrer.

order_by.description: Field name to order results by. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'expired_at', 'ip'.

order.description: Sort direction, either 'asc' or 'desc'.

filter_from.description: Filter for sessions created after this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

filter_to.description: Filter for sessions created before/on this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

filter_ip.description: Filter sessions by exact IP address.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.description:
Session token record for an authenticated customer login, as tracked in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.

Represents a unique login or persistent authentication event for a specific customer. Each session maintains metadata such as creation time, expiration (if applicable), IP address, and referring URLs for compliance, auditing, and fraud tracking. Sessions are always linked to an owning customer and do not expose authentication tokens over the API. This schema matches the exact structure and constraint definitions from the shopping_mall_customer_sessions Prisma model.

Session data is only accessible to the customer themselves or platform admin actors with appropriate privileges. Used in account management and regulatory audit endpoints.

The `customer` property references the owning customer and is always included as an actor summary object for atomic completeness and actor context. The raw foreign key field is not returned in this read DTO; frontend clients should use the provided reference summary for business and display needs.

id.description:
Primary key for the customer session record.

Unique identifier for each session, used to distinguish individual sessions for a customer.
This value is referenced in API paths and used for direct record lookups and audit trails.

customer.description:
Owning customer account for this session (actor summary).

Summary object representing the customer who owns this session. Transformed from the shopping_mall_customer_id raw FK to a context-rich summary object for UI display and business reasoning.

ip.description:
IP address for the client initiating the session.

Records the client's source IP at login, providing essential context for audits, fraud detection, and regulatory compliance. Typically an IPv4 or IPv6 address string.

href.description:
Original connection URL (referring page) at the start of session creation.

Captures the entry point for session authentication, used for compliance and to reproduce client context during investigations.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL for the session's origin context.

Indicates which page or service forwarded the user to the login or registration endpoint. Useful for attribution and advanced security review.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of session record creation in UTC.

Time when the session was first established. Used for lifecycle tracking, expiry calculations, and session listing sort order.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp in UTC, or null if currently active.

When present, indicates the explicit expiration or invalidation time for this session. Null means the session is still active. Used for status filtering and auditing.

search.description:
Full-text search string for filtering addresses by recipient name, street, city, province, or phone.

Used to enable user-driven filtering within their address book UI. Supports partial and multi-field matching for usability.

city.description:
Filter to restrict address results to a specific city.

When supplied, only addresses where the city field matches this value will be included.

province.description:
Filters addresses by province, state, or administrative region.

Useful for narrowing results based on user preference or business logic (e.g., sender/receiver must be in the same province).

country.description:
Restricts result set to addresses within the specified country (ISO/local format).

Allows international address book segmentation and targeted address selection.

is_default.description:
If true, restricts the search to only default address entries per actor.

Enables clients to quickly select a primary/default address for shipping, billing, or contact.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based).

Starts at 1, increments per page of results. Used alongside 'limit' for navigation.

limit.description:
Maximum number of results per page of address search.

Bounded to avoid excessive server/memory usage. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100.

oneOf.description:
Field used to sort address result sets.

Permitted values match indexed/address book relevance fields. Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.
